Results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6).

The paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three studies, total n=59 controls) performing social-related tasks (person knowledge, famous names, socially relevant concept words) contrasted against non-social semantic conditions and active baselines. Group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses (one-way ANOVAs and contrasts such as social > non-social) are reported, with peak coordinates and whole-brain results described and shown. Results for the healthy/control group are presented separately and clearly. Reporting of voxelwise task-evoked maps and coordinate tables/figures satisfies whole-brain evidence requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria for empirical task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain group results are met.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social-related approach-avoidance (AA) task comparing social versus nonsocial stimuli (meets social-processing requirement). Participants were healthy adults (male, mean age 21.35) with results reported separately for treatment groups of healthy subjects. The manuscript reports group-level task analyses and explicitly states exploratory whole-brain results were performed and reported (in main text/supplement), and contrasts are clearly identified at the group level. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8), using an impression-formation task involving social perception of faces varying in race and socioeconomic status — a social-related construct (perception and understanding of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task analyses (GLM contrast images used for PLS; voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster reporting and coordinates identified via xjview) and presents whole-brain PLS results and clusters. Results for the healthy adult sample are reported directly and are not restricted to a narrow subgroup. Thus the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for task fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain task-evoked maps. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6.

The study reports task-based fMRI of joint dyadic interaction (leading/following), which probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, social coordination). The sample is healthy adults (n=18, ages ~40) meeting the age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts, conjunctions) with Talairach coordinates and cluster thresholds described, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Results are presented for the healthy participant group (whole-group and subgroup analyses). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is an empirical fMRI study).

The study uses fMRI during a social perception task (trustworthiness/fear appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group (ages 18–45). However, the paper does not clearly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map that is explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain results appear to be across all participants or between-group contrasts, and control-group results are reported mainly via ROI analyses and statistics rather than an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (real-time mutual eye contact) in healthy adults (mean age ~21.8). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with corrected inference and provides tables/figures of activated clusters and interbrain synchronization. Results for the healthy participant group are reported separately and satisfy whole-brain reporting requirements.

This study reports task-based fMRI using a social-emotional Face Processing Task (fearful vs neutral faces), recruiting healthy adult participants (N=49, ages 18–33). The paper presents group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and whole-brain analyses (TFCE, FWE-corrected, 5,000 permutations) for contrasts (Fearful > Neutral and Neutral > Fearful) and reports coordinates and figures for these results. Questionnaire-regressed and seed-based FC results are supplemented by whole-brain exploratory analyses and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it meets inclusion requirements for an fMRI social task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group-level activation maps (also described in text and figures).

This is an fMRI study using a social task (modified cyberball) probing social exclusion — a social-related process. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (female, mean age ~21.7, final N=71 across groups) within the 18–65 range. The authors report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (initial whole-brain threshold p<0.001 uncorrected with clusters surviving FWE small-volume correction), provide peak MNI coordinates and statistical maps/figures, and describe contrasts and within-group effects. Results are clearly from healthy participants and reported as whole-brain task-evoked activations (coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply.

This study used task-based fMRI to measure neural responses to dynamic social interactions (dyads) in healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–35). Group-level whole-brain analyses are described: whole-brain beta maps were generated, whole-brain contrasts were used for localizer ROI definition (interaction > scrambled interaction, bodies > objects, faces > objects, mentalizing > pain), and a whole-brain searchlight analysis was performed and reported. Results include group-level statistical outcomes and descriptions of whole-brain searchlight peaks. Thus the paper meets the requirements for task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (reported in main text and supplementary materials).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=31 analyzed) investigating social perception of others (neural and behavioural responses to facial disfigurement; relevant to perception/understanding of others and stigma). The fMRI analysis includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SnPM nonparametric group analysis with familywise error correction and cluster-level reporting) comparing pre- vs post-surgery faces, with results presented as whole-brain activation/deactivation clusters. Participant ages (18–35) fall within the 18–65 range. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults are met.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social-economic paradigm (prisoners' dilemma) addressing social behaviour (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (15 controls, ages 18–50) with results reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses and explicitly describes significant activations for the control group (one-sample t-tests per group and visualizations/tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group maps (I5). Whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, reports within-group healthy results (not only between-group contrasts), includes adults within 18–65, and is empirical fMRI data. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this fMRI study involves a social task (dynamic facial expression processing) and includes a healthy adult control group, the full text does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly attributable to the healthy/TD group alone. The paper reports ROI-based results and whole-brain analyses focused on group differences, and emphasizes between-group contrasts and DCM (effective connectivity) findings. There is no clear presentation of a whole-brain within-healthy-group task effect (e.g., TD: expressions > mosaics) in the reported results or figures/tables described in the text. Therefore the study effectively reports only between-group contrasts and connectivity/ROI analyses without the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map, meeting exclusion criterion E4.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of action observation and weight-discrimination (perception of others’ hand actions), which falls squarely under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Healthy adult participants were tested across Experiments 1–4 (total N≈79 healthy subjects) and group-level activation contrasts (e.g., ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve contrasts) are presented. Analyses include voxelwise, group-level statistical maps (reported and visualized across the whole brain and specifically the cerebellum; some contrasts are presented at whole-brain level, e.g., NoSleeve–Sleeve FG4 result). Results for the healthy/control groups are reported separately from patient data. Therefore the study meets the fMRI social-task requirement, includes healthy adults, and provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (reported in figures/text/tables), satisfying I3, I4, I5 and I6.

The paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (listening to movie excerpts and inferring characters' mental states), satisfying the social-related task requirement. A healthy adult group (HC, n=28; age range 18–65 eligibility stated) is reported separately alongside a patient group. The manuscript provides group-level whole-brain within-group contrast maps for the healthy controls (INT>HIN), thresholded at p<0.05 FWE and presented in figures/tables, meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy group are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy map, ages within range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

I3 (fMRI during social tasks) and I4 (healthy adult control group, ages 50–60) are met: the study used fMRI with social tasks (SID, EFP) and includes a demographically matched healthy control group. However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain maps are reported for the combined sample and ROI and between-group contrasts are emphasized, but an unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect is not presented. Therefore I5 is not met and exclusion criterion E4 applies (no accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map). Consequently the study is excluded.

This article is a non-empirical review article in Japanese and does not report original fMRI data from healthy adult participants. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not report an fMRI study during a social-related task), I4 (no reported healthy adult sample with separate results), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I6 (no whole-brain results in text/tables). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=51, mean age 22.5) that used an explicit social-related task (passive observation of dynamic facial expressions — social communication/perception of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (dynamic expressions vs. dynamic mosaics) with family-wise error correction and presents statistical maps and activation coordinates/results in the text/tables/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper is a narrative/review article synthesizing multiple prior fMRI studies rather than reporting original empirical fMRI data from a healthy adult sample. It does not present new, original group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from healthy adults as primary empirical results (figures and maps are adapted from prior published studies). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical review without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria I3–I5 are not met for this paper itself: it does not itself report an original fMRI social-task study (I3), does not report an original healthy adult sample analysis (I4), nor does it report original group-level whole-brain activation maps from healthy/control participants as new results (I5). Full text appears complete. Exclusion: E6. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=37, ages 18–25) that used a task involving observation and imitation of others’ actions and examined neural correlates of the urge to imitate. The task involves social-related processing (perception/understanding of others’ actions and the drive to imitate). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation, one-sample t-tests, cluster-corrected thresholds) with coordinates and tables/figures of activations, and also reports PPI results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (eye-gaze, self-propelling motion, mental inference) in healthy adult participants (N=45, analyzed samples aged 19–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, contrasts such as E–O and S–X, voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction) with results presented in figures and tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy/intimacy/attachment) in healthy adult participants (N=36, mean age 23). The study uses whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (Pain vs. Neutral across Self/Loved-one/Stranger) with group-level random-effects analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates and thresholding (FDR-corrected maps, tables of peaks). Methods, results, and discussion are present, so the full text is complete. Reporting of whole-brain maps and coordinates satisfies whole-brain evidence requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates attractiveness comparisons (a social-perception task) in a sample of healthy adult participants (25 women, mean age 23.46). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects ANOVA), conjunctions, tables of coordinates, and statistical parametric maps, and describes results in the text and figures. Thus it satisfies social-task relevance (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and provides whole-brain task-evoked group results presented as maps and coordinate tables (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Although this fMRI study uses social-related tasks (ToM, face/voice perception, biological motion) in healthy adults (ages 19–31) and reports group-level analyses and coordinates, the group-level statistical maps were restricted to a bilateral STS mask rather than reported as whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task-evoked maps. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain task map (I5). This meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-restricted analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain group-level map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The provided "full text" is not the article content but a website privacy/cookie notice; core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are missing. I cannot verify that the study: used a social-related fMRI task (I3), included a healthy adult sample reported separately (I4), or reported whole-brain group-level task activation maps (I5). Therefore the study is excluded due to incomplete/full-text unavailability preventing assessment. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/uncertain: I3, I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a validated social cognition task (Animated Triangles Task) satisfying the social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (N=17, ages 18–30) with results for controls reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activations for the control group (text describes control-group activations; individual group activations are referenced in the supplementary material) and presents whole-brain statistical mapping procedures (FLAME, cluster correction) and figures. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy group map, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social influence/decision-making in healthy adults. Neuroimaging cohort comprises healthy adults aged 18–53 (within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level GLM analyses (random-effects), voxelwise statistical maps with multiple-comparison correction (SnPM), and makes maps available on NeuroVault. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants viewed person dyads (congruent, incongruent, non-interaction) while performing a sex-categorization task and BOLD responses were measured. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=12, ages 21–31). The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM analyses with voxelwise and cluster thresholds and provides peak coordinates and tables/figures (e.g., Table 3, Figs. 6–8). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study employed task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (evaluating fremdscham and schadenfreude), enrolled healthy adult participants within the target age range (N=34, ages 19–31), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SIT>NEUT) with FWE-corrected results and accompanying tables/figures. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognitive task (face processing, emotion recognition, affective ToM) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=18) with results reported separately. The paper reports second-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with a whole-brain significance threshold (P<0.001 uncorrected) and describes task-associated activation in the healthy controls (e.g., bilateral STS, inferior prefrontal gyrus), with supplementary tables referenced—satisfying the requirement that whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps for the healthy group are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group map, age outside range, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=35, ages 21–55) that used a social-related task: participant-generated autobiographical social situations and negative self-beliefs (social embarrassment/shame/humiliation), which clearly targets social processing and self-perception. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and tables/figures (cluster-corrected results, TFCE confirmation) from the healthy sample, and also provides amygdala ROI analyses in addition to whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This empirical study reports task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (undergraduates mean age ~18.9). The fMRI task contrasts faces versus houses (a social perception/face-processing paradigm relevant to ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’). Group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses were conducted in SPM8 and significant clusters (including bilateral fusiform gyrus) are reported and visualized (tables and figures); suprathreshold voxel counts in bilateral FG are explicitly reported. The sample consists of healthy adults and the whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social communication (speech-act comprehension: Naming vs Requesting) in healthy adults. The methods report fMRI acquisition and whole-brain random-effects analyses (FDR-corrected) with results presented in tables/figures and text. Participant sample consists of healthy native English adults (n=18 after exclusions), ages 18–41, satisfying the age/sample criterion. The study reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts (e.g., Request > Naming; Words > Faces) clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group only, not outside age range, and it is empirical primary data). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article reports an fMRI study using a social-cognition task (valence classification of agentic vs. communal trait words), with healthy adult participants (N=42, ages 18–25). The paper presents group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (agentic vs. fixation, communal vs. fixation, conjunctions, and direct contrasts) analyzed with SPM8 and AlphaSim cluster correction and reports peak coordinates and statistical maps in text/tables/figures. Thus it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of communicative/social speech production (communication vs description tasks), involving social processing (understanding context of interaction, biographical familiarity). Sample: 29 healthy adult participants (ages 18–24) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts (SPM random-effects second-level analyses, contrasts and cluster-corrected thresholds), with figures and tables of activated regions/coordinates. Thus it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI of social processing in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Socio-emotional Preferential Task assessing social appraisal of emotional faces), satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) with results reported alongside patients, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with FWE-corrected peaks and cluster statistics and describes within-group task activation (e.g., “Both SZ and HC recruited medial prefrontal cortex/ACC during the SePT”), indicating a healthy-group task-evoked whole-brain map is available, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of online social interaction (free imitation) in healthy adults (N=23, analyzed N=21; ages 18–30). The task is clearly social (imitation/being imitated/synchronous interaction) satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (GLM contrasts: imitating, being imitated, observation vs rest) with familywise error correction and provides coordinates/tables and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (GLM and PPI), discussion, and references, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of a social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adults (ages 18–22), so it meets I3 and I4. However, the paper’s analyses are ROI-based (MANOVA on averaged ROI beta values) and task-based PPI connectivity within a predefined network; it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E3 (reports PPI/seed-based connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete. Consequently, exclude.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI target-detection task using face (social) and shape (non-social) stimuli, with healthy adult participants (N=19; ages 19.3–47.5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FSL mixed-effects, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, P<0.05) and results are reported in figures and a table of MNI coordinates. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) involving healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 22.3). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results (statistical maps, Talairach coordinates, cluster-corrected thresholds, and figures/tables) clearly derived from the healthy/control group. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps, participants are within 18–65).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Cyberball ball-toss task (a social interaction paradigm) with healthy adult participants (final N=31, ages ~21). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ball-toss [high-frequency – normal-frequency] > button-press [high-frequency – normal-frequency]) with statistical thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction; coordinates and figures are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age outside range, or non-empirical issues).

This is an original, empirical fMRI study that investigates social hierarchy processing (a social cognition/social status task) in healthy adult participants. The sample comprises healthy adults within the 18–65 age range (N=72, 24 per experiment; reported ages within range). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (thresholded and FDR-corrected) with tables of coordinates and figures for healthy participants, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core article content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample, or only between-group contrasts) are met.

This fMRI study directly probes social-related processing (gaze, social vs. arbitrary facial expressions) using virtual characters and an event-related task, satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 25.9) satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2), contrasts, stereotactic coordinates, tables and figures of activations (e.g., main effects and interactions), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and tables/figures; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social stimuli (traffic campaign videos) to probe socio-cognitive processing — satisfies I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (male drivers aged 19–30) with group-level results reported separately — satisfies I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (CV vs NV) for the control/safe driver group (see Fig.1, Table 2 and text describing whole-brain analyses), meeting I5. Whole-brain results are clearly described in figures/tables and text, acceptable under I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

The study used task fMRI for self/other social processing (meets I3) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the typically developing (healthy) control group (meets I5 and I6). However, the reported sample includes minors (original age ranges include 15 and 16) and the paper does not provide results for a healthy adult (age 18–65) subgroup analyzed separately. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are strictly met. Full text appears complete.

This study used resting-state fMRI and graph-theory connectivity (Network Centrality) analyses rather than an fMRI social task. It includes a healthy control group but does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from a social task for the healthy participants. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (resting-state analyses only, no healthy-group whole-brain task activation map); E4 also applies because the paper reports between-group connectivity contrasts (patients vs controls) without providing an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (there is a healthy adult control group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task) and I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s requirement for task-based whole-brain fMRI activations in healthy adults and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social working memory (SWM) task (trait ranking of friends) during fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 21.56). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunction and contrasts of parametric modulation by load), with cluster thresholds and tables/figures of results and coordinate tables. These satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI during social-related tasks, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked maps; reporting includes tables/figures of coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/metadata/abstract-level content). Cannot verify key elements required for inclusion: whether the study used a task-based social fMRI paradigm with a healthy adult group (age 18-65), and whether it reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore I cannot confirm inclusion criteria. Exclusion is based on incomplete full text preventing assessment; no exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the provided content.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI during a social decision-making (iterated prisoner's dilemma) paradigm; (I4) sample consists of healthy adults (N=20, ages 23–38); (I5) reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrasts (e.g., conjunction analyses, COMP>COOP) with multiple-comparison correction; (I6) whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and tables. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not between-group-only, age within range, and empirical fMRI data present).

Exclusion criterion E4 met: the paper reports whole-brain group-level interaction (Group×Stimulus) and post hoc between-group simple effects, but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or main-effect task map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task—the Why/How social inference task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, results for groups are reported separately in ROIs and post hoc tests). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 (no clear whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group is reported; whole-brain results focus on between-group interactions rather than an unmasked within-control group activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded per E4.

This full-text fMRI study examines social-related processing (explicit mental simulation of another person’s actions and feelings) in healthy adults (n=20, ages 21–47). It uses task-based fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain results: ISPS maps, SBPS connectivity, and conventional GLM SPM-t maps with cluster-level FDR correction; ROIs and whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study on healthy adults (N=78, age 18–40) that includes multiple social-cognition tasks (false belief/ToM, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes intention, trustworthiness, vocalizations) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects (voxelwise) analyses (p<0.05 FWE-corrected) and supplementary peak listings and maps. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy cohort are reported separately. Whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are clearly reported and compared to meta-analyses; the full article includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text is complete.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of social perception (affiliation vs. isolation), fulfilling the review objective. The sample includes a healthy younger adult group (n=16, M age = 20.75), which falls within the 18–65 range and is reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses, contrasts (e.g., Affiliation vs Isolation, Social vs Nonsocial), conjunctions, and tables/figures of activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range without eligible subgroup, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is an empirical fMRI study but does not investigate social-related processing: the fMRI task used low-contrast concentric rings (motion vs. static)—a low-level visual motion paradigm (non-social). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (a healthy adult control group is included and reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (task is not social-related), I5 (no clear report of a whole-brain, within-group healthy/control task activation map identified as coming from the healthy group). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the paper focuses on between-group contrasts and group differences/correlations without providing an unambiguous whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-rejection (Cyberball) task that probes social-related processing (affiliation/attachment, social exclusion). The sample comprises healthy adult university students (unmarried, right-handed, screened for neurological history) within the adult age range. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects task contrasts (exclusion vs inclusion) with FWE-corrected thresholds and presents whole-brain results in figures and tables, plus two-sample whole-brain comparisons; ROI analyses are supplemental but whole-brain healthy-group activation maps are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 reported separately). While the paper uses fMRI during a social-related face encoding task (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the control (healthy) group with coordinates/tables (I5 and I6 satisfied), the control group includes adolescents/minors (mean age 18.7 with participants under 18 mentioned) and the authors do not report a healthy-adult-only subgroup analysis. Thus I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This dual-fMRI hyperscanning study reports an fMRI task of social interaction (cooperation/competition; meets I3). The sample comprises 44 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.4), reported and analyzed as a healthy group (meets I4). The paper presents group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (FLAME) with nonparametric permutation correction and reports whole-brain results in tables and figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false. Inclusion criteria applied: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria applied: none.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social judgment task (trustworthiness of faces) — satisfying I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (mean age 32.2) with results reported separately — satisfying I4. The manuscript presents group-level whole-brain within-group analyses for the control group (whole-brain thresholds and Tables/Figures are described), meeting I5 and I6. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study investigates voice-identity recognition, a social-related process (perception/understanding of others). It includes healthy adult control groups (n=16 each, ages ~31) reported separately, and presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and coordinate tables for control participants (vocal>non-vocal; speaker>speech). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that manipulated social vs. non-social contexts during encoding and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses of healthy adult participants (n=24, ages 18–28). The paper provides full methods, contrasts, SPM-based random-effects analyses, tables/figures of activation (e.g., right and left mPFC), and discusses social-context and self-generation effects. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a deception task (a social-cognitive paradigm related to perception/understanding of others and theory-of-mind processes). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=24 males, ages 19–60). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise contrasts (lie > truth and truth > lie) with thresholds and clusters reported in tables/figures and describes whole-brain preprocessing and analysis; ROI small-volume correction was used for some regions but whole-brain group effects are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of Theory of Mind (social cognition) using an established moving-triangles task (meets I3). The sample includes 20 healthy adults age 24–64 with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (ToM > R, ToM > Baseline) with statistical thresholds and coordinate tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the review.

This is an fMRI study of vocal emotional processing in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper reports ROI-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical analyses (Power-264 parcellation) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate-based whole-brain activation results for the healthy group. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5/I6). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (only ROI/connectivity analyses with no whole-brain results) and E3 (connectivity-based analyses without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no voxelwise whole-brain task map reported) and I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/coords). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets several inclusion criteria for the review (it uses task-based fMRI with social stimuli (emotional faces), and it reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the control (neurotypical) group, with results presented in tables/figures). However, it does not satisfy the sample-age inclusion criterion (I4): the healthy/control group is a mixed adolescent-adult sample (age range 12–23) and the paper does not report results for a healthy adult (age 18–65) subgroup separately. Therefore I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines social-related processing (CT-targeted affective touch), using a task probing affiliation/affective touch perception. Sample: 22 healthy adults aged 19–35 (meets adult healthy group criterion). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results for arm > baseline, palm > baseline, and direct arm > palm contrasts (voxelwise maps, thresholds and cluster corrections described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Whole text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages, or only between-group contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-role judgment task (self, friend, celebrity) directly probing perception/understanding of self and others (social-related processing). The sample is healthy adults (n=37, mean age 22.9), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and thresholding (p<.05 FDR with voxelwise p<.001), with peak coordinates and tables/figures (whole-brain task-evoked maps/contrasts: self vs. celebrity, friend vs. celebrity). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (approachability judgments from faces) that includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps/contrasts for the healthy/control group (detailed cluster coordinates and corrected p-values are provided and figures described), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports healthy-group task effects). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

Exclusion criteria met: E2 and E4. The full text reports fMRI task contrasts and gPPI connectivity but results are reported using a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and primarily as between-group (Depressed vs Healthy) differences. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related/attachment task - baby-cry with self/other conditions) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group is provided; reported effects are ROI-restricted and mainly group-difference contrasts). Therefore the study must be excluded because it relies on ROI analyses and between-group contrasts without providing the required whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps.

This is an fMRI study using a dynamic social gestures (DSG) task that directly probes social versus nonsocial processing (I3). The sample comprises healthy young adults (N=20; mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7), reporting results for the healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (cluster-corrected Z-stat maps and local maxima coordinates in Table 1) clearly from the healthy/control group (I5), and whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and tables (I6). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range sample-only, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective and is included.

This paper reports an fMRI task that manipulates perceived live versus recorded social speech (a social-communication paradigm) in healthy adults (final N=29, ages 18–27). It includes group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (Live > Social; Social > Standard) thresholded and cluster-corrected and described in the text/figures/tables. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study reports an fMRI experiment investigating prosocial learning (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants (n=31, ages 19–32). It uses whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (flexible-factorial GLM) and reports group-level task-evoked effects and contrasts with coordinates/tables and figures (main effects and contrasts are described; Tables S1–S4 and whole-brain reporting procedures are provided). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and supplementary procedures, so the full text appears complete. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain results (coordinates/tables), satisfying I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (observation of social vs. individual actions; modulation by gaze), meeting I3. The sample comprises 17 healthy adult participants (mean age 26), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and tables of coordinates (SPM{t} maps, Table 1, figures) from a random-effects analysis, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and there is no indication of ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-eligible ages, or non-empirical status. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) satisfying I3. The sample includes a clearly described healthy adult control group (n=22) with matched demographics and separate behavioral and imaging results, satisfying I4. The manuscript reports whole-brain, group-level task analyses (e.g., ToM>Emo>neutral; Table 3) and a group × condition interaction and refers to within-group/ group-specific contrasts in the supplementary materials, satisfying I5 and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and supplementary analyses). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group maps, age outside 18–65, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and supplementary materials are noted but not required for inclusion. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults. It used task-based fMRI combining self-referential and implicit social stimulus processing (social stimuli defined as pictures containing humans), meeting the review’s domain. Sample: 28 healthy right-handed adults aged 30–50 (within 18–65). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were reported (ANOVA across subjects, SPM8; results reported FDR-corrected, p<0.05, cluster k≥20; coordinates/tables/figures provided). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing: recall of self- and other-related relationship episodes, fitting constructs of self/other perception and attachment. The sample comprises 35 healthy adult participants screened for mental disorders. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self-relevant > control, other > control, etc.) with cluster inference (FDR-corrected) and tables/figures of activation peaks. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The provided text is an abstract only (Background, Methods, Results, Conclusions) and lacks full methods and participant details. Inclusion criteria met: I3 — the study uses fMRI during social-related tasks (attentional and attributional judgements related to self). Inclusion criteria not verifiable: I4 — no explicit participant ages or full sample description to confirm healthy adults aged 18–65; I5 — although regional activations are reported, the abstract does not clearly state a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map (could be ROI-based or unreported whole-brain details); I6 — unclear whether whole-brain results are provided in tables/figures. Exclusion criteria: none explicitly met (E2–E6 not demonstrably applicable). Because core article content (detailed methods, demographics, and explicit whole-brain analysis reporting) is missing, I cannot confirm all inclusion criteria; thus exclude pending retrieval of full text. If full text is provided, re-screening may allow inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test) in healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 26.4). The paper reports group-level task-evoked activation contrasts within the healthy/placebo condition (ToM > gender) and also provides exploratory whole-brain analyses (reported at P<0.001 uncorrected) with coordinates/tables (Table 2/Table 3), thus satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy/social cognition in healthy adults (N=16 analyzed, mean age 27.8). The task involved viewing social scenes (emotional/neutral; one/two persons) during fMRI and reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (EMOT vs NEUT; TWO vs ONE) with statistical maps, cluster thresholds and tables of Talairach coordinates (FDR q<0.05). Methods, results, and group-level analyses for the healthy sample are fully reported. Thus it meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (attribution of emotions/theory-of-mind to humans and non-human animals) using task-based fMRI (Explicit and Implicit tasks), meeting the review’s social-processing scope. Sample consists of healthy adults within 18–65 (final n=16–17 after exclusions; mean age ~29), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (conjunctions, contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) and presents whole-brain results and tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study probing social cognition (Theory of Mind and empathy) using a comic-strip task. Participants are nonclinical college students (ages 17–21, mean 19.3) comprising healthy adults within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain SPM activation maps (random field theory corrected) and refers to cluster peak coordinates (Data S1–Table S3); these whole-brain task-evoked maps are clearly described and used in analyses. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (task-based social processing fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level maps). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an empathy task (social-related processing) and reports group-level whole-brain task activations for the healthy control group (one-sample t-test maps, tables and figures). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=14) matched to patients; ages fall within 18–65. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are clearly described for the control group (thresholding, cluster extent, Anatomy Toolbox labels). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. VBM results are additional but do not affect eligibility. Although sample size is small, no exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI study of self-, mother-, and social-attribution processing in healthy adults (n=17 analyzed; mean age 21.5), using task-based whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM contrasts, FDR-corrected maps and uncorrected group contrasts), and provides Talairach coordinates and group-level statistical maps/tables. The tasks are clearly social-related (self/other processing, theory-of-mind/social attribution). All required inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI of social constructs (I3); healthy adult sample 18–65 with results reported separately (I4); group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and coordinate tables (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, age appropriate). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses social-cognitive tasks (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) during task-based fMRI (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group reported separately and matched by age (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain within-group results for single groups (reported at P<0.001 uncorrected, Supplementary Tables S1–S4) and whole-brain group comparisons (meets I5). Whole-brain results are reported in the main text, tables, figures, and supplementary materials (meets I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This article reports an fMRI task study of social cognition (mentalising/theory of mind) in healthy adults and meets all inclusion criteria. It uses task-based functional MRI during social-related mentalising tasks (I3). Healthy adult participants are reported (Experiment 2: N=17, mean age 22; Experiment 1 behavioral N=39 adults) (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (mentalising > factual; parametric modulation contrasts), with SPM analyses, thresholding, tables of significant clusters and coordinates, and figures (I5,I6). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and provides access to neuroimaging data. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social stimuli (reappraisal of angry faces), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (n=60; age range 18–57), meeting the adult sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry; Increase vs Observe-angry) with tables/figures and cluster-level FWE correction, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables and figures (supplementary tables referenced), so acceptable per I6. Although resting-state and seed analyses are included, the study also provides unmasked whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates neural correlates of processing political beliefs—a social-cognitive task involving self/other processing and social decision-making. Sample: healthy adults (ages 22–45), reported separately and meeting inclusion age range. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (parametric effects, second-level maps, thresholding reported, figures/tables provided). Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines emotion evaluation from vocalizations and music, which maps onto social-related processing (perception and understanding of others). The participant sample comprises healthy adults aged 18–26 (N=16 analyzed), satisfying the age and healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain surface-based analyses (GLM, random-effects, conjunctions) with tables and figures describing activation maps and ROI analyses; thus whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group are available. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (hand-holding with friend, stranger, or alone during threat-of-shock) examining social regulation of threat responding, satisfying I3. Sample consists of healthy adults (mean age ~23.6, N=22), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses: multisubject ROIs were identified via cluster-wise whole-brain tests (FSL, Z>2.3, cluster p<.05) with reported ROIs, coordinates and cluster sizes (Table 1), meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is original fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

Exclusion (E4): The paper does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. It reports ROI-based within-group results for the healthy controls and reports exploratory whole-brain analyses only for between-group contrasts (healthy>manic, manic>healthy) in the supplement, but no whole-brain healthy-group ‘social>non-social’ map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI with social vs. non-social stimuli) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map provided), I6 (not applicable because qualifying whole-brain healthy results are absent). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (n=36, ages within 18–65) using a social-related task (observation of cooperative vs affective interactions). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (parametric and categorical contrasts) with corrected statistical maps and tables/figures, and clearly identifies results from the healthy sample. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that assesses self- and other-evaluation (social-related constructs: perception/understanding of self and others) using a task-based fMRI paradigm. The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) reported separately and matched to patients. Whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy/control group are reported (one-sample analyses for SELF vs baseline, OTHER vs baseline, conjunctions, and contrasts), with tables/figures and correction for multiple comparisons. Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables/figures/text). The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: It used task-based functional MRI during a social cognition task (Social Detection Task) assessing valence judgements of naturalistic social interactions (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (final N=38; age range 18–30) with results reported for this healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (full-factorial ANOVA, whole-brain FWE-corrected results; Table 1 and figures), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables and figures (I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are in age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be included.

Full text appears incomplete (only highlights/abstract/metadata provided). While the abstract indicates an fMRI social task (I3 met), the manuscript as provided does not include methods/results needed to confirm sample age/health (I4) or whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported (I5). Cannot verify inclusion criteria I4 and I5 from available content. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the truncated text. Therefore exclude due to incomplete full text preventing verification of required criteria.

The full text reports task-based fMRI during two social-cognitive tasks (emotional perspective-taking and emotion attribution) directly addressing social-related processing. The sample is healthy adults (n=120–129, ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected main effects and whole-brain regression analyses with cluster reports and MNI coordinates) for the healthy sample, with results described in text, figures, and tables. All core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only highlights, abstract, and references provided). From available content: I3 is satisfied (fMRI during an interactive mentalizing/prisoner’s dilemma social task) and I4 is satisfied (healthy adult sample, n=195). However I5 (reporting of at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group) cannot be verified from the truncated content: the abstract reports neural activations but the full methods/results (statistical maps, thresholding, and whether unmasked healthy-group whole-brain contrasts are presented) are not available. I6 (acceptable reporting format confirmation) likewise cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the provided text. Because the full article text (methods/results/discussion and figures/tables) is missing, critical items required to confirm inclusion—especially I5—cannot be verified, so the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

This full-text reports an fMRI study using a social/emotional face-processing task (dynamic fearful faces), includes a healthy adult control group (n=19, mean age 31.8 within 18–65), and presents group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and contrasts (face > place) clearly described and thresholded (one-sample t-test, p<0.05 FWE cluster-corrected) for the control/combined groups (figures and tables referenced). The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state-only, no healthy-group whole-brain map, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 28.7) that uses task-based fMRI during a social face-viewing paradigm addressing perception/understanding of others and affiliation-related constructs. The paper reports both ROI and random-effects, whole-brain, parametric group-level analyses (with tables/figures and supplementary tables; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and Table S4 are described), and results are clearly reported for the healthy/control sample. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, tasks, imaging acquisition and analysis), results, and discussion (with SI Text), so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition using a social-comparison task (close other vs roommate), satisfying the review topic. Participants were healthy adults (N=20, mean age 18.7), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (random-effects SPM{t} maps) with reported peak coordinates, cluster sizes, t-stats, and corrected P-values; results are presented as voxelwise contrasts (coordinates and figures/tables) for the healthy participant group. Although several tests used ROI-based correction, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and coordinate reports are provided. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of impression formation/updating (a social-cognition task: perception and understanding of others), meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults aged 18–45 (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (interaction and L2>F3 contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction, presented in figures/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social-cognition tasks (empathic and forgivability judgments) (I3). It includes a healthy adult comparison group (N=14, mean age 30.5) with results reported separately (I4). Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results for the healthy/control group are described (within-group activations and contrasts across scans are reported in the text and supplements), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used fMRI during a social-related task — empathic and forgivability judgments). Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed from provided content: I4 (sample age 18–65 not specified; only 'ten volunteers' mentioned, ages not reported), I5 (cannot confirm reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group). No exclusion criteria are explicitly met based on the provided content, but inability to verify I4 and I5 due to incomplete full text prevents inclusion.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (False-Belief Localizer) which probes theory-of-mind (I3). It includes healthy adult control groups reported separately: a Caltech group (n=18; ages 21–46) and a large MIT group (n=462; ages 18–69) — the Caltech group clearly falls within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps and whole-brain contrasts (Belief > Photo) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/reference groups, including unthresholded and thresholded maps and voxelwise analyses (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical, not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and provides healthy-group whole-brain activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and supplementary materials are referenced. Therefore, include this study in the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during social-related processing (self-construal/self-judgment; I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (N=24 university students; I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and presents whole-brain contrasts and coordinate tables (e.g., main effects and interactions, and regression analyses), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and reports healthy-group whole-brain task activations. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI probing social-related processing (meaning-related ratings engaging social cognition), (I4) sample comprises healthy adults (n=25, mean age 24, screened for neurological/mental problems), (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (meaning>physical and other contrasts) with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates, (I6) whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: a within-subject, randomized, double-blind fMRI investigation using the Cyberball social exclusion task. The sample comprises 21 healthy adults (age range 20–37), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., not receiving ESE > receiving INCL) and provides whole-brain results in Tables S3 and S4 (uncorrected P < 0.001) and SVC ROI analyses, clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps/contrasts), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates processing of vocal versus non-vocal sounds (socially relevant vocal signals) using task-based functional MRI. Participants were healthy adults (Experiment 1: n=13, ages 21–41; Experiment 2: n=18, ages 18–33), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and activation maps (vocal>non-vocal) with thresholding and cluster criteria; results are described in text and figures. The task (voice processing) fits social-communication / perception of others constructs. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and figures, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social-related tasks (affiliation and power movie clips) with healthy adult participants (n=17, mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (affiliation > control; power > control) with cluster results, MNI coordinates, figures, and corrected statistics, clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 19–36) that uses a task probing animacy perception—a social-related construct falling under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunction and contrasts with FWE correction) and provides coordinates and whole-brain results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; the healthy control group results are reported separately and are not limited to an ROI-only or connectivity-only analysis. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria listed (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of the effects of implied social presence on functional connectivity; it does not report any task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only resting-state/connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample: healthy adult participants aged 18–22). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task; the design is resting-state with instructional manipulation rather than a task), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on task-evoked whole-brain fMRI studies of social processing.

This is an fMRI study of social gaze processing (mutual vs. averted gaze) in a dynamic social context, involving healthy adult participants (right-handed young adults). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (t-statistic activation maps; Figure 4 and voxel-based analyses are described), in addition to ROI analyses. Full article contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction (joint action with haptic contact) in healthy adult dancers (mean age 40.4, range within 18–65). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts (random-effects), reports Talairach coordinates and FDR-corrected maps/tables for partnered vs. non-partnered and role contrasts, clearly arising from the healthy participant group. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI social-processing task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This empirical fMRI study reports task-evoked whole-brain activation maps from a healthy adult control group (n=28) performing a social-related moral reasoning task. The paper includes adults (18–55), reports one-sample (within-group) whole-brain analyses for the HC group (FWE-corrected and Monte-Carlo corrected results), and provides tables/figures of healthy-group activations. Although the study also includes an ASD clinical group, results for the healthy controls are reported separately.
