The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during live social interaction and joint attention paradigms (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (Experiment 1 final n=16, Exp 2 final n=13; ages 18–29) and reports their results separately (meets I4). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Live > Recorded, Joint Attention > Solo Attention) with correction for multiple comparisons and provides coordinate tables and figures (meets I5 and I6). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only group effects, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition (theory-of-mind) task (Frith–Happé animations), satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (NT; N=23, ages 19–56), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level one-sample t-tests and whole-brain analyses for each group, and explicitly notes whole-brain results for within-group contrasts (NT and ASD) with results presented (Supplementary Data 2) and activation maps in figures, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is not ROI-only (whole-brain maps reported), not resting-state/seed-only, reports unmasked healthy-group task effects, includes adults within 18–65, and is empirical. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study used a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) versus a non-social control (Gamble), in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=20, females, mean age 20.8; Experiment 2: n=30, mixed sex, mean age 21.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (PD–Gamble) with thresholded statistical maps, tables of activations, figures, and ROI/whole-brain exploratory analyses explicitly for the healthy subject groups. Whole-brain results are clearly described and presented (tables, figures, coordinate listings). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (only ROI-only, resting-state-only, patient-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related visual perspective-taking task and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the reported task activation analyses were restricted to predefined prefrontal ROIs (region-of-interest analyses) and the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Instead it reports ROI activation results and seed-based functional connectivity. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete. Consequently I exclude the study.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/highlights/metadata provided). Based on available content: Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related mentalizing task, Prisoner’s Dilemma) and I4 (sample of 164 healthy adult subjects). Inclusion criterion I5 (clear report of at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task activation map) cannot be verified from the truncated content—while the abstract lists activated regions, the full methods/results and explicit whole-brain group map reporting (tables/figures/coordinates) are not available. Therefore the study is excluded until full text can be confirmed. Exclusion criteria: none identified from the available excerpt. fulltext_incomplete=true.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the study reports only resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps) and E5 (participants are children/adolescents, age range 6.5–18.7 years, with no healthy adult subgroup in the 18–65 range). Inclusion criteria: none are satisfied. Specifically, inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI social-related task; study uses resting-state fMRI), I4 (no healthy adult sample 18–65; sample is male children/adolescents), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation map from a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion; exclusion is based on content, not incomplete reporting.

The study uses fMRI with a social threat task (viewing threatening faces) and reports a separate healthy control group, satisfying I3 and I4. However, all neuroimaging results reported are ROI-based (amygdala parameter estimates and correlations) and the paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, peak coordinate tables, or whole-brain figures for the healthy/control group. Thus it violates exclusion criterion E2 and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=63, ages ~20–36) using a social incentive delay task (social vs monetary rewards). The full text reports group-level task-evoked activation results, including whole-brain analyses (e.g., whole-brain FWE-corrected activations and tables of coordinates) for anticipation and outcome contrasts, clearly attributed to the healthy/control cohort. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=26, mean age 20.7) that used social tasks (Cyberball exclusion and a modified Dictator Game) addressing social processing (punishment/forgiveness of excluders). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., exclusion no-ball > inclusion-ball; excluders > includers; excluders equality > includers equality) with cluster results and tables and discusses voxelwise FDR correction. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets fMRI social-task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group results (I5), and acceptable reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social processing: participants played a repeated public good game probing social tie formation and prosocial decision-making, with model-based regressors (social tie, impulse) tied to neural activity. Sample: healthy adult participants (25 scanned; mean age ~22.6), reported separately. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (FSL FEAT GLM), with cluster-wise FWE correction and coordinates reported in text/tables/figures (MNI coordinates reported for pSTS, TPJ, mPFC, PCC, insula, etc.). Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and statistical thresholds; supplementary material referenced but core article content is present.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) using task-based contrasts with healthy adult participants (n=15, age 21–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM5; ANOVA contrasts, cluster-size and voxel-wise thresholds, conjunctions, and coordinates/tables/figures of activations) clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, task, acquisition, analysis), results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults age 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social attribute framing (self and reflected perspectives), recruiting healthy adult participants (ages 19–41). The methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative frames, frame-consistent vs inconsistent) with coordinate tables and thresholding, clearly identified for the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and no exclusion criteria apply.

The manuscript analyzes task fMRI from 493 HCP participants (healthy adults) and explicitly includes a social cognition task alongside working memory and motor tasks. The authors report group-level task-evoked activation patterns derived via GLM (e.g., mean WM evoked activation maps shown in figures) and perform sensitivity analyses identifying whole-brain regions implicated in the social cognition task (supplementary figures). The sample is the HCP healthy adult cohort (within 18–65). Whole-brain, group-level task activation maps are described and shown (main figures and supplementary material), satisfying acceptable reporting formats (figures/supplement). Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures, supplementary noted).

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adults (N=38, mean age 27.5) using an emotion-discrimination task with faces — a clear social-processing paradigm (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (one-sample SPM analysis FACES>OBJECTS) with statistical maps and thresholding (p<0.001 voxelwise, p<0.05 FWE cluster), and provides figures/tables of whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study used fMRI during incidental processing of fearful faces (social-related task) and included a healthy control group (so I3 and I4 are met). However, the paper, as described, emphasizes multivariate functional connectivity (three-way multidimensional scaling) and reports abnormal connectivity and between-group differences; there is no evidence in the abstract/metadata of any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map reported for the healthy/control group. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met based on available content. This matches exclusion criteria E3 (connectivity-focused analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reporting primarily between-group contrasts without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Because the full text is incomplete, certainty is limited.

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial emotion perception (social perception/understanding of others) using a passive viewing task, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (27 community controls) recruited with age restrictions 18–65, satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports within-group whole-brain task activation results for the control group (within-group analyses and whole-brain activation maps/coordinates are described and figures/tables present control group effects), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are presented in text, tables, and figures; acceptable reporting formats are used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, no healthy-group whole-brain map, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (affective and cognitive Theory of Mind) in a healthy adult sample (n=23). The task used comic-strip ToM paradigms during BOLD fMRI, and the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FDR correction and peak coordinates (Table 2, whole-brain results described in text). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants appear to be adults, and this is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; sufficient for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in a healthy adult sample (ages 18–22), satisfying the review focus on social-related processing. The sample comprises only healthy adults and results are reported for these groups separately (OT vs placebo), meeting the sample criterion. The manuscript includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (treatment-by-methylation interactions and whole-brain contrasts, thresholded and reported in tables/figures) derived from the healthy participants, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/tables (including subgroup analyses for rs53576 GG), which is acceptable per the guidelines. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study examines facial color processing (natural vs bluish faces vs scrambled), a form of social-related face perception and social communication relevant to perception of others. It reports data from healthy adults (N=25, mean age 25, within 18–65). The paper includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (natural-colored face vs natural-colored scrambled image) with peak coordinates, figures and tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (ROI analyses are present but are accompanied by whole-brain results). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and is INCLUDED.

Full text incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From available text, I3 is satisfied: the study used task-based fMRI of a social cognition construct (theory of mind). However I4 (participant age range 18–65 confirmation) cannot be verified from the abstract alone; the study reports younger and older adults but exact ages/healthy-group specification for 18–65 are not provided. I5 (reporting of at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map for the healthy/control group) is not verifiable in the abstract — the paper discusses intrinsic/resting-state connectivity within a task-defined network but does not clearly state an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. I6 (acceptable reporting formats) likewise cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied from the abstract. Because key inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an fMRI study of live verbal social interaction (social communication) in healthy adult participants (22 right-handed women, mean age ~27), meeting the sample age-range and healthy-group requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level voxel-wise t-tests, cluster thresholds, figures and tables of activations) for task conditions (talking, listening, imagining) and inter-individual coupling analyses; whole-brain results are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social/attachment-related processing: tasks explicitly probe implicit attitudes toward monogamy/adultery and regulation of interest in extra-pair relationships (social affiliation/attachment). Sample: 27 healthy adult males (ages 20–32) with no neurological/psychiatric history. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation is reported for the IAT contrast (incongruent vs. congruent) with clusters passing cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates presented in tables; thus a healthy-group whole-brain task effect is available. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text is complete and meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self and other reflection; SR > AL contrasts), (I4) includes a healthy adult sample (N=22, mean age 37.4, screened for DSM disorders), and (I5/I6) reports group-level whole-brain surface-based/task-evoked results (SR > AL) with cluster-wise corrected maps and tabled coordinates/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (task activation and resting connectivity), and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore it should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

Full text is inaccessible (page shows only a privacy/cookie preference prompt and no article content). Therefore I cannot verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (use of task-based fMRI for social processing) not confirmed, I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) not confirmed, I5 (whole-brain group-level healthy-control task map) not confirmed, I6 (results described in text/tables/figures) not confirmed. No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the available material. Because the full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is not available, the study cannot be included at this time.

This is an empirical fMRI study of affective theory-of-mind (a social cognition task) in healthy adults (N=21 analyzed; mean age 23.7). The paper reports group-level, within-healthy-group whole-brain activation contrasts (2nd-level one-sample t-tests) with tables and figures of peak coordinates and cluster results, and describes ROI and PPI analyses. Whole-brain task-evoked maps/results for the healthy group are clearly reported in text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an event-related fMRI study that explicitly probes social-related processing (positive social interaction, human faces, erotic scenes) during task-based picture viewing (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (N=14) with ages in the adult range alongside a clinical depressed group, and results for the healthy/control group are reported separately in the text and figures (meets I4). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise (voxel-by-voxel repeated-measures ANOVAs) with Monte Carlo correction, and clusters/coordinates are reported in tables and figures; control-group task responses (within-group contrasts/simple effects) are described and illustrated (meets I5 and I6). The full-text content provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI of participants viewing and anticipating another person’s actions (action observation/anticipation), which maps onto ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (I3). Participants are healthy adult badminton players (experiment 1 and 2) with analyses reported for these groups (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects task contrasts (shots–mctrl; thresholded at p<0.05 FWE) and provides peak coordinates and figures/tables of activations, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, healthy adult sample).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy, perspective-taking) in healthy adults. The study used task-based fMRI during an empathy/perspective-taking paradigm (needle vs. Q-tip stimuli) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Pain > No Pain, No Pain: Dissimilar > Similar) with stereotactic coordinates and statistical thresholds. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=23, ages 19–34). Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables/figures acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age in range, empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Study reports an empirical fMRI experiment using a social mentalizing task (thinking about friends vs kin) in healthy adult participants (n=25, mean age 23.2). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (friend>kin contrast and linear parametric analyses across network layers), with cluster correction (GRF, z>2.3, p<0.05) and activations presented in tables and figures. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of legal decision-making that directly involves social-cognitive processes (responsibility judgments, punishment decisions, trait/biological descriptions)—meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (final N=20; ages 18–45), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts and provides whole-brain coordinate tables and descriptions of results (multiple whole-brain contrasts and regressions), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirements (and acceptable reporting formats). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

The provided “full text” is incomplete (only title/metadata/navigation and no methods, participants, results, or discussion). Therefore I cannot verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 reported separately), I5 (report of at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), and I6 (whole-brain results available in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria from the review checklist are explicitly met based on available information. Because the core article content needed to assess eligibility is missing, the study must be excluded from the review pending a complete full text.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (imagining triadic interactions, self- and other-referential tasks) in healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (conjunctions and contrasts) with coordinates and whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds, and includes methodological details (methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses task-based fMRI examining observers of virtual social interactions (meets I3). It reports group-level, whole-brain activation maps (social interaction vs control) from N=15 participants with activations in STS, mPFC, and amygdala, satisfying I5 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) and I6 (results presented as activation maps/figures). Participants are described as recruited on basis of age/health with informed consent and ethics approval; although exact ages are not explicitly provided, the description and typical JoVE recruitment practices indicate healthy adult participants (I4). No evidence of ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study, so no exclusion criteria apply. Slight uncertainty about explicit age reporting lowers confidence slightly.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a modified Cyberball social exclusion/performance task (a social-evaluative paradigm) in healthy adult participants (20 men, 20 women; mean age 27.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (GLM, random effects), uses voxelwise FWE correction, and provides whole-brain results in tables of MNI coordinates and cluster sizes for multiple contrasts (e.g., EX > IN, PG EX > FG EX, conjunctions). Full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging), tables and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining political attitudes (social cognition) using an IAT with faces/names while participants underwent fMRI. Participants were healthy adults (ages 21–40; n=24 analyzed). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM2 preprocessing and random-effects one-sample t-tests; FDR correction for whole-brain results and tables/figures of activations), and presents coordinate tables and figures for contrasts (congruent vs incongruent, congruent vs control, etc.). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, age-appropriate, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study (EmpaToM) investigating empathy and Theory-of-Mind using task-based fMRI in a sample of healthy adults (N=178, mean age 40.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (emotional vs neutral videos; ToM vs non-ToM questions/videos) entered into one-sample t-tests and presents activation maps and peak coordinates. All required inclusion criteria are met (task-based fMRI of social processing; healthy adult sample within 18–65; whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported; acceptable reporting via figures/tables/coordinates). None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, sample within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social sharing (a social-related process) using a task manipulating whether participants viewed emotional stimuli together vs alone. Sample consists of healthy adult volunteers aged 20–33 (n=58 behavioral, n=26 fMRI), satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, within-subject whole-brain random-effects analyses and presents whole-brain corrected activations (e.g., DLPFC, precuneus) as well as ROI-corrected reward circuitry results (VS, OFC). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 27.2) who watched realistic social interaction video clips during whole-brain fMRI. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain contrasts (relational vs. alone; relational vs. rest) with correction for multiple comparisons and presents figures and tables of activations. The methods, results, and discussion are present and sufficient. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group task activation maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI during a social-evaluation task (I3) and includes healthy adult participants aged 18–22.9 (I4). However, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain task activation map specifically for a healthy adult group (I5 not met). Analyses are conducted across a mixed-age sample (8–22.9 years) using age predictors and report age-related effects and whole-brain maps across the entire sample, but no unmasked adult-only whole-brain task effect or separate adult subgroup results are presented. Because the sample includes participants under 18 and adult-only results are not reported separately, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adults (N=304; ages 18–22). It reports task-evoked, group-level voxelwise analyses including a main effect of unreciprocated cooperation (CD>CC) across participants and whole-brain analyses (with results referenced in main text and supplementary figures/tables). Thus it meets inclusion: I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task effect reported), and I6 (whole-brain results available in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and includes unmasked healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathy/multimodal social communication) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=24; mean age 35.3, within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task analyses (GLM, cluster-corrected voxelwise results) and within-group T-contrasts for each participant group (controls), with activations described in the text and cited supplementary tables/figures (channel-sensitive contrasts, online Tables DS3–5). All core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (gaze shifts of a face) that manipulates social context during a stimulus–response compatibility paradigm. The sample comprises 23 healthy adult participants (ages 21–37). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (second-level SPM ANOVA), with thresholded SPMs, cluster-level corrected results, tables/figures of activations (main effects and interactions) clearly coming from the healthy group. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 22–35) that investigates co-speech gestures and narrative comprehension — a social-communication paradigm. The methods report task-based, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected results and tables of peak coordinates (contrasts and cluster extents are provided). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample within 18–65; I5: whole-brain group-level task maps reported; I6: whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study used a social attribution (Theory of Mind) task (People vs. Bumper conditions) and reports task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise results. The paper includes group-level whole-brain maps and contrasts for the healthy control group (CON) separately (figures and tables showing CON People–Bumper maps and ROI coordinates/values), satisfying the requirement to report healthy-group whole-brain task effects. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=17, ages 18–45). Although a clinical group (recovered AN) is also included, results for the healthy group are reported separately. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age out of range, non-empirical) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This fMRI study directly examines social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluations) using an active task, satisfying the review’s definition of social processing. The sample consists of healthy adults (final N=31, ages 19–24), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (contrasts SC vs SA, OA vs OC, SA vs Fixation) and a whole-brain multiple regression with self-esteem, with tables of coordinates and figures; psychophysiological interaction results are supplementary but whole-brain activation maps and coordinates are clearly reported in the main text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial emotion recognition (a social-related task—perception/understanding of others), conducted in a healthy adult sample (29 participants aged 20–35). The paper reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (FWE-corrected whole-brain results, tables/figures and SPM random effects analyses are described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI collected during a social group categorization task (group membership and emotion processing), in a sample of healthy adults (N=20 analyzed; mean age 23.4). The paper presents whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (SPM8; voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction) and reports localization and coordinates of activation clusters (e.g., mPFC, STS/TPJ). The manuscript includes methods, results, and tables/figures describing whole-brain findings for the healthy participant group. Therefore it meets the review's requirements for fMRI during social processing, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level results.

This is an event-related task fMRI study of social-related processing (self-reference vs other-reference) in healthy adults (N=110, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (SR>OR, OR>SR, SR+OR>baseline) with FWE-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates/figures, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the review’s fMRI social-task focus, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (the paper includes whole-brain task activation maps in addition to DCM analyses).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction (gaze-based joint attention) in healthy adult participants (n=24, age 20–34). Group-level within-subject contrasts (e.g., self>other, JA>NJA, selfjoint>selfnonjoint, otherjoint>othernonjoint) are reported with peak MNI coordinates and statistical inference; results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Although multiple-comparison correction was performed using small-volume correction (SVC) within a priori ROIs, the analyses were voxelwise contrasts across the brain and peak coordinates are provided (acceptable per I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (empathy for pain modulated by minimal ingroup/outgroup manipulation), conducted in healthy adults (N=30, ages 18–35). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 ANOVA; main effects and interactions with tables of activations, cluster sizes, and corrected/uncorrected thresholds), clearly attributable to the healthy sample. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The provided file contains abstract, highlights, keywords, and references but lacks core article sections (methods, participants, detailed results, and figures/tables). From the abstract it is clear this is an fMRI study of social cognition (cooperation vs. competition), so inclusion criterion I3 is met. However, I cannot verify participant details (age range and whether a healthy adult group is reported separately) or whether at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported. Therefore I4 and I5 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied from the truncated content. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot determine eligibility with certainty; the study is therefore excluded at this stage pending access to the complete article (full methods and results including participant demographics and whole-brain analyses).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–31) using a social cognition task (joint attention/attribution of what another person sees). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (body>place and place>body contrasts) with statistical maps and a table of activation coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full methods, results, and discussion are provided in the full text.

The study includes an fMRI experiment using a social-related task (interactive social gaze/joint attention) and reports group-level fMRI results for a healthy adult control group (n=16). A voxelwise one-sample (control group) contrast (self-initiated JA > self-initiated NJA) was conducted and reported (see Fig. S4 and Table S4) after whole-brain GLM analysis (threshold uncorrected p<0.005) with subsequent SVC in predefined ROIs. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, and healthy-group results are clearly described with coordinates/figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. Note: primary inference used ROI SVC, but a within-group voxelwise contrast in controls was performed and reported.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that probes social-cognitive processing (why/how judgments about actions that engage mentalizing/theory-of-mind processes). Sample: healthy adults (N=17 after exclusions), ages 21–46, satisfying the age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (cluster-level FWE correction, whole-brain maps, Supplementary Tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (causal attributions/mentalizing) using an event-related task in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–41) with no psychiatric diagnoses. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (each attribution locus > truth baseline), conjunctions, and whole-brain analyses with voxelwise thresholds and FWE-corrected results (see Table 1 and figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and clearly separates healthy-group findings. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of impression formation (social evaluation) in healthy adults using a block-design task manipulating moral and financial status, satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample: 20 healthy adult males (age 19–31) — meets the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA and provides whole-brain activation results (Table 1, Fig. 3) derived from group-level contrast images (condition vs. fixation), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are reported in tables/figures. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.1) that investigates social processing (learning of includer/excluder roles) using task-related fMRI during face perception pre- and post-social interaction. It meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65). Although primary results are ROI-based, the paper also reports a group-level, whole-brain searchlight analysis with family-wise-error-corrected effects in superior temporal sulcus (MNI coordinates reported), satisfying I5 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results) and I6 (coordinates/results clearly described). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of pragmatic language processing involving social inferences from voices (a social-related task). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=24, ages 18–39) reported separately. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level task contrasts and reports within-group whole-brain activation maps/clusters for the control group (tables/figures and text), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (the ultimatum game) with healthy adult participants (male, ages 23–28). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: offline whole-brain SVM classification across subjects with discriminating volumes reported as MNI coordinates (Tables/Figures) and thresholding (p<0.05), allowing identification of informative brain regions beyond pre-specified ROIs. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review requirements for a healthy-adult, task-based fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (55 healthy young men, age within 18–65) using a social-related task (erotic/attachment and fearful social scenes) and intranasal oxytocin. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., erotic > neutral, fearful > neutral, erotic > fearful) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and ROI analyses; coordinates and thresholding are described and supplementary tables are referenced. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI during social-related processing (dynamic happy and fearful facial expressions), includes a healthy adult control group (n=52; age early 20s within 18–65), and provides group-level whole-brain task activation maps and contrasts for the control and FR groups (figures and cluster-level statistics reported). Whole-brain analyses were carried out (FLAME; cluster thresholding) and results for the healthy/control group are presented in figures/tables, satisfying reporting requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is present in the provided content.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: participants performed a referential communication task and compared collaboratively vs individually encoded labels, engaging social cognition (theory of mind) networks. Sample: healthy adult participants (ages 18–33; N=70) meeting age and health criteria. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task contrasts are reported and corrected for multiple comparisons (cluster-level correction; tables/figures of contrasts provided). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about others’ mental states) using healthy adults (N=20; ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight MVPA and network analyses with one-sample random-effects t tests and cluster correction), and presents statistical maps and tables (figures and supplementary tables). The task and measures clearly address social-related processing. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This is an fMRI study of social cooperation (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (final N=18, mean age ~21). The task is clearly social-related, and the paper reports both ROI and whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts with tables of coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected results (e.g., CC > other outcomes; context interactions), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI to probe social processing of gaze direction (I3). It includes a typically developing (healthy) control group composed of adolescents and adults (age range includes adults up to 42.4) and reports the healthy/control group results separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts for the typically developing group (Direct > Averted gaze) with coordinates and cluster statistics presented in Table 2 and figures (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group healthy whole-brain effects are provided. Although the healthy group includes some participants under 18, adults are included and their group-level results are reported separately, which satisfies the age/sample requirement. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: Reading the Mind in the Eyes ToM task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, the paper only reports between-group voxelwise comparisons (high-risk vs low-risk) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map (or clearly described within-group whole-brain results) for the healthy/control group alone. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map). Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social cognition task (the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test), in healthy adult participants (16 typical young women, mean age 20.8). The manuscript includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (emotion vs control) with cluster-level FWE correction and corresponding tables/figures describing these whole-brain activations; thus group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy sample are clearly reported. The study therefore meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not only connectivity/resting-state; not between-group-only; participants are within 18–65; empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This study meets all inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI of a social-related process (perception/understanding of others’ actions via point-light biological motion) (I3). The sample is healthy adults (13 right-handed males, mean age 28.2) reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts (canonical vs scrambled biological motion; p<0.05 corrected) with coordinates and tables (I5, I6). Although the paper also includes connectivity/DCM analyses, whole-brain task results are present and clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (dynamic face processing) and includes a healthy adult control group, the manuscript does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Results focus on between-group contrasts (patients vs controls) and do not present a standalone healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study uses a social-related task (social reward; mutual liking) and reports whole-brain results (I3 and I6 satisfied). However, it does not report results for a separate healthy adult/control group: the sample (n=27) is a mixed late-adolescent sample (ages 18–21) including participants with current Major Depressive Disorder and analyses are dimensional/regression-based across the whole sample rather than reporting a distinct healthy adult group-level whole-brain task map. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (separate healthy adult group results) and I5 (a whole-brain task-evoked map clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the review (E2–E6) are directly triggered, but failure to meet key inclusion criteria requires exclusion.

The provided content appears to be an abstract/summary only and lacks complete methods and results. Inclusion: I3 is met (fMRI during a social-related task: viewing/imitating/producing facial expressions and social hand gestures). Cannot verify I4 because participant ages and confirmation of a healthy adult (18–65) group are not reported in the provided text. Cannot verify I5 because the excerpt does not explicitly state that at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group is reported (though activations and significant differences are described, the full methods/results are missing). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available information. Due to incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending access to full article to confirm I4 and I5.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants (N=34, healthy adults, mean age 22.2) watched a movie and analyses show the DMPFC preferentially responds to social interactions. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise reverse-correlation results (group-level maps/statistics; Fig. 3 and associated χ2 thresholding) and ROI analyses. Thus it provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results from a healthy adult sample during a social-related task. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses (fcMRI) rather than task-evoked fMRI during a social-related task (Exclusion E3). In addition, the sample comprises adolescents aged 11–18 (both ASD and typically developing), not healthy adults aged 18–65 (Exclusion E5). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use task-based fMRI for social processing; uses resting-state), I4 (sample is not healthy adults 18–65), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy/control adult group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of facial emotional processing (social perception) and includes a separate healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the full text reports primarily between-group contrasts (VCFS vs controls) and presents between-group differences (Table 1) without reporting an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no control-group whole-brain main-effect or within-group contrast maps or tables of control-only coordinates are provided). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map) and consequently I6 (acceptable reporting formats for such healthy-group whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI study using a Theory of Mind (social cognition) task (animated shapes) in adults and includes a healthy control group (n=20, ages 22–56). The paper provides within-group whole-brain task-evoked activation results for the healthy subjects (significant activations, corrected, reported in text/tables/figures) and reports between-group random-effects analyses. Full methods, results, and discussion are present, and healthy-group whole-brain activations are clearly described. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=46, ages 18–45) during viewing of emotionally negative IAPS images, a social/emotion-related paradigm engaging perception/understanding of others (images contained people and dmPFC/social-cognition interpretations are discussed). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results for the HA− > Neutral contrast (thresholds, cluster sizes, and activated regions described; supplementary table referenced), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only reporting, age range appropriate, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an event-related fMRI study of social evaluation (trustworthiness judgments) in healthy adult participants (initial N=16, 14 included in analyses; ages 18–30), satisfying the sample requirement. The paradigm is clearly social (perception/understanding of others). Group-level random-effects SPM analyses across the healthy subject group are reported, with whole-brain results and coordinate tables and figures; small-volume corrections were applied for ROIs but whole-brain task-evoked effects and coordinates are provided. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related Theory of Mind task (satisfies I3) and includes a separate healthy control group reported alongside patients (satisfies I4). However, the paper reports results primarily as between-group contrasts (ALS > HC) and uses ROI-restricted (small volume) second-level analyses. It does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Therefore exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI-restricted results without whole-brain results) and E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts without a healthy-group whole-brain task effect) apply. Full text appears complete.

Study meets several inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI for a social-related task (eye-gaze/social cognition) (I3), reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the neurologically normal (control) group (I5), and presents results in figures/tables/coordinates consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). However, it does not satisfy the sample criterion (I4) requiring at least one group of healthy adult participants aged 18–65: the reported control group age range includes a 15.5-year-old (range 15.5–32.4), so the healthy group cannot be confirmed to consist solely of adults within 18–65. No exclusion criteria from the list directly apply. Therefore the study is excluded because I4 is not met.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review: the study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (face emotion discrimination), reports data from a healthy adult community sample (screened for Axis I disorders), and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (one-sample and contrast maps with tables of coordinates and flexible factorial group analyses). The full text includes introduction, methods, results (task effects across participants and group contrasts), and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and within-group healthy-task effects are reported).

The full text reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (social motor response/inclusion-exclusion) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 42 ±12). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examines cortical processing of voices—a social-perception task—comparing adults with autism and age-matched healthy adult controls. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise activation for the control group (voice > non-voice, P < 0.001 corrected) with figures and supplementary tables, and provides separate results for the healthy adult group (n=8, mean age 27.1). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. This full-text reports an fMRI study using a third-party punishment task that assesses social cognition/mentalizing (perception/understanding of others), satisfying I3. The sample comprises 26 healthy adult participants (mean age 26 ±5.7), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with voxelwise activations and Talairach coordinates (e.g., R TPJ, R anterior insula) using an FDR threshold, meeting I5. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and tables, meeting I6. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext appears complete). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (charitable donation decisions), with a task probing affiliation/attachment and moral/social decision-making. Sample: 19 healthy adult participants (mean age 28.2) within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported (random effects analyses, contrasts, tables of coordinates, and thresholding described), and the text/Methods present whole-brain analysis details. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (biological motion) using a passive viewing task (point-light displays), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=48, ages 20–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts (e.g., biological > scrambled motion, Sex×Condition ANOVA) with cluster correction and provides tables/figures of results. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an event-related BOLD fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-cognitive task addressing ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’), conducted in healthy adult participants (12 right-handed males, mean age ~19). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., self vs. familiar, familiar vs. unknown, unknown vs. scrambled) with statistical thresholds and cluster reporting. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain task fMRI in healthy adults.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (gaze-following toward political in-group/out-group faces), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=28 after exclusions), ages 18–36, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (incongruent > congruent) with voxelwise results, cluster-level correction, tables of activated clusters and figures, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly reported (no exclusive clinical groups). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy for pain (a social-cognitive task: perception/understanding of others) including a healthy adult control group (13 controls, mean age ~33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts and tables/figures for the control group (within-group [Painful–Baseline] and [Painful–Nonpainful] effects, with coordinate tables and figures), satisfying requirements for unmasked whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind) using the REMICS task, which manipulates social vs. physical scenarios and contextual adjustments. The sample is healthy adults (n=19; ages 20–53), meeting the 18–65 requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (one-sample t-tests, voxelwise p<.001 with cluster correction; peak coordinates and tables provided), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so fulltext appears complete. Therefore I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This article reports an event-related fMRI study of a social cognition task (false-belief/theory-of-mind), uses healthy adult participants (n=34, ages 20–28), and presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and tables (ROMS vs CTRL) with voxelwise statistical thresholds and coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, behavioral and fMRI procedures), Results (behavioral and whole-brain activation results, ROI and correlation analyses), and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20 males, mean age 24.8) performing a social decision-making task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma probing cooperation/trust). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (flexible factorial and one-sample t tests) with FWE cluster-corrected results and tables/figures of activations across task phases, clearly from the healthy/control group. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI during social-related tasks, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task activation reporting.

This fMRI study examines social processing (interpersonal resource conflict) using task-based fMRI (I3 satisfied). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age 23.5; final N=17), satisfying the adult healthy-sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Conflict > No Conflict; interaction and covariate whole-brain analyses) with thresholded maps, tables, and figures, providing unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation results (I5 and I6 satisfied). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the age range. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and figures/tables, so fulltext appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study manipulating social vs. nonsocial working memory (n-back) in healthy adults (mean age 22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster-corrected results and tables of peak coordinates and maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind; Why/How contrast) in healthy adult participants (ages 19–38). This paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) in healthy adult samples across three experiments (Exp1a N=25, Exp1b N=65, Exp2 N=178). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–25) using a social, competitive matching-pennies task with pre-scanning social interactions. This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathic concern) using empathy-evoking film clips and contextual/musical manipulations, with healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 30.3) and group-level whole-brain task analyses. This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (joint attention) in healthy adult participants (discovery n=26, replication n=50; ages reported within 18–65). These voxelwise component maps and the reported within-group statistical association with the interaction phase meet the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results (reported in figures/tables and text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not resting-state-only/seed-based-only; not between-group-only contrasts; participants are within age range; empirical data present).

This report describes an fMRI study of social cognition (trustworthiness judgments) using a task with feedback—clearly a social-related task (I3). This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures) in healthy adults, reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (TFCE permutation testing, tables/figures provided). This study reports task-based fMRI of face perception (a social-cognition task: Perception/Understanding of Others), includes a healthy adult group (adults aged 18–37) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (faces>objects contrast and whole-brain linear regression maps reported in figures and Table 3) derived from the healthy sample. This study used task-based fMRI to test emotion modulation of a trained mirror-neuron response (social-related processing/emotion), enrolled healthy adult participants (mean age 27.7, N=19), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with coordinates and cluster-corrected results (e.g., untrained>trained whole-brain activations in SMA and IFG). This fMRI study examines evaluative processes of social/moral emotions (guilt, embarrassment) — a clearly social-related task involving Theory of Mind and perception/understanding of others. The sample comprises 19 healthy adult participants (ages in reported means within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (contrasts G−N, E−N, E−G, G−E) using SPM, with tables of peak coordinates and thresholded statistical maps/figures. Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of perspective-taking/empathy (social-related processing) in healthy adults (n=18; ages 21–31). The full text includes detailed methods, results, and discussion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Self vs Other; View-Pain vs View-No-Pain), conjunctions, and cluster/peak coordinates with FWE-corrected inference and ROI SVC details, clearly attributable to the healthy sample. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for task relevance, sample, and whole-brain healthy-group results; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses a social face-processing task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (I4). However, it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The paper reports whole-brain results for the combined sample and reports between-group contrasts (NT vs AS) and ROI analyses for the control group, but no standalone, unmasked voxelwise healthy-group faces>houses activation map is provided. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts/interaction without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This is an fMRI study of social processing that includes a healthy adult (neurotypical) control group and uses a naturalistic social task (watching a TV episode), so it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). However, the paper does not present a within-group, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The whole-brain results are reported either collapsed across groups (all subjects) or as between-group contrasts (NT > ASD). Because there is no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map clearly reported, it fails inclusion criterion I5 and therefore must be excluded under exclusion criterion E4.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a socially relevant interaction (a Taylor Aggression Paradigm with opponent facial expressions), includes a healthy adult sample (32 healthy males, mean age 23.3), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (angry>neutral contrasts with cluster-wise FWE correction, tables/figures). Whole-brain results are clearly presented in the text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (analyses are not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity or between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and this is an empirical fMRI paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The paper is excluded because it does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI activation maps for healthy participants. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample of healthy adults, N=63). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (this study reports structural VBM analyses, not an fMRI task-based whole-brain study; only references prior fMRI data used in a secondary correlation), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI map from the healthy/control group is reported), I6 (not applicable because no fMRI whole-brain results are provided). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) specifically apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text provided appears to be title, abstract, and metadata only (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on available information: Inclusion met: I3 (study uses fMRI during social-related task—face/voice perception). Inclusion not met / not verifiable: I4 (participant demographics/confirmation of healthy adults aged 18–65 not reported in the excerpt), I5 (no verifiable group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps can be confirmed from the abstract alone). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the excerpt, but because essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I exclude. Recommend obtaining the complete article (methods and results) to reassess.

This is an fMRI study explicitly probing social-related processing (group vs individual social interaction images; participants asked to imagine themselves — mentalizing/empathy), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=29, mean age 32.4) reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts for control subjects (main effects and group-positive/group-negative vs individual contrasts) with MNI coordinates and figures describing the control-group activations, satisfying I5 and the acceptable reporting formats in I6. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Note: several reported effects were tested within predefined ROIs and reported with small-volume correction, but the manuscript nevertheless presents voxelwise control-group contrasts with coordinates and figures. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion as an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=14, mean age 29.4) that used a social-related task (observing social interactions vs non-social motions) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task contrast (SI vs NSI) with FDR-corrected results and peak coordinates/tables. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, ages within 18–65, empirical study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related face identity discrimination task (social perception of others) and reports results for a healthy adult control group (CA; mean age 31 years, N=17). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are described and visualized (mean z-score images for CA controls are shown; group ANOVA and voxelwise maps corrected for multiple comparisons are reported), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural processes during a social-communication task (message propagation), using healthy adult participants (interns N=19, producers N=79; mean ages ~20.5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (thresholds and cluster correction described; coordinates/tables referenced) linking neural activity to social influence outcomes. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-adult sample, or non-empirical paper) apply.

The available content (title/abstract/metadata) shows this is a task-based fMRI study of mentalizing (social cognition) including a healthy control group of adults, so I3 and I4 are met. However the provided full text is incomplete (only metadata/abstract present) and does not allow verification that the paper reports at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked map for the healthy/control group (I5). Because I5 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included. No specific exclusion criteria (E2–E6) could be confirmed from the truncated content.

This is an fMRI study of impression formation (social perception of others) using an event-related task pairing faces with political views—clearly a social-related task. Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–30; n=18 after exclusions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent) with FDR correction and tables/figures of activations (Table 1, Fig. 2) and MNI coordinates; ROI analyses supplement but do not replace whole-brain results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables, references).
