This is a task-based fMRI study using a social-related paradigm (participants imagine/mentalize performing body-checking actions of another person), addressing perception/understanding of self and others. It includes a healthy control group (n=15 age-matched females within the study's 17–34 range, i.e., adults included in 18–65) and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy/control group (figures and cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (observation of socio-affective touch) (I3); includes a separately reported healthy neurotypical adult group (n=21) (I4); and reports group-level whole-brain task activation results for the healthy/control group (univariate contrasts, with group maps and MNI coordinates reported in main/supplementary figures and tables, satisfying I5 and I6). The full article text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only without healthy-group maps, age range appropriate, empirical fMRI study).

This is an event-related fMRI study of self-recognition (face and name) addressing perception/understanding of self, a social-related construct. Participants were healthy adults (n=35 analyzed; ages 18–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with contrasts and cluster/corrected thresholds; coordinates and figures/tables of activation peaks are provided. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical, or age outside range) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Full text is paywalled and not available here (fulltext_incomplete=true). The abstract indicates an fMRI task using dynamic social interaction videos in healthy young adult volunteers, so I3 (social-task fMRI) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported) are likely satisfied. However, I cannot verify whether the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5) because methods, results, tables/coordinates and figures are inaccessible. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the abstract alone. Because a required inclusion criterion (I5) cannot be confirmed from the available content, I exclude this study pending access to the full text.

This is an fMRI study of perception of different laughter types (social communication/emotional processing), using healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 26). The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and conjunction contrasts (reported in tables and figures with MNI coordinates and corrected ROI analyses), showing stimulus- and task-driven effects. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for fMRI during a social-related task in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18–37) that investigates social cognitive processing (empathy/Theory of Mind) using narrative tasks—meeting the review's definition of social-related tasks. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SnPM whole-brain contrasts, corrected p<0.05) with coordinates and figures, and also presents methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self, mother, president referential judgments — self/other perception), (I4) includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=15, ages 31–58) reported separately, (I5) reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps/statistics for the healthy control group (within-group t-tests and ANOVA; figures and corrected maps shown), and (I6) whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not resting-state or connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20 males, ages 20–28) that used task-based fMRI while subjects watched traffic-awareness campaign videos designed to elicit empathy (a social-related task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects one-sample t-test; CV>NV contrast) with FWE-corrected results and provides tables/peak coordinates and figures. Behavioral measures of empathic expression were related to BOLD responses in STS. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables/figures provided). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that used a social perception task (viewing approaching characters with angry vs. happy expressions) addressing affiliation/dominance (social-related processing). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (Angry>Happy and Happy>Angry) with coordinates, figures, and random-effects analyses in healthy subjects. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain task activation in healthy adults (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=41, mean age ~22) using a social-affective mimicry task probing affiliative/ social processing (emotion and group membership), satisfying the review topic (I3). The paper reports within-group, group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Incongruent>Congruent and masked contrasts), provides tables of activation coordinates and cluster-level whole-brain corrected results (I5, I6). Sample meets the adult healthy range and results are reported for the healthy group (I4). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, not outside age range, and it is an empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=40, mean age ~25.8) that manipulates social touch context and reports task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise results (tables of coordinates, cluster statistics, and family-wise error corrected p-values). The task probes social-related processing (affiliation/affective social touch). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary materials not required for eligibility.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract provided). Based on available content: I3 (fMRI during a social attribution task) and I4 (healthy young adult sample) are clearly met. However I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group) cannot be verified from the abstract alone. I6 (allowable formats) likewise cannot be confirmed. Because I5 (required whole-brain evidence) is not verifiable, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded pending full-text confirmation. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met based on available information. Request full article (methods/results/tables/figures) to reassess inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Chinese college students) performing social-related tasks (self-, mother-, and celebrity-judgments assessing mental, social, and physical attributes), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (simple and hierarchical regression in SPM2) with results presented in tables and figures (Tables 2–3, Figures 1–2) and multiple whole-brain contrasts (self vs celebrity, mother vs celebrity), satisfying I5 and I6. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (in-group vs out-group action perception) in healthy adult volunteers. The sample comprises healthy, right-handed Caucasian males with ages reported (behavioral: 17–39; fMRI: 17–43) and group-level analyses are reported for the healthy sample. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., own team > other team; paired-trial judgments > baseline) with coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction for the whole brain. The article includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Although a small number of participants are reported as age 17, the sample is otherwise healthy adult volunteers and the paper reports group-level healthy participant results, so inclusion criterion for healthy adult sample is satisfied. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E4: The paper’s whole-brain analyses are reported only as between-group (control > patient) contrasts from an exploratory voxel-wise analysis; it does not report an unmasked, within-group whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social task — multi-round trust game) and I4 (healthy adult control group, results reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map identified as coming from the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (laughter perception and explicit social evaluation) using task-based fMRI. Inclusion criteria met: I3 — tasks involve social communication/perception (laughter type categorization and implicit bout counting); I4 — healthy adult sample (n=18, mean age 26, screened for neurological/psychiatric illness); I5 — reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., CSL>TIC, CAT>COU) with statistical thresholds and FWE cluster correction; I6 — whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is original empirical data). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials noted but not required. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

Although this is an fMRI study of facial emotion recognition (a social perception task) in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain coordinate tables for group comparisons, the paper only presents between-group (LDA vs HDA) whole-brain contrasts without reporting an accompanying unmasked, within-healthy-group whole-brain task activation map (e.g., a main effect of emotion > neutral across the healthy sample or an unmasked LDA or combined healthy-group task map). This means it reports only subgroup comparisons rather than a clear healthy-group whole-brain task effect required by the review. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4.

This study should be excluded because it reports only seed-based intrinsic/background functional connectivity analyses (seed-based voxelwise coupling) derived from task fMRI data and does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy control group. It does meet inclusion criteria I3 (uses fMRI with a social-perception task context) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). It does NOT meet I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported). Therefore exclusion criterion E3 applies (connectivity-only analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (subjective pleasantness of social reputation) using a task during fMRI. The sample comprises 28 healthy adult participants (14 males, 14 females; ages 20–24), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (voxelwise threshold p<0.001, cluster-level FWE p<0.05) with coordinates and a results table, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and is original empirical work). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a social-related task (viewing dyadic biological motion depicting social interactions) while performing an orthogonal task, satisfying the construct of perception and understanding of others. The sample consists of healthy adults (10 right-handed males, mean age 25) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise activation contrasts (e.g., atypical > typical) with cluster-size correction and tables/coordinates, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported in the main text, figures, and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study uses rt-fMRI targeting the right pSTS for facial/social communication processing, so it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related task). However, no participant/sample details are reported in the provided content, so I4 (healthy adult sample with results reported separately) cannot be confirmed. The abstract describes correlation analyses focused on activations extracted from the right pSTS (an ROI) rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task activation maps; therefore I5 is not met and exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) appears to apply. Because whole-brain healthy-group task maps are not reported in the provided text and key sample information is missing, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded. Full text incomplete flag set.

Full text provided appears incomplete (abstract, highlights, and metadata only). From the abstract, the study used fMRI during a social-related task (emotion face perception) in 40 healthy volunteers, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, I cannot verify that group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group are reported (I5) because methods/results sections are missing. Without the full text, it is not possible to confirm whole-brain results (or rule out that only ROI/seed-based analyses were reported). Per screening rules, all inclusion criteria must be verified; therefore the record is excluded pending access to full text. Request full article to reassess.

Full text appears to be a list of experimental stimuli and metadata (title, authors, journal, DOI) but lacks core sections (methods, participants, fMRI acquisition/analysis, results, group-level whole-brain statistical maps). Therefore I cannot verify required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none can be confidently confirmed. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I3 (cannot verify fMRI task details and confirmation of functional MRI use from the provided content), I4 (sample details and confirmation of healthy adult group not provided), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or contrasts are present), I6 (no clear whole-brain results in text/tables/figures/supplementary provided). No exclusion criteria from list E2–E6 are clearly met based on the available content, but because the full text is incomplete (core content missing), I exclude the study pending complete full text.

The study is an fMRI investigation of social evaluation (approachability judgments of faces) in healthy adult participants and the abstract reports group-level neural activations (e.g., left amygdala, frontal gyri) linked to task conditions and trait anxiety, meeting the review topic and sample criteria. However, the provided full-text is incomplete/behind paywall and I cannot verify whether a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map or coordinate tables are reported (required for I5/I6). Because the full article content (methods/results with explicit whole-brain statistics or coordinate listings) is not accessible here, I mark fulltext_incomplete=true and apply only the inclusion criteria that can be confidently ascertained from available content.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (action understanding; why/how task), using healthy adult participants (ages 18–32). Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses are reported with coordinates (Table 1) and random-effects analyses; whole-brain results are referenced as provided in the Supplemental Material. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes core article content (methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level voxelwise task results reported/coordinates), and I6 (results presented in tables/ supplemental as described). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (viewing faces of political candidates), includes healthy adult participants (20 registered voters, ages within 18–65), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (faces vs rest and contrasts) with thresholding and tables/figures. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age out-of-range only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study investigating neural processing of emotional facial expressions (social communication / perception of others) using a task-based design — satisfying I3. The sample includes 23 healthy adult human participants aged 24–34, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with significance maps (Figures 3,4) and stereotactic coordinates in supplementary tables, fulfilling I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata), so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: analyses are whole-brain task-evoked activations (not ROI-only, not resting-state, and healthy adult results are reported separately). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is included.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (face/gaze processing) in healthy adult men (meets I3 and I4). However, the reported neuroimaging results appear to be primarily between-group comparisons (low fear scorers vs. normal fear scorers) and the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map from a general healthy/control group independent of the narrowly defined subgroups. This violates the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5) and therefore meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study of labeling brief emotional facial expressions, which qualifies as social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises 50 healthy adult participants aged 18–29. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps and main effects (HA>NE, AN>NE, FE>NE) and second-level regression results with cluster-level FWE-corrected statistics and reported coordinates/tables. Results are reported for the healthy sample (no exclusive reliance on subgroup or between-group contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (facial emotion and age judgments of faces), meeting I3. The sample includes a community control group of healthy adults (age inclusion criteria 18–65 reported), and results for controls are reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps and between- and within-group whole-brain contrasts (cluster-based permutation testing, tables/figures/coordinates are provided), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include an unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented a social interaction simulation probing friendship (meets I3). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (28 right-handed, mean age 22.6; meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVA; FWE-corrected results, cluster tables/figures are provided), satisfying I5 and I6. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not restricted to non-adult ages, and is empirical).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/summary provided). I3 is met: the study used fMRI during a social-related task (decoding vocal emotional prosody). However I4 (sample: healthy adults 18–65) cannot be confirmed because participant demographics/age are not reported in the provided content. I5 (reporting at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the abstract; the paper describes multivariate pattern decoding in auditory cortex but does not clearly report whole-brain group-level voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the available content. Because core information required to verify inclusion (I4, I5) is missing, the study cannot be included based on the provided full text.

The provided content appears to be only the abstract/full text is incomplete, so I cannot verify whether the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy adult group (required I5/I6). Based on available information: the study is an fMRI task examining self-regulation/personal goals (social cognition), and reports data from 16 participants (healthy adults), so I3 and I4 appear satisfied. However, I cannot confirm whole-brain group-level results from the truncated text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone. Because full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria (I5/I6) cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a social-related Face Matching Task (implicit emotion/face perception), with a sample of healthy adults (n=10, mean age 25, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests; results referenced in Supplementary Table S2 and Figures S1–S3) in addition to ICA. Thus it provides whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps from the healthy/control group. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not solely seed/connectivity or resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, participants are adults, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of prosocial decisions toward family—a social-related construct involving mentalizing/affiliation—satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults (Mage=20.2, n=25) meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward) with tables of coordinates and whole-brain-corrected results, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or non-adult sample) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social attribution (self/other responsibility) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults. The sample comprises 12 healthy right-handed adult males (ages 20–51). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM fixed-effects; significant activations reported at P<0.05 corrected and shown in tables/figures) for contrasts of interest (internal vs external attributions; self-serving vs non-self-serving), clearly from the healthy participant group. Results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present).

This paper reports task-based fMRI during a social cognition (virtual face-to-face attribution) task (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (14 right-handed healthy volunteers, ages 18–45), reported separately from the bipolar group (meets I4). The authors present group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts for the healthy/control group (e.g., Emotion vs Control within-group maps, Tables of coordinates and figures showing ACC, IFC/insula activations), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (meets I5 and I6). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not restricted-age, and not non-empirical).

The paper reports a task-based fMRI study of affiliative/attachment-related social processing (affiliation/kinship scenarios), with healthy adult participants (final N=27; ages within 18–65). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., affiliative vs nonaffiliative; FWE-corrected results and whole-brain maps/tables/figures), and healthy-group results are clearly described. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI with social stimuli—happy, fearful, neutral faces) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with effects reported separately). However, the reported fMRI results are restricted to an a priori amygdala ROI with statistics corrected within that ROI; the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map or whole-brain coordinates for the healthy group. Therefore it fails I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses reported without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion IDs met: E2. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction (joke-telling and listener laughter) in healthy adults (n=38; ages 19–29). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (SPM analyses) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates and statistical maps for main effects and interactions. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria: uses fMRI during a social-related task (I3), includes a healthy adult sample within 18–65 (I4), and reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked voxelwise results clearly identified as the healthy group (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not solely connectivity/resting-state; includes within-group healthy task effects).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (direct vs averted gaze) using a task engaging social cognition, meeting the review’s definition of social-related task. The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=16) reported separately. The manuscript reports whole-brain, group-level within-control-group task activation results (whole-brain analyses and figures/tables reporting cortical activations for controls), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-group healthy results, empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of audiovisual integration of non-verbal emotional signals (social communication) in a healthy adult sample (24 adults, age 18–41), so it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult participants). However, the paper uses a region-of-interest (individual STS mapping) analysis and reports results based on extracted ROI/measuring-point contrast estimates rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. No unmasked, whole-brain group task activation map or voxelwise results for the healthy group are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and does not meet I5/I6. Decision: EXCLUDED.

Exclusion E4 applies: the study reports whole-brain task activation maps, but only for a clinical group (depressed mothers); no healthy adult control group whole-brain task effect is reported. Inclusion I3 is met (study uses fMRI during a social-related task—mothers viewing affective clips of their own children). Inclusion I4 is NOT met: there is no healthy adult (18–65) group reported separately. Inclusion I5 is NOT met: although whole-brain results are reported, they are not reported for a healthy/control group as required. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (perception of fearful vs. neutral body gestures), includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=12; adults within the 18–65 range), and presents group-level whole-brain task activation results for controls (conjunctions, between-group maps, tables and figures showing control-specific activations in amygdala, IFG, PM, STS). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (SPM2, thresholding, tables). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathic (social) decision-making in healthy adult participants (n=32 males, mean age 22.8), meeting the review’s population requirement. The task explicitly probes social processing (empathic choice / understanding others), satisfying the social-related task criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation results (GLM contrasts, conjunctions) with cluster-level correction and provides tables of activations (Tables 1–5) and figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, participants within 18–65, empirical data present). Therefore the study should be included.

Although this is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4), the paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (e.g., main effect of face viewing). The reported whole-brain voxelwise results are seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analyses and the primary activation results are reported from functionally or structurally defined ROIs (FFA and amygdala). Therefore the study reports only seed-based connectivity and ROI analyses without a standalone whole-brain healthy-group task activation map, meeting exclusion criterion E3.

The paper reports event-related fMRI of evaluative judgments, a social/self-referential task (theory-of-mind/self-processing). It includes a separate healthy adult control group (mean age 26.4, n=7) and reports whole-brain, group-level within-control contrasts with voxelwise maps and coordinates (figures and Table 3). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interactive task (modified Taylor aggression paradigm) that probes social processing (retaliation, observing another’s suffering, empathy). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=16 males, mean age 28.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM2 results, voxelwise thresholding and whole-brain FDR correction) with coordinates, tables and activation maps for the healthy group. Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly tests social-related processing (perception of socially relevant facial expressions and facial mimicry) using task-based whole-brain fMRI. Participants: 17 healthy right-handed adult males (mean age 25.9) — meets healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects ANOVA, FIR analysis) with reported activations, figures, and stereotactic coordinates (table), clearly attributable to the healthy group. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (core content appears complete). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (biological motion perception), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (N=15, ages within 18–65) with results reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and tables of coordinates for the healthy/control group (within-group contrasts and main effects; P<0.001 uncorrected; tables and figures), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not resting-state-only, and healthy participants are within the age range. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task—live eye contact). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I4 (no participant/sample details or ages provided to confirm healthy adults 18–65), I5 (no report of group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables in the provided text). No exclusion criteria from the list can be confirmed based on the available content. Because the core article content (methods, participants, full results) is not available, I cannot verify critical eligibility items; fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

Exclusion: E3 (study reports only seed-based connectivity/PPI analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — direct vs averted gaze) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no unambiguous whole-brain, task-evoked activation map reported for the healthy/control group — the paper reports whole-brain PPI connectivity results and between-group contrasts; within-group ‘whole brain analyses’ mentioned refer to connectivity and are in supplementary material, not a healthy-group task activation map). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded under E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (gaze-based joint attention) in healthy adults (n=21). The Methods report BOLD fMRI acquisition and group-level GLM analysis (SPM5). Results describe whole-brain, voxelwise task effects (e.g., MPFC, PCC, anterior temporal poles; voxel-level correction noted) comparing joint attention vs non-joint attention and other contrasts. The sample is healthy adults and results are reported for that group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample; I5: whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported; I6: whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used task-based fMRI (viewing humorous vs non-humorous cartoons) addressing social-related processing (humor appreciation/social communication and understanding), included a healthy adult sample (10 healthy male subjects), and performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM regression) with coordinates and figures reported for significant clusters. Whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly described (right inferior parietal lobule cluster and others) and reported in tables/figure. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of eligibility.

This is an fMRI study of charitable donation decisions (a social decision-making task involving empathy and perspective-taking), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: 22 healthy adult females (ages 19–38), meeting the 18–65 healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, whole-brain corrected results, coordinates, and SPM thresholds) and describes these maps and contrasts in detail (figures and supplemental tables). Full methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; contains task activations beyond connectivity analyses).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related face-processing task (familiar vs unfamiliar faces) with healthy control participants and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts for the control group (partner>unfamiliar and faces>baseline). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported for controls), and I6 (results reported as coordinates and contrasts). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete and contains the necessary group-level healthy control whole-brain results.

This is a task-based fMRI study examining neural responses to communicative vs. noncommunicative vocal sounds (social communication domain). Participants: 20 healthy adults (mean age 22) meeting the adult age range. The paper reports random-effects, multisubject, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (vocal > nonvocal; communicative > noncommunicative) thresholded and accompanied by peak coordinates and figures, clearly from the healthy participant group. Full article includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment investigating vicarious somatosensory responses to observed (nonpainful) touch—a social perception task involving understanding others' sensory experiences, satisfying the review objective. Participants were healthy adults (n=22, ages 23–39). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with family-wise error correction and reports voxelwise results (figures and Table 1, peak MNI coordinates), meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based functional MRI of social-related processing (perception of others' eye gaze; social communication). Participants: healthy adults (n=9, mean age 24), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (clusters selected with z>4, cluster extent, Talairach coordinates reported) comparing face versus control and contrasts for identity vs gaze and averted vs direct gaze; results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly probes the mirror neuron system using a social-related task (passive observation of goal-directed hand actions) relevant to perception/understanding of others and empathy. Participants: healthy adult college students (n=37 total; analyzed groups: ALEX n=16, non-ALEX n=13), meeting the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (one-sample tests for each group, conjunction analysis, and tables/figures with MNI coordinates and corrected thresholds), clearly identifying results for the healthy subgroups. ROI analyses are supplemental but whole-brain results are present. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used task-based functional MRI to examine social evaluation (social-meaningful and social-irrelevant vs non-social) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, cluster-corrected) and presents conjunctions and contrasts for the young (20–29) and older (61–85) groups; the young adult group (20–29) satisfies the 18–65 sample requirement and within-group whole-brain task effects are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (final N=33, age 18–21) that uses a social-related task (viewing social vs non-social scenes) probing social cognition/mentalizing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (social > non-social), with FDR-corrected maps and cluster reporting (figures and Table 1 with coordinates) and describes ROI follow-ups; whole-brain evidence is explicitly presented and attributed to the healthy participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of participant characteristics, task, imaging analysis, and experience-sampling behavioral outcomes. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original fMRI study investigating social action perception (recognition of ‘vitality forms’), which is a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others). Participants: 19 healthy adults (ages 21–29) are reported and analyzed as a healthy group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., how vs what) with statistical thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates (Tables 1–3, figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not outside age range, empirical data present). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (comparison of goal-directed vs non-goal-directed biological motion), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=12, mean age 29.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts (BR motion minus BU motion), provides peak coordinates and figure of activations, and describes thresholds used. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 26) that investigates neural processing of empathic vs. unempathic social responses. The task is social (processing empathic comments after negative feedback) and targets social cognition/emotion processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts (e.g., empathic > unempathic; negative > positive feedback) with FWE-corrected clusters and tables of results; figures and methods detail whole-brain SPM analyses. The sample is within the 18–65 range and healthy participants are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so content is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social/intergroup competitive task (self vs. other moral processing) in healthy adults (final N=21, mean age 23.1, no history of psychiatric/neurological problems). The paper reports both ROI and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (whole-brain results described and reported in tables/clusters; see Table 2 and accompanying text) using corrected thresholds. Whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., main effects and contrasts collapsing across conditions) are reported for the healthy participant group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, empirical with original fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This empirical paper uses fMRI during a clearly social impression-formation task (meets I3). The sample is healthy adults (N=19, mean age 19.1), within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (functional localizer: form impression > sequencing) with Talairach coordinates and cluster-correction, and presents coordinates/cluster sizes for the main task as well (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity- or resting-state-only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are in the eligible age range (E5), and it is an empirical fMRI study (not E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adults. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects contrasts; tables/figures of activations) and clearly describes methods, participants (12 healthy adults aged 21–28), results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (live bidirectional conversations; social communication/mentalizing) in a healthy adult sample (n=21, mean age 25.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM full ANOVA; contrasts HHI vs HRI and main effects; FDR-corrected cluster maps) and provides whole-brain results (figures, Neurovault/OpenNeuro links). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and data accessibility).

Although this is an fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults (I3 satisfied) with a healthy adult sample (15 males, age 18–65) meeting I4, the paper reports voxelwise analyses constrained to a priori regions (amygdala ROI and a brainstem ROI) rather than presenting an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The main reported effects (amygdala activation and amygdala–midbrain connectivity) are ROI-based or seed-based connectivity results, and no whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task effect (faces/scenes vs control) is clearly reported for inclusion. Therefore this study meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked map reported), I6 (not applicable because no qualifying whole-brain results are provided). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI task that directly probes social-related processing (social interaction recognition from point-light displays), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult group (n=16, ages 20–41), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (SI > NM contrasts) for the adult group with peak- and cluster-level statistics and FWE-correction statements, fulfilling I5; results are presented in figures/tables consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and within-group whole-brain adult task activations are reported. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Full text provided is incomplete (only abstract and metadata). The abstract confirms fMRI experiments on social interaction/intention, satisfying I3. However, critical criteria cannot be verified from the available content: participant sample characteristics and ages (I4) are not reported in the abstract, and it is not possible to confirm whether whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task activation maps are reported (I5). Therefore the study cannot be included based on the current materials; full text is required to confirm I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively applied from the available information.

Exclusion (E4): The study used task fMRI of social perception and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the manuscript reports whole-brain analyses primarily as between-group contrasts (schizophrenia vs. control) and follows up with ROI analyses. It does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., no standalone whole-brain within-group healthy-control task map is reported). Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (and thus I6 is not applicable since qualifying whole-brain healthy-group results are not provided).

Full text unavailable in the provided content (only abstract/metadata/DOI link). From the abstract the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (pleasant touch) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, I cannot verify whether the paper reports at least one unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked map for the healthy/control group (I5) because the full article (methods/results/tables/figures) is not available. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) can be positively identified from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete and a key inclusion criterion (I5) cannot be verified, I must exclude the study pending full-text review.

The full text describes an fMRI study using a social imitate/observe task (affiliation/social communication/perception of others) (I3). The sample includes healthy adult participants (discovery: 70 controls, ages 18–55; replication: healthy controls included) with results reported separately and analyzed (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (imitate > observe) with first-level t-maps, second-level group analyses, and cluster-level maps; Methods state group analyses were run separately for each site and group and supplemental figures (Figure S1) show group analyses, meeting the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Based on the provided information, the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and is eligible for inclusion.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (simulation/empathy) and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map reported). I6 (acceptable reporting formats) is not satisfied in a qualifying way because the available whole-brain results are reported for the combined HC+SZ sample rather than for the healthy group specifically. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are directly met. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet I5.

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion processing (a social cognition task) that includes a healthy control group and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps for the control group. Methods and results describe within-group one-sample t-tests and paired t-tests in the control participants with whole-brain correction (p<0.05 FWE) and tables of activated regions (Table 3 and supplemental materials). The sample includes healthy adult participants (controls recruited from university/community; overall participant ages 16–40, which includes adults within 18–65), and healthy-group results are reported separately from the clinical group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only reporting, non-empirical paper, or only out-of-range ages) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind and empathy) in healthy adults (N=13; ages 19–36). The task is social-related (cartoon ToM/Empathy task) satisfying I3. Results are reported for a healthy adult group separately, satisfying I4. Analyses used whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM2 contrasts with group-level maps and tables of significant activation foci (z>3.09, cluster>10 voxels), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical).

This study uses task-based fMRI with a social cognition (Theory of Mind) task (MASC video adaptation), includes a healthy adult sample (n=18, ages 20–45), and reports group-level whole-brain GLM results (contrasts ToM vs PI) with thresholded statistical maps and coordinate tables. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results (behavioral, GLM, T-PICA) and Discussion, providing the necessary whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The study uses fMRI in a social-related face perception/attention task (meets I3). However, the sample consists of chronic traumatic brain injury (TBI) participants only (no separate healthy adult group reported), so it does not meet I4. Consequently it also fails I5 because the reported group-level whole-brain analyses pertain to the TBI sample rather than a healthy/control group. No exclusion criteria from the list are directly triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing required sample and healthy-group whole-brain reporting criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From available information: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is clearly satisfied—the study used fMRI to examine learning about others' emotions. I4 (healthy adult sample) cannot be confirmed from the abstract (no ages or explicit statement that participants were 18–65 healthy adults). I5 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map) cannot be verified from the abstract—while the abstract mentions brain regions, it does not explicitly confirm whole-brain voxelwise group results. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on provided content. Because the full text (methods/results) is missing, key inclusion criteria cannot be verified; therefore I exclude the study pending full-text access.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 25.9) investigating perception of affective vocalisations from humans and other primates—a social communication / perception task. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME; species contrast human>chimpanzee>macaque) with statistical images, coordinates and a table of regions, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task results), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The study includes an fMRI social-related word-processing task (I3) and includes healthy adult participants in the overall sample (I4). However, the fMRI analyses reported in this paper involve a patient-only fMRI subsample (N=25) and report correlations and ROI (amygdala) results for patients; the manuscript does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group/interaction results or patient-focused maps without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: participants performed a social judgment task (dominance/trustworthiness judgments) during fMRI, satisfying I3. Sample consists of 23 healthy adults aged 21–43 with results reported for the healthy group, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment) with cluster tables and peak coordinates and statistical thresholds, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results (whole-brain tables/figures), and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an event-related fMRI study of facial emotion processing (a social cognition task). The paper reports data from a healthy adult control group (n=9; ages within 18–65) separately from the Asperger group. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and statistical contrasts for the control group are reported (figures, tables, and detailed methods for whole-brain permutation-based voxel- and cluster-wise analysis). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, out-of-range participants, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study is excluded because it does not include any healthy adult control group and therefore fails key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — facial emotion/gender discrimination). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy adult participants reported), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task activation map reported for a healthy/control group). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only clinical group within- and between-treatment contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Additionally, the provided full text appears incomplete (abstract/metadata only).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata available). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI used with a social communication task). Inclusion criteria not confirmed: I4 (participant ages 18–65 not reported in the abstract), I5 (unable to verify that a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map from the healthy/control group is reported — abstract mentions activations but full methods/results and tables/coordinates are not available), I6 (cannot verify location/format of whole-brain results). Exclusion criteria met: none (E2-E6 not demonstrably applicable from the abstract alone). Because core article content (methods, full results, figures/tables) is missing, I exclude for now due to incomplete full text; full inclusion assessment requires the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (third-party punishment/mentalizing) in healthy adult participants (mean age 26) using task-based fMRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (Decision Phase: Experimental > Control; q(FDR)<0.05) and parametric cluster-corrected results, with activations listed and displayed; effective connectivity is additional but does not replace whole-brain task maps. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task results), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social referential task (Visual–Verbal Self-Other Referential Processing Task) examining self- vs other-related processing and affect—directly relevant to social-related processing. Sample comprises 20 healthy adult women aged 18–52 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked BOLD contrasts (figures, tables, MNI coordinates, voxel-wise thresholds and cluster reporting) for the healthy participant group. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Ultimatum Game) with clear social-processing constructs (strategic social decision-making), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult group (ages 19–28) reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (unfair–fair) with one-sample t-tests and full-factorial ANOVAs and shows thresholded statistical maps and tables (figures and Table 1), satisfying I5 and I6. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of healthy adult fMRI studies of social processing.

Exclusion E3 met: although the study collected fMRI during a social task (mothers viewing infants) and sampled healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 satisfied), the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked (voxelwise) activation maps for the healthy group. The reported fMRI analyses are resting-state/intrinsic connectivity (seed-based network correlations) and region-of-interest PET ([11C]raclopride) dopamine results. Thus it provides seed-based/resting-state connectivity and PET/ROI findings but no unmasked whole-brain task activation map (I5 not met). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3.

Excluded because the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map explicitly for the healthy/control group. Exclusion criterion met: E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: audiovisual speech/perception, social communication), I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages within 18–65), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures for main effects and interactions). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain healthy/control-only task-evoked statistical map is clearly reported; results are presented as combined-group congruency main effect and group×congruency interactions). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED for lacking the required healthy-group whole-brain activation map (E4).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (bystander effect) using task-evoked stimuli and reporting group-level whole-brain analyses. The sample is healthy adults (ages 18–27). The paper reports random-effects GLM whole-brain results with cluster-corrected statistical maps and tables of activations. Full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study investigating mirror-system responses to action observation and trained arbitrary shapes — a social-cognition relevant task (perception/understanding of others). Participants: 21 healthy adults (mean age 24), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (second analysis across whole brain at p<0.001 uncorrected) and provides peak coordinates/tables for effects. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI task of social gaze processing in a healthy adult sample (meets I3 and I4). However, all reported statistical results are ROI-based (amygdala and inferior occipital gyrus) with FWE correction within ROIs, and the paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate tables/figures for the healthy group. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting) and does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the manuscript presents ROI-based MVPA and ROI-localizer procedures without reporting any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group in the main text or supplementary material provided here. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (emotion identification and attribution) in healthy adults, using task-based fMRI with 22 right-handed healthy participants aged 19–32. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts (e.g., How>Why, Why>How) with tables of coordinates and thresholding details, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (perception of biological motion) in healthy adult participants (age range 18–39), and it reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (corrected cluster-wise results) showing a significant cluster in right pSTS associated with social-network diversity. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion enabling assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception/mentalizing in healthy adults: participants (undergraduate adults, mean age 20) performed social-related tasks (inferring food preferences; categorical age judgments) while whole-brain fMRI was acquired. The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with contrasts, Talairach coordinates, cluster sizes, tables and figures (task and social-group main effects and simple effects). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (linking person perception and person knowledge) in healthy adults. Sample: 21 healthy adult participants (age mean 24.6, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical contrasts (main effects and interactions) with voxelwise thresholds and tables, and describes whole-brain univariate and connectivity (PPI) analyses. Whole-brain results are clearly reported and masked by functional localisers; coordinates and cluster-level corrections are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: participants read personal narratives and judged protagonists’ values (social cognition, understanding others). Sample consists of healthy adults (N=78 across three cultural groups; ages in 20s, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., stories vs rest, protected-value vs non-protected stories) with cluster correction and whole-brain GLM analyses; results are presented in text, figures, and supplementary material. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, empirical, healthy adult sample).

This record is a non-empirical review article (labelled 'Review' and described in the abstract) and does not report original fMRI data from healthy adult participants. It therefore does not meet I3 (no original fMRI task data), I4 (no reported healthy adult sample results), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task activation maps), nor I6. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical papers without original fMRI data) applies. Additionally, the provided full text is limited to abstract/metadata (no methods/results), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=37, ages within 18–65) using an explicit social communication/addressment task (participants judged whether they felt addressed). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (main effects and interactions) with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an fMRI task study of supramodal emotional (social) processing in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–34). The task probes social communication / perception of others (facial and vocal emotion integration). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (conjunctions, contrasts), with thresholding, figures, and tables of activations (whole-brain voxelwise maps and coordinate tables). Healthy adult sample is reported separately. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text appears incomplete (HTML body empty); core article content (methods, participants, results) is not available. Cannot verify inclusion criteria: I3 (use of functional MRI during a social-related task) not confirmed; I4 (presence and separate reporting of a healthy adult group 18–65) not confirmed; I5 (reporting of at least one group-level, whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked map) not confirmed; I6 (whole-brain results available in tables/figures/supplement) not confirmed. No exclusion criteria are demonstrably met from the available content. Exclusion applied because full text is incomplete and inclusion criteria cannot be assessed.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating self/other social-cognitive processing during episodic recollection. Sample: healthy adult participants (N=18; ages 19–29), meeting the age and health requirements. Methods report task-based fMRI with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM8 and normalization to MNI space; results include whole-brain activations reported with FWE-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures (i.e., group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts from the healthy group). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using Human Connectome Project data (n=787 healthy adults, ages within 22–>35) that includes a social-processing task contrast (TOM vs Random). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-activation maps (Cohen's d maps and level-3 z maps), with figures and tables describing voxelwise cerebellar and whole-brain activations. Thus it meets I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps from the healthy group), and I6 (maps and results clearly reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text is complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (decisions about sharing/selecting news, involving mentalizing and social-cognition processes) and reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (select>content, share>content, share>select) for a healthy adult sample (N=41, ages 18–24). Whole-brain results are explicitly reported (tables/figures) and meet the meta-analysis requirements; full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction perception (point-light and shape-animate stimuli) in healthy adult participants (N=14, ages 20–32), meeting the review population. It includes group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (e.g., interaction > independent; animate > physical) with reported peak MNI coordinates and group maps/figures, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (functional MRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and the paper is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study using social tasks (take advice game; trust game) examining neural representations of honesty and trust. Sample: 31 healthy adult participants (mean age ~24, right-handed, no neurological/psychiatric history), satisfying the healthy adult (18–65) criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results: univariate whole-brain contrasts (voxel-level and cluster-level FWE-corrected results), MVPA searchlight analyses across the whole brain, and tables/figures with reported coordinates and statistical maps. These whole-brain results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not resting-state/seed-only; not between-group-only contrasts; participants within age range; empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study does not meet the review’s key content requirement (I3). Although it uses fMRI and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (I5) and includes healthy adult participants with at least one group wholly within the 18–65 range (I4) and reports whole-brain results in figures/coordinates (I6), the experimental task is a speech repetition/word-imitation paradigm focused on motor and memory processes rather than social-cognitive or social-communication processing per se.
