While the authors discuss vocal imitation’s relevance to social communication, the task itself does not probe social-affiliation, social interaction, perception/understanding of others or other social-related constructs targeted by the review. Therefore I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related auditory processing (listening to one vs two walkers) in healthy adults. Sample: 12 healthy volunteers aged 22–37, meeting the adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and multiple voxelwise contrasts (e.g., STEP1+STEP2 – REST; STEP2 – NOISE2; STEP1 – NOISE1) with statistical maps and reported Talairach coordinates (tables and figures), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of communicative speech (a social communication task) in healthy adult native Japanese speakers (n=27–30 analyzed; ages 19–31), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM random-effects ANOVA), with voxelwise statistical maps and tables of peak coordinates and figures illustrating activations (e.g., main effects and interactions). The task explicitly probes social communication and theory-of-mind/action-simulation networks (affiliation/communication/perception of others). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, tasks, acquisition, preprocessing, analysis), Results (behavioral and imaging with tables/figures), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is included for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Reading the Mind in the Eyes task, a social-perception/mental-state decoding task (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–27 from two cultural groups, reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., RME − GD), with tables and figures of significant activations and corrections (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-affective task (SoVT film clips depicting people in distress; constructs include affiliation/compassion and perception/understanding of others). (I4) The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 45–62 (within 18–65). (I5) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative, Reappraisal > Watch-Negative, Compassion > Reappraisal) with cluster-level FWE correction and detailed whole-brain results. (I6) Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Thus the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group, but the provided full text does not clearly present a group-level whole-brain task activation map specifically for the healthy/control group. The authors report whole-brain analyses (main effects across groups, group × condition interactions, and a main effect of group) and describe post hoc within-group peak-voxel comparisons for HCs, but do not explicitly provide or label an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map or its coordinates in the main text. Supplementary t-contrasts are referenced but their content is not included here, so we cannot verify an HC whole-brain map. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group/interaction effects reported without a clear healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social task) and I4 (healthy adult participants). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete (core article present).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social attribution (theory of mind/understanding others) in healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 21–46). The methods describe a task manipulating social vs. nonsocial attributions, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, ROI and whole-brain group-level analyses (conjunctions and cluster-corrected maps), and reported whole-brain results (tables/figures). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an fMRI study that directly examines social cognitive processing (social working memory) and manipulates social load, satisfying the social-task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (N=16; mean age 20), meeting the sample inclusion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise threshold and cluster-size correction described; coordinates and figures/tables S2–S3 reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study using a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain results described in section 3.4.2 with thresholding and FWE correction) and presents activation maps and ROI analyses. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/figures). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Included for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: subjects learned moral/social status (cooperator, defector, neutral) via interactive Prisoner’s Dilemma and were scanned during face presentations, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (scanned sample: 11 right-handed adults, mean age 25.6, range 21–36; behavioral sample described separately), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects across the healthy scanned group) with coordinates and statistical maps/tables (p-values, peaks, ROI and whole-brain results), fulfilling whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of patients with early-course schizophrenia randomized to cognitive enhancement therapy (CET) vs enriched supportive therapy (EST), using the POP cognitive control task (non-social) and reporting treatment×time effects between patient groups. It does not include any healthy adult (18–65) participant group, nor does it report whole-brain task-evoked maps from a healthy/control group. No social-related fMRI task is used (social cognition was measured behaviorally), so it fails the review's inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI social-related task), I4 (no healthy adult group reported), I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions among patient groups without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based stimuli depicting own vs other child and inappropriate vs neutral child behaviors (social/attachment-related processing), with methods, results, and discussion present in the full text. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social-related constructs: attachment/understanding of others), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported using random-effects models and voxel-by-voxel tests), I4 (sample consists of adult mothers scanned as a group; mothers’ ages are treated as covariates, consistent with adult participants in the 18–65 range), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI analyses, connectivity/resting-state only analyses, between-group-only contrasts without a healthy-group task effect, or non-empirical data. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Confidence is slightly reduced because exact participant ages are not explicitly listed in the provided excerpt, but the study clearly involves adult mothers and reports group whole-brain task activations relevant to social processing.

This is an fMRI study that investigates processing of emotional facial expressions (a social-related task), satisfying I3. It includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=9, mean age 27±7), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and describes/control-specific task-related activations (reports main effects, interactions, and plots mean FPQ for controls in figures/tables), providing whole-brain task-evoked results attributable to the healthy/control group, satisfying I5. Results are reported in tables and figures and described in the text, meeting I6. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or absent healthy-group whole-brain map) apply.

This fMRI study meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (participants imagined encountering neutral faces in goal-relevant vs. goal-irrelevant social situations), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adults aged 20–36 (n=17 analyzed), meeting I4. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (second-level random-effects ANOVAs, cluster-corrected thresholds) with coordinates, figures, and tables of activations (ventral striatum, VTA, STS, etc.), meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This article is a 'Personal View' (non-empirical review/commentary) summarizing mirror neuron research in autism and does not report original fMRI data from healthy adult participants. The provided content is only abstract/metadata (full text not available here). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task reported), I4 (no healthy adult sample results reported), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6. It meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Full text is incomplete in the provided materials, preventing verification of any omitted empirical data.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social crowd perception (social interaction and emotion in crowds), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 19–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (ANOVAs) with cluster-corrected results, tables of clusters/peak voxels, and figures—i.e., unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participant ages within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (Theory of Mind) using comic-strip intention conditions, includes a healthy adult control group (N=12, mean age 24.8) with results reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain analyses and coordinates/figures for the control group (second-level ANOVA, within-group contrasts, tables and figures). The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social visual processing (sensitivity to two-body face-to-face vs nonface-to-face configurations), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=20; mean age 24.1). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., dyads > single-bodies; facing > nonfacing dyads), with tables and figures of voxelwise results, and describes methods, results and discussion in full. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of social communication (processing of angry vocal prosody) in healthy adults (15 right-handed undergraduates, mean age 24.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts, MNI coordinates, t-values, and cluster-level inference (e.g., STS, amygdala, OFC, cuneus), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results for the healthy sample are reported separately and not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, imaging, statistical analysis), Results, and Discussion; therefore full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range participants) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about others' mental states) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight representational similarity and voxelwise repetition-suppression results) with corrected statistical maps (TFCE-corrected p<0.05) identified in medial prefrontal cortex and precuneus. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task modality, sample, and whole-brain reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=116 males, mean age 24.7) using an event-related emotional face recognition task—clearly a social-related processing paradigm. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts and regression results (coordinates and pFWE-corrected values are provided for contrasts such as FearHighPLC>baseline and FearPLC>NeutralPLC and OXT effects), clearly attributable to the healthy/control sample. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Abstract and metadata indicate an fMRI task examining perception of others' emotional facial expressions (a social processing task), with 14 healthy adult participants (mean age 29±6). The paper reports group-level statistical parametric mapping (SPM) results identifying dorsal medial frontal cortex activation, consistent with whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked findings. However, only the abstract/metadata were provided (full text content appears truncated), so I flag the full text as incomplete and assign moderate confidence. Full text is needed to verify details (e.g., that the reported SPM results are unmasked whole-brain group maps and to extract coordinates/tables if required).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social learning task (participants learned about others’ generosity) with healthy adult participants (median age 23.5, range 19–37; N=26 included in analyses). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and contrasts) with voxel-wise thresholds and whole-brain cluster correction; coordinates and tables of activations are provided. The task and contrasts clearly relate to social processing (learning about others), meeting the review objective. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within the 18–65 range, and this is an empirical paper with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates perception of others (identity and emotion) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (congenitally blind and sighted; mean ages within 18–65). It reports whole-brain voxelwise univariate analyses (main effects, interactions) and searchlight multivariate (MVPA) whole-brain results with cluster-level corrections and tables/figures of coordinates, and describes within-group patterns for sighted and blind participants. The study therefore meets the meta-analysis objective (social-related processing) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social perception), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (results reported as maps/coordinates/figures). Full text is complete. No exclusion criteria applied.
