This is an fMRI study of action observation and interaction representation (social perception of others’ actions), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: 29 healthy, right-handed adults aged 18–28, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Observation > Neutral; 2H DIFF > 2H SAME) with FWE correction, peak coordinates, and tables/figures—meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy group-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others’ actions; mentalizing vs mirror systems) in healthy adults. Methods report fMRI acquisition and whole-brain, second-level random-effects analyses with multiple-comparison correction; results include group-level whole-brain activation maps and tables of coordinates (Tables 1 and 2) and reported voxelwise effects. Sample: 12 healthy right-handed adult volunteers (mean age 27.3), within 18–65 range. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (visual perspective-taking) and includes a healthy adult control group with group-level results reported (meets I3 and I4). However, all activation analyses were conducted within a predefined combined region-of-interest mask and analyzed voxels were restricted to that mask rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met, and exclusion criterion E2 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 21–24) that investigates neural responses during tasks involving social context (peer observation) and decision making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (e.g., Go/No-Go and Stoplight contrasts) and provides thresholded/unthresholded maps via NeuroVault, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. The sample consists of a healthy adult cohort and task paradigms include a clear social manipulation (peer presence) relevant to social processing. The study also reports whole-brain connectivity and activation results (not ROI-only). Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task) meeting the social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (age-matched controls) reported separately from HD patients. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level models) and presents group contrasts and control-related effects (including comparisons within control subgroups and tables/figures of results), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment of social attribution (asking subjects to judge another’s awareness), meeting the review’s construct of social-related processing. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=50, ages 18–49) with the TMS subset reported separately; healthy-group results are reported. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (H trials − E trials) thresholded and corrected (P < 0.05, cluster correction) with Talairach coordinates and figures (Table 1, Fig. 3), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy age group only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not report a standalone, unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (exclusion E4). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — cyberball), I4 (healthy adult control group reported), and I6 (whole-brain results and contrasts are described in the text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map or within-group contrast for HC is presented; the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts and conjunctions involving HC). Full text appears complete; exclusion is based on missing healthy-group whole-brain effect required by I5/E4.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata available). From abstract, the study uses fMRI of emotional facial expression (a social communication task) in 12 healthy subjects, so I3 and I4 appear satisfied. However, I cannot verify whether the paper reports a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (I5) because the full article (methods/results/tables/figures) is not accessible. Unable to confirm whole-brain voxelwise reporting; therefore the review inclusion criterion I5 is not met based on available information. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively applied given incomplete text. Decision: EXCLUDED due to inability to confirm I5 and incomplete full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotional prosody comprehension, a social-cognitive task involving perception and understanding of others' emotions (social-related processing). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 18–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (emotional vs neutral; complex vs simple emotions) with cluster-level correction and tables/coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15 after exclusion; ages 19–42) that investigates perception of others (facial gender categorization), a social-related process (I3). The paper reports both ROI analyses and a whole-brain, voxel-wise random-effects group analysis (gender-different > gender-same) with reported clusters and coordinates (right collateral sulcus, left precuneus, right lateral occipital gyrus, right putamen), satisfying the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map (I5/I6). Participants are within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported separately (I4). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This study used fMRI with social/attachment stimuli (listening to attachment narratives) in healthy adult participants and reports seed-based whole-brain functional connectivity results, but it does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy group. Primary neuroimaging analyses focus on post-narrative resting-state seed-based FC (caudate nucleus) rather than task-evoked voxelwise activation contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based / resting-state connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with social/attachment task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I6 (results reported with coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=26, mean age 24.4), using a social-related task (perception of others' pain, agency, and empathy), satisfying the review focus on social processing. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects analyses, contrasts such as pain>no pain and social-context contrasts), reports thresholded results (FDR-corrected) and provides stereotactic coordinates in tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps/contrasts reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only sample, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full text appears incomplete in the provided content (only abstract/highlights/metadata present). From available information I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: dynamic facial expression perception) is clearly met. However the manuscript as provided does not report participant demographics or ages to confirm I4 (healthy adults aged 18–65), nor does it provide verifiable whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy group (I5). Because these key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete/fulltext provided, the study is excluded pending access to the full article. No formal exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly met based on the abstract alone.

The study does not use an fMRI task that probes social-related processing (I3 not met). The task is a continuous performance test with monetary reward (non-social cognitive/reward paradigm), although authors correlate reward-related activation with social symptom scores. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported for control group), I6 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study uses task fMRI of a social-related task (RMET) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map or coordinates clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; results primarily report between-group ANOVA and post-hoc contrasts and an ROI amygdala analysis. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met and exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) to relate intrinsic network topology to emotional intelligence rather than a task-based social processing paradigm, so it does not provide any whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy control group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (resting-state analyses only). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (study includes a healthy control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task) and I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked map from healthy participants). Full text appears incomplete in the provided content (only abstract/highlights/metadata), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes social-related task conditions (theory-of-mind / understanding others) presented as text and video, meeting the review’s construct scope. The sample consists of 45 healthy adult participants (ages 19–23) reported separately, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (fixed and random effects, strict conjunctions, multiple-comparison correction) and provides peak coordinates and whole-brain maps, meeting whole-brain evidence reporting standards. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is an empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendices).

The study reports an fMRI investigation of social influence during an interactive emotional-arousal rating task (social communication/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adult students (mean age ~24; n=20 scanned), satisfying the sample criterion. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (clusterwise FWE correction reported) with tables/figures of activations (insula, ventral striatum, amygdala), satisfying whole-brain evidence and coordinate reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, age-out-of-range, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Trust Game) probing reciprocity and perspective-taking—clearly within ‘social-related processing’. Participants are healthy adults (ages 18–22) and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical contrasts (e.g., defect > reciprocate; regression analyses) with coordinates, cluster correction procedures, and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are presented in text, figures and tables. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=60, ages 18–60) using a social-related task (observation of mouth actions/oral communicative actions by humans and other species), reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and between-/within-group results (SPM8 random-effects analyses, coordinates, figures, p<0.05 FWE). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in the text. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, absence of healthy-group whole-brain task maps) apply. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and references; fulltext appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not use an fMRI task probing social-related processing (I3 not met). The tasks are verbal executive/inhibition paradigms (verbal fluency and Hayling sentence completion), not social cognition/affiliation/communication or perception of self/others. The paper does include healthy adult control participants (I4 met) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy/control group in the text and figures (I5 and I6 met). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of self/other trait judgments (social cognition), conducted in healthy adult participants (13 included, ages 19.4–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation contrasts (e.g., self>syllables; old/same>new) with SPM maps and coordinate tables and describes methods, results, and discussion in full. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates and figures clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, nor non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment explicitly probing social conceptual processing (social concept meaning relatedness judgments). Participants were healthy adults (n=26, mean age 29.4, range within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., social vs. animal; whole-brain analyses with voxelwise thresholds and reported peak coordinates and Table 1) and parametric regression/conjunction analyses; results for the healthy group are clearly presented. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (stereotype/social-category judgments) versus non-social semantic judgments. Participants are healthy adults (N=19, ages 19–28), satisfying the sample age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., 'social > non-social' and 'non-social > social') with figures and tables of peak voxels and cluster extents (P < 0.05, corrected), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=27, mean age 27) using a social-related task (viewing others' facial expressions; perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task contrasts (e.g., canonical disgust vs neutral; canonical disgust vs distaste) with voxelwise results, cluster coordinates and tables, and FDR-corrected activations. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, participants are within 18–65). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception), satisfying the review’s social-related processing focus. Participants were healthy adults (ages 18–32); results for the healthy group are reported. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise contrasts and lists coordinates and clusters for multiple contrasts (e.g., faces associated with behaviors vs novel faces; disgusting vs aggressive), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are presented in tables of coordinates and described in the text. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are met.

The paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial decisions) in healthy adult participants (N=32 females, mean age 22.7), satisfying the sample criterion. It includes group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects second-level contrasts, cluster-level correction, reported coordinates and tables/ROIs), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (N=32, ages 18–39) using a social task manipulating collaboration and competition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM with clusterwise FWE correction) and presents activation results (e.g., ventral basal ganglia, TPJ, mPFC) and VBM structural results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; reports healthy-group whole-brain effects). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial emotion recognition (a social-related task) with both adults with Asperger syndrome and a separately reported healthy adult control group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses, including within-group whole-brain results for the healthy/control group (NT controls: significant clusters for NTOXT>PLA reported in the whole-brain analysis and Table 2). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (real-world speed-dating) probing responses to romantic interest and rejection, which falls under social-related processing (affiliation/attachment, social communication, understanding others). The scanned sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 19–31 (N=38) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8; thresholds and cluster-correction reported) and provides tables of coordinates and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and should be included in the review.

This study meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social processing: empathy for pain paradigm) and I4 (healthy adult sample, males 18–40). However, the paper as presented reports whole-brain results only for between-group contrasts (STRESS > CONTROL and conjunctions) and ROI analyses; I cannot find a clearly reported unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map identified as coming from a healthy/control group (within-group or all-participants main effect) in the provided full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and falls under exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. Exclusion IDs met: E4.

This fMRI study investigates mirror-system responses during observation and execution of hand and foot actions, a form of social-related processing (perception and understanding of others) relevant to the review. Sample: healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 20–34), satisfying the age and health requirements. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (conjunction analyses and contrasts thresholded at P<0.05 corrected across whole brain; activations reported in Table 1 and figures), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided in the supplied text. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI task of naturalistic mentalising (social-related processing) with detailed methods and results. It includes a healthy adult control group (age range 19–46) reported separately. The paper presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (ToM vs physical inference) and reports significant activations for the control group with tables/figures (whole-brain, cluster-corrected results and coordinate tables). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6).

Full text is not accessible (only metadata/abstract available). Cannot verify whether the study used fMRI during a social-related task, included a healthy adult group reported separately, or reported whole-brain task-evoked results. Therefore I cannot confirm any inclusion criteria. Per instructions, mark fulltext_incomplete=true and exclude due to insufficient information to verify eligibility.

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotional speech prosody (a social-communication task), conducted in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 24.8). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task results (emotional > neutral prosody) with cluster-corrected findings and a table of results, in addition to ROI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and tabulated). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (dynamic facial expressions) in healthy adults (ages ~22), and reports group-level activation coordinates and ROI/SVC results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). However, the paper’s analyses and reported significant effects are based on ROI/small-volume-corrected tests (methods and Results repeatedly state ROI analyses and SVC), and no unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map is clearly reported. Therefore criterion I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results) is not satisfied, and Exclusion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (why/how mentalizing; default-mode/mentalizing network) using a task contrast targeting understanding of others' actions. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages reported, mean ~25.7, range 21–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (conjunctions, main effects) with cluster thresholds, tables of regions/coordinates and figures. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported via tables/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This paper reports task-based fMRI experiments in healthy adult participants (ages 18–27) using social cognitive tasks (mentalizing about groups and individuals), includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., member mental > member physical; group mental > group physical) with voxelwise thresholds and tables of activation, and reports univariate and multivariate searchlight results. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI investigation of reciprocity using a social interactive task (modified Trust Game) in healthy adults (ages 18–30; N=19 included in imaging analyses). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise analyses (GLM contrasts, one-sample/t-tests) with reported brain regions, contrasts, tables (Table 3) and figures (Fig. 2) including MNI coordinates and cluster-thresholding details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review (fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, whole-brain group-level task maps reported, acceptable reporting format). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: it manipulates social context (social vs unsocial faces) and goal-directedness of gaze shifts and measures neural responses. Healthy adult participants are reported (fMRI sample: N=12, ages 18–40). Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed using SPM2 and multiple whole-brain contrasts are reported (e.g., gaze-shift vs no-movement; incorrect vs correct; social vs unsocial), with thresholding and tables/figures of activated loci described. Thus the paper meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mental state attribution/intentional stance) manipulating belief that music was composed by a human vs computer, meeting the review objective. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=12 analyzed; ages 21–31) satisfying age and healthy-group requirements. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts are reported (Composer > Computer), with voxelwise statistics, cluster-correction thresholds, and stereotaxic coordinates presented in tables and figures. Results are clearly reported for the healthy/control group. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an fMRI experiment manipulating social competition (a social-cognition task: social comparison/mentalizing). The sample is healthy adults (female, aged 18–35; N=20 analyzed). The authors conducted whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (contrasts such as Competition > No Competition) with cluster-level correction and report peak coordinates and figures/tables, and link neural results to behavior. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E6). Full text appears complete.

The paper reports task-based fMRI of dynamic audio-visual emotion perception (a social cognitive task: perception/understanding of others), includes healthy adult participants (Study 1: n=10, ages 18–33; Study 2: n=5, ages 18–23), and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses and coordinates (multiple whole-brain contrasts, conjunctions, and tables/figures described). Results are reported for the healthy participant groups (Study 1 uses random-effects group analysis; Study 2 uses fixed-effects and still reports group-level maps). Whole-brain maps and coordinate tables are provided and clearly attributed to the healthy/control group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of social perception using a task where healthy adults rated naturalness of dyadic nonverbal interactions (social communication). Sample: 21 healthy adults aged 23–33. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (flexible factorial, contrasts, cluster-corrected results with coordinates/tables). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=7, ages 20–35), meeting the sample requirement (I4). Although the task is sentence reading, the analyses explicitly probe social-related content: a prominent factor labeled “people and social interactions” (correlating with NPSFs such as person, communication, social norms) and associated voxel clusters are reported (Figure 4A, Supporting Table S3), indicating the study examines perception/understanding of others/social interaction content and therefore meets the social-task criterion (I3). The paper reports group-level voxelwise results and brain voxel clusters derived from factor analysis across participants (whole-brain factor-related clusters and maps), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5); these results are reported in figures and supplementary tables (I6 acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-cognitive task addressing 'Perception and Understanding of Self'), performed in healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 26.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects; cluster Z>2.3, corrected p=0.05) with coordinates and figures (tables of MNI coordinates provided). Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses and healthy-group whole-brain task contrasts (self>other and other>self, plus self-rest and other-rest) are clearly reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI comparing social vs. non-social image appraisal in healthy adults (ages 23–50). It uses a social-related task (valence appraisal of social stimuli), includes a healthy adult sample, and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (social > non-social contrast) with cluster-level thresholds and tables/figures. The full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes appropriate age range, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 (and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures consistent with I6).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (male participants aged 18–35) that uses a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) probing social-related processing (responses to an ostensible opponent). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., high > low provocation) with voxelwise analyses and cluster-level FWE correction; coordinates and whole-brain results are provided in tables and figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study used fMRI during a clearly social task (charades) involving gestural communication between healthy adult participants (mean age 27.5; final N=18) and reports group-level, whole-brain statistical maps derived from between-brain Granger-causality mapping (bbGCM) and GLM-based analyses. The bbGCM results are presented as group-level differential G-causality maps thresholded for multiple comparisons, and the paper explicitly describes group analyses and whole-brain thresholding procedures. Participants are healthy adults within the required age range. Reporting of whole-brain maps and methodological details satisfy the review’s reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain task map, clinical-only samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

This is an original fMRI study of impression updating (social cognition/perception of others) in healthy adults (N=21; ages 18–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and interactions (e.g., L2>F3, updating-by-condition ANOVA) with cluster-correction and peak coordinates in tables/figures. Analyses are task-evoked (not resting-state or connectivity-only) and results for the healthy control sample are reported directly. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social expectancy violations along warmth and competence), using a social task relevant to perception/understanding of others. Participants are healthy adults (undergraduates; mean age 20.4, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects; Talairach coordinates, cluster statistics, corrected thresholds) and tables/figures of results from the healthy participant group. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. Note: sample size is small (n=12 analyzed) but still within inclusion requirements.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that used task-based fMRI to probe perception/understanding of self vs others (own vs others' body parts), a social-related construct. Participants were healthy adults (ages consistent with inclusion). The paper reports group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., body minus objects localizer; localization of EBA, LOC, V1/2) with Talairach coordinates and voxel counts and describes whole-brain thresholding, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain group results (reported in text/tables/figures). Analyses are not limited to ROI-only reporting. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examines pain empathy (a social-related process: perception/understanding of others and self) using task-based fMRI in a sample that includes a healthy control group (n=21; age inclusion 18–60). The paper reports ROI analyses and secondary whole-brain within-group and between-group task contrasts (e.g., controls: Self>Other activation in posterior cingulate/precuneus; Other>Self maps for patients; Supplementary Table S1 and figures), satisfying the requirement for at least one healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines neural responses during a social-cognitive task (perception and understanding of others / mentalizing) involving sexualized and clothed human targets, satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (heterosexual men, Mage ~21) reported separately, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain contrasts, voxelwise threshold p<.001, cluster correction via AlphaSim) and presents tables and figures of these results, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition and preprocessing), results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging), and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range age) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social-cognitive processing (impression formation of people vs objects) in healthy adults (N=14, ages 18.3–23.7). The task is explicitly social (forming impressions of persons) and imaging methods report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SPM99 analyses, voxelwise threshold P<0.001) with coordinates and tables of activations (e.g., dorsal mPFC peaks, Tables/Figures). The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social group processing in healthy adults (supports inclusion criteria I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample, mean age ~20.9). However, the paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group. Analyses are ROI/parcellation-based (visual field masks, category-selective ROIs, and averaged signals across 55 Harvard–Oxford regions) and the primary reported contrasts are within-group vs between-group intersubject-correlation differences. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task maps (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI/parcellation analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results) and E4 (reports between-group ISC differences without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (gambling for self, best friend, or an ‘antagonist’) in healthy adult participants (N=31; ages 18–26), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (repeated-measures ANOVAs) with results presented as tables of coordinates and figures (Tables 1–2; reported whole-brain contrasts and Person × Outcome interaction in the striatum and social brain regions), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used fMRI to probe face perception, explicitly manipulating gaze and expression (social communication), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates. However, the paper does not report participant ages; it only states "All eight observers had normal or corrected to normal visual acuity" and gives no ages or age range. Because inclusion criterion I4 requires at least one group of healthy adult participants aged 18–65 and this cannot be confirmed from the provided full text, the study fails to meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (masked fearful/happy eyes focusing on eye region) in healthy adults (male participants, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain results with coordinates and tables) in addition to ROI analyses, and healthy-group effects are clearly described (within placebo group and group-level contrasts). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates neural correlates of cooperation in one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma games (a social/mentalizing task), conducted in healthy adults (final sample n=35, ages ~24.6). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., proself vs prosocial, cooperate vs defect) with cluster-size correction, tables/figures of activations and peak coordinates. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This article reports an empirical fMRI study using an action imitation/observation task (social-related processing: perception/understanding of others, biological motion and imitation). A healthy adult control group (N=16) is included and analyzed separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts (within-group effects for healthy subjects: imitation>nonimitative and animated>nonanimated), with peak Talairach coordinates and figures/tables (Table 2, figures, and supplemental materials). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants appear to be adults, and the paper is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (racial in-group/out-group facial emotion perception) using a task involving passive viewing of faces (social perception). Participants were healthy adults (final N=26, mean age ~21), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA, whole-brain contrasts, corrected thresholds) with reported activation clusters/tables and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Although PPI connectivity analyses are also presented, they supplement rather than replace whole-brain task activation results. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text.

This paper reports an fMRI study using an interactive social task (virtual handshake) that probes social rejection (meets social-related task construct). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=16; mean age 27.4, within 18–65) and reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the control group (refusal vs acceptance) with thresholding and cluster reporting (right pSTS and right thalamus). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. The study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of healthy adult social-related fMRI activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social persuasion (celebrity ‘expert power’) examining perception/understanding of others and attitude formation—clearly a social-related task. Participants were healthy adult females (mean age 21.8), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects whole-brain results, cluster correction, tables/figures of activations) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma), uses a healthy adult sample (n=30, mean age 21.2), and reports group-level whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses and exploratory whole-brain correlations with coordinate/cluster results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind: cooperation, deception) in healthy adults. Participants: 13 healthy adults aged 22–38 (within 18–65). The task is social-related (ToM cartoons probing intentions/beliefs). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (second-level random-effects SPM analyses), with reported statistical maps, contrasts, thresholding, and peak coordinates/tables and figures. Results for the healthy group are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study using a social-perception task (viewing point-light and human-like walkers; participants judged facing-towards vs away), directly addressing social-related processing. Sample: 16 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.75), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task analyses with stereotactic coordinates and thresholding (FWE-corrected results, Table 1 and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements; results are presented as contrasts and discussed. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI of a social-related task (socio-emotional preference ‘‘Do I like this person?’’) in healthy adults (ages 23–51, N=21). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (Preference > Gender and other contrasts) with thresholding (p<0.05 FDR), tables of activation peak coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20, age range 23–39) that used task-based fMRI while participants made social judgments (social coordination of ambiguous interactions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and t-tests) with FDR-corrected results, statistical maps (figures) and tables of coordinates for task-evoked activations in somatosensory cortex, IFG, hippocampus, amygdala, etc. Behavioral and imaging results are reported for the healthy/control group. All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E2 – the reported group-level voxelwise results are presented and corrected using a small-volume (ACC) mask (SVC), i.e., effectively ROI-restricted results rather than unmasked whole-brain maps. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is an fMRI social-related task probing processing of others' decisions), I4 (healthy adult sample, n=12, ages within 18–65), I6 (results reported with coordinates and PSTHs). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 – the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group; statistical inference was restricted/corrected within an ACC anatomical mask. Therefore it meets the ROI-only exclusion and fails the whole-brain map requirement.

The study is a resting-state fMRI investigation comparing ASD (with/without ADHD) and typically developing (TD) participants; it does not use a social-related task fMRI paradigm and does not report any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for a healthy adult group. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria: I3 (no task-based social fMRI), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group map), and I4 (no clearly reported healthy adult subgroup aged 18–65 — the sample is mixed-age from ABIDE II and no separate healthy adult task results are provided). It meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only resting-state analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses task fMRI of a social-related process (vocal emotion recognition) and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and figures/tables. However, the sample consists of children and adolescents aged 8–19 with no separately analyzed healthy adult (18–65) group. Inclusion criterion I4 (at least one group of healthy adults age 18–65) is not met, so the study does not fit the meta-analysis target population. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Exclusion E2 applies: the fMRI results are reported using ROI-based analyses (beta extractions from predefined anatomical ROIs) rather than reporting any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task — social closeness task with friends vs unfamiliar faces) and I4 (sample includes healthy adult participants aged 19–30 alongside adolescents). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group is reported). Full text appears complete.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (trustworthiness judgments) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses (mean percent signal change from a priori ROIs) and statistical tests on those ROIs; it does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or tables of whole-brain coordinates for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task effects (I5 not met). Exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect accompanying group contrasts) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social communication task (gaze following vs finger pointing) in healthy adult participants (n=17, age 20–34). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (task vs baseline and condition subtractions) with statistical thresholds and cluster criteria, and provides coordinates and activation figures. The task assesses social attention/communication, meeting the meta-analysis construct. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and the manuscript contains full Methods, Results, and Discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of self-face recognition (Perception and Understanding of Self), a social-related process. Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM results) with reported coordinates and cluster-level correction for contrasts such as Morph 50% recognized as self vs friend, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy age groups, non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study investigates attributional style (a social-cognitive task involving inference about others’ emotional behaviors) using a task-based fMRI paradigm, satisfying the social-processing requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (n=16) and compares their task performance and brain responses to patients, satisfying the sample requirement. The paper reports group-level voxelwise results: regions and coordinates are described (Table 1) and the text explicitly states significant % signal changes for the control group (within-group contrasts: experimental > control condition), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; reporting of coordinates/tables meets I6. The study is empirical, not ROI-only or resting-state, and presents task-evoked activation maps for the healthy group. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (judgments of a self-conscious social emotion, pride, contrasted with joy), meeting the review topic. Inclusion criteria met: I3 — task involves social cognition/Perception and Understanding of Self/Others (pride judgment, ToM-related processes); I4 — sample comprises healthy adult participants (16 healthy university students, mean age ~21); I5 — reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (P−N, J−N, P−J) with random-effects analysis and tables of peak coordinates; I6 — whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, age outside range, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, tables, figures, references).

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation of theory-of-mind/social cognition (social vs non-social stories) in healthy adults (N=24, mean age 25.7). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise P<0.001, cluster-wise FWE-corrected) with tables/coordinates and ROI and MVPA results. All core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group results.

The study is an fMRI investigation of social processing (emotional face recognition of one’s own vs. unfamiliar child), satisfying the social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (mothers without early life maltreatment) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps/contrasts for the control group (e.g., CON mothers showed a significant own>unknown familiarity effect in the medial frontal gyrus with whole-brain FWE-corrected coordinates and statistics), and whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study using social-emotional stimuli (angry and happy faces) during an explicit task (gender identification), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample is 30 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.2), within the 18–65 range and reported separately, satisfying the sample criterion. The authors performed whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (random-effects full factorial ANOVA) and report FWE-corrected whole-brain results and contrasts (with tables/figures and ROI supplements), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only metadata/abstract provided). The abstract confirms fMRI during a social decision task affecting interaction partners, so I3 is satisfied. However the paper does not state participant ages or report group-level whole-brain task activation maps in the provided text. The abstract emphasizes functional connectivity between regions, suggesting connectivity-focused analyses but does not confirm unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Because I4 and I5 cannot be verified from the supplied content, the study is excluded pending full-text verification. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied from the abstract alone.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (emotional face perception; incidental gender task), satisfying I3. Sample comprises 30 healthy adult volunteers (screened for psychiatric disorders), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (e.g., main effects and contrasts, whole-brain comparisons, coordinate tables and figures), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions), meeting I3. The sample consists of 24 healthy adult participants (mean age 26), meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with FWE-corrected results and coordinates (conjunctions, contrasts, whole-brain maps), meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and figures/tables; it appears complete (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 23.6) that used a social-related task (viewing dynamic two-person violent interactions; perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts with statistical activation maps and coordinates (figures and supplementary tables) and describes voxelwise analyses and cluster correction. Results for the healthy participant group are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (pupillary signaling) in healthy adults, meeting the review objective. It uses functional MRI during an implicit social-related task (monitoring others’ pupil changes) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates, thresholds, tables and figures for main effects and interactions. The sample comprises 14 healthy adult participants (mean age 22) within the 18–65 range and reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). The paper is empirical and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical approaches. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating facial recognition (a social-perception task falling under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’). Participants were healthy adults (N=18; ages 19–36), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (contrasts of false recognition vs. recognition/correct rejection) with cluster correction and provides Talairach coordinates and figures, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are presented for the healthy group. Although ROI analyses are also reported, whole-brain results are clearly available, so E2 (ROI-only) does not apply. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing: social reward via expert agreement) and I4 (reports a healthy adult control group, n=17, ages 18–60). However, it does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (within-group or main-effect map). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). inclusion_criteria_met: I3, I4. inclusion_criteria_not_met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain map).

This study used fMRI with a social (Theory of Mind/intentional causality) task (I3 met) and included a healthy adult control group (ages ~22.6) (I4 partially met as to sample). However, the paper does not report an unambiguous whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. Component maps were created from all participants combined (n=36) and the main reported results are between-group comparisons (ASD vs control) and ICA-derived networks; no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect is clearly presented. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social fMRI). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (results for healthy group not reported separately as required when clinical groups are included) and I5 (no clear healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports empirical fMRI experiments using dynamic facial emotion stimuli (a social-perception task), with healthy adult participants (mean ages ~25, N per experiment reported), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (dynamic > static, dynamic > baseline) with cluster correction and stereotaxic coordinates; it also includes ALE meta-analyses using published whole-brain coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group healthy whole-brain task effects; participants are within 18–65; empirical fMRI data are present). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (prediction of others’ behavior; ToM vs deontic reasoning) in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social-related and uses task-based fMRI), I4 (sample: 18 healthy adults, ages 18–44), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses with cluster correction and MNI coordinates), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described in text). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (explicit trustworthiness and attractiveness judgments) on vocal stimuli in healthy adults (N=44, ages 21–60). The paper provides complete methods, behavioral results, and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8; cluster-level FWE correction) with reported peak coordinates and conjunction analyses. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (24 analyzed; ages 19–31) that used a task involving social-related processing (recognition/familiarity judgment of personally familiar vs famous vs unfamiliar faces), directly addressing perception and understanding of others and social/attachment-related responses. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures of activation contrasts (e.g., P1–Cp1, P1–F1), fulfilling the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is original empirical work). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self/other understanding in romantic relationships), sample of healthy adults aged 23–40 (N=42) with exclusions applied, and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (SPM12 GLM, FWE-corrected contrasts, tables/figures). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (anticipatory active interpersonal touch) in healthy adults (N=16; ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts and cluster-corrected maps for the healthy sample (multiple contrasts and conjunctions are described and reported), and includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study reports only resting-state fMRI analyses and does not include any task-evoked, whole-brain healthy-group activation maps (exclusion criterion E3). Inclusion criteria met: none []. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI during a social-related task; MRI data are resting-state only), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group), and I4 (while a healthy volunteer group is included, participants span ages 12–24 and no separate healthy adult (18–65) subgroup results are reported). Only abstract and metadata are provided (full text incomplete). The abstract confirms this is an fMRI study of social communicative intentions, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI during social-related task) is met. This is an empirical fMRI study of perception/understanding of others' actions (mirror system) — a social-cognition construct — using fMRI during auditory action perception and motor pantomime. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects; participants are adults; is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-interaction task (face-to-face joint attention), includes healthy adult control groups (two NT groups, ages within 18–65) with results reported separately, and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps/contrasts for the healthy/control group(s) (e.g., RJA vs. SA within NT). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete for screening.

The study uses task-based fMRI of empathizing (social processing) and includes healthy control participants (including adults), but the full text reports mainly group-difference/age-interaction whole-brain results and extracted peak correlations rather than presenting an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants present and analyzed), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map for the healthy/control group is reported separately from between-group or interaction contrasts). This fMRI study uses a social-related task (effect of expert advice — social influence) during decision-making, satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45) alongside adolescents, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-level correction, reported voxel coordinates and statistical maps/contrasts) and provides coordinates and thresholding details, meeting I5 and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/rest, not only between-group contrasts without any whole-brain task effects, and include adults within the 18–65 range. This is an empirical fMRI study of affective speech comprehension that explicitly probes social-cognitive processes (mentalizing/Theory of Mind) during an emotional sentence-classification task, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 51 healthy adults (age range 18–53), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with FWE correction and provides coordinates and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements and should be included in the review.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during persuasion, a social-cognition/social-processing task (mentalizing/perspective taking). Participants are healthy adults (American and Korean samples; ages reported in range 20–22 and 20–27, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (persuasive > unpersuasive) with coordinate tables and conjunction/whole-brain analyses (thresholding and MNI coordinates provided). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating theory-of-mind and emotion/pain judgments (social-related processing). It uses task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants (n=46 females, age 18–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests, cluster inference using SnPM) with whole-brain maps and tables/figures illustrating task contrasts (e.g., B>Ph, E>Ph, Pa>Ph) clearly coming from the healthy participant group. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task fMRI of social processes), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social cognition (intention understanding from cooperative vs. affective interactions) while participants viewed social scenes. Participants: 27 healthy adult subjects (ages mean ~25, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise statistical maps (FWE-corrected results, conjunctions, whole-brain contrasts) and tables/figures of activation coordinates; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are clearly presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during emotion processing, a social-related construct) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, the full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The paper reports a main effect across all subjects and between-group contrasts (siblings vs. controls) and ROI analyses, but no standalone whole-brain healthy-group task map or coordinates/figure clearly labeled as the healthy group alone. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies: the study reports between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect. Inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=15, mean age 26.6) that uses task-based fMRI to investigate animacy perception/social cognition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric modulations and contrasts) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds, tables of coordinates, figures, and detailed methods and results. The task probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others/animacy). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (male college students, ages ~20–22) that used a task manipulating social context (rival-fan perspective) to probe memory retrieval and social-cognitive processes (self-referential processing, mentalizing). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric and categorical contrasts) with tables and figures of activation and SPM-based thresholds. Full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition and analysis), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy/emotional perspective-taking (a social-related task: perception/understanding of self and others) using task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=26, mean ages ~24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation results (thresholded SPMs, tables of coordinates, figures) for both within-group effects and contrasts; these are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control sample. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures descriptions, references) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an fMRI experiment of self-referential processing and perspective taking (social-related constructs) in healthy adults, reporting activation in medial prefrontal cortex subregions for task contrasts. This satisfies I3 (fMRI social task) and I4 (healthy adult participants). The abstract reports group-level activations (contrasts/interactions) localized to MPFC regions, consistent with whole-brain voxelwise results, meeting I5 and I6. However, the provided content appears to be an abstract/summary rather than the full article (methods/results sections not fully present), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true; confirmation of whole-brain analysis details in the full text would raise confidence. No exclusion criteria are met.

The paper reports an empirical 3T fMRI task study investigating attachment-related processing (social-affiliation/attachment) in healthy adults. Sample: 51 healthy right-handed adults (mean age 28.5), within 18–65. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., masked sad vs neutral faces) with coordinates and cluster statistics for a priori ROIs and whole-brain results, and describes group-level effects for the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study (two experiments) investigating perception/interpretation of social actions (social-related processing: perception/understanding of others). Samples are healthy adults within the 18–65 range (Experiment 1: N=20, ages 20–30; Experiment 2: N=20, ages 19–32), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise searchlight RSA results with voxelwise thresholding (p=0.001) and cluster-level correction (p=0.05), and provides cluster coordinates/tables (fulfilling I5 and acceptable reporting per I6). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates perception of others' emotions from voice (a social communication task), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes 22 healthy adults (ages 19–36), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task activation maps for the voice localizer contrast ([vocal > non-vocal]) used to define the TVA (cluster-level corrected whole-brain results and coordinates are provided), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results and peak coordinates for the main experiment are also reported. Reporting in text/figures and coordinates meets acceptable presentation standards. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (dyadic fMRI during face-to-face eye contact) in healthy adults (19 pairs; ages 18–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (ΩA, ΩB, Ω+, Ω-) derived from GLM and paired t-tests, provides cluster coordinates, atlas labels, and figures/tables of activations, and includes ICA projections onto these maps. Therefore it meets: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/atlas labeling provided).
