No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This study uses fMRI during an implicit emotional face discrimination task (social communication/perception), includes a healthy adult control group (n=19; ages 18–51), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (contrasts and reported activations for control subjects, e.g., fearful faces) rather than only ROI analyses. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Study uses task-based fMRI to probe social processes (empathy/sympathy) using validated stimuli and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses. Sample includes healthy adult participants within 18–40 years (embedded in a 7–40 continuous sample), satisfying the requirement of at least one healthy adult group. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and contrasts (e.g., PCS–NPS, PCO–PCS) identified from the healthy participant sample, with coordinates and statistical thresholds provided. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are presented in full; full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (multiround trust game), addressing social processing (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=21; ages 18–47) with results reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and voxelwise analyses for the healthy control group (figures and whole-brain thresholds, cluster PFWE reported; I5). Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and supporting tables (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are provided. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self, other, reflected self evaluations) satisfying the review objective. It includes a healthy adult group (19 adults, ages 22–31) reported separately and screened. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (2×4×3 repeated-measures ANOVA with age group as between-subjects factor), corrected for multiple comparisons, and presents cluster results and maps; separate within-age-group analyses are referenced in the Supplementary Materials. Reporting of whole-brain results in main text/tables meets acceptable formats. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=23 after exclusions; ages 18–27) performing social-cognitive simulations of personally familiar people, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight RSA, whole-brain t tests, permutation-corrected maps) with figures and a table of peak voxels/cluster sizes, meeting whole-brain evidence reporting. Full-text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and data availability is described. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore I include the study for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigated socially-induced emotion regulation (Social-Reg) using a psychotherapist-delivered reappraisal task during task-based fMRI, addressing social-related processing (social cognition, attachment). Participants were healthy adults (female, ages 22–32). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction, includes tables/figures of activations, and compares to resting-state DMN; results are clearly from the healthy sample. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, age in range, empirical data present).

Study uses task-based fMRI with naturalistic socio-emotional film stimuli that probe social cognition/conflict processing (meets I3). Sample consists of healthy adults (25 fMRI datasets, mean age 26.29) (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (voxelwise z>2.3, P<0.05), conjunction analyses, and tables/figures of results (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=98, age 18–30) using an emotional face-matching task (social perception of others’ emotions). The paper reports group-level task-evoked activation analyses including an a priori ROI analysis and an exploratory unmasked whole-brain analysis (faces > ovals) with FDR correction, and provides whole-brain results in tables/figures and supplementary materials. It therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults, and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The paper reports an fMRI social task (perception of fearful faces), includes a healthy adult control group (N=13, age 25.6), and presents group-level, voxelwise task activation maps for the control group (within-group contrasts: main effect of faces vs scrambled baseline and linear contrasts), with coordinates and figures. Although the authors used small-volume corrections for a priori ROIs, they ran whole-brain GLM analyses (global threshold reported) and report unambiguous control-group activations. Thus it satisfies I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps for healthy/control group), and I6 (results reported as coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (fearful facial expressions) — satisfies I3. It includes a healthy adult control group reported separately — satisfies I4. However, the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group (the authors used controls to localize an amygdala seed but do not report an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect or coordinates/figures/tables of healthy-group activation); the primary reported results are PPI effective connectivity and between-group connectivity contrasts. Therefore it fails I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map) and meets exclusion criteria E3 (reports only effective/seed-based connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: allocentric social hierarchy and social alliance judgments (social-related tasks). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 24.2), and analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (second-level random-effects SPM2; coordinates, tables, and figures; p<0.05 FWE). The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not investigate social-related processing in healthy adults. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (participants outside 18–65 with no healthy adult subgroup reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the control group) and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (task is a non-social visual attention task, not a social-related task) and I4 (sample comprises boys/adolescents, not healthy adults 18–65). Full text appears complete and methods/results/discussion are provided, but failure to meet I3 and I4 and meeting E5 requires exclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using social/attachment stimuli (own-infant vs stranger-infant videos), satisfying the social-related processing domain. Participants were healthy adult mothers age 22–37 (final N=23), meeting the adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM contrasts (own infant > stranger infant) with figures/tables of activations and voxelwise analyses, and also provides ROI and functional connectivity results; whole-brain task-evoked maps are clearly presented. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-evoked fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=21 in the imaging experiment) during repeated retrieval of real-life social interactions (oral examination enacted by an actor), which qualifies as social-related processing (perception/understanding of self in social context). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation results (hippocampus, retrosplenial cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, etc.) with corrected statistics and reports these effects in the main text/tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, empirical fMRI data reported). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. No exclusions identified.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 20–31) using a social perceptual task (voice-face identity recognition) that probes perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (random-effects GLM) and presents task contrasts and peak coordinates from those analyses; results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain voxelwise modeling was performed and reported (with ROI-masked displays and peak coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I6 (results reported via figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related cognitive empathy task (I3 satisfied) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (n=24, ages 18–50) (I4 satisfied). However, the paper’s imaging results are reported as whole-brain between-group contrasts (control > schizophrenia and schizophrenia > control) and cluster differences; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or within-group main effect clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) is not met and exclusion criterion E4 (only reporting between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E4. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study includes a healthy adult control group (mean age ~28) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task activation results for the control group (one-sample t-tests; Table 2 and text). The task is social-related (imagining sentences about mother/father—affiliation/attachment and social cognition). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map), and I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables/text) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=98, mean age 20.7) that examines social cognition (self, friends, strangers) using task-evoked BOLD contrasts. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses and displays whole-brain maps and contrasts (e.g., self > Bush, friends > strangers) thresholded and described in the text. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample within 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social appraisal (preference judgments of faces) that includes a healthy adult control group and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the control subjects (within-group PREF>GENDER contrasts shown in figures/tables). The task targets social-related processing (appraisal of others), healthy adults (n=21) are analyzed separately, and whole-brain results for the healthy group are reported in text, tables and figures. Full article contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic investigator feedback) in healthy adult participants (men aged 21–39). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts (negative social feedback > positive social feedback) with corrected voxel- and cluster-level results, tables of activations, figures, and coordinates. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, participants, imaging acquisition/analysis), Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion.

This is a longitudinal fMRI study of compassion training using the Socio-affective Video Task (SoVT), a social-affective task probing responses to others’ distress (affiliation/compassion). Participants: healthy adult sample (N=94 females, ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and results (FWE-corrected whole-brain results and coordinate tables/SVC ROI results) for the healthy participants and contrasts (pre/post; compassion vs memory). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants aged 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study used fMRI in healthy adult participants during face perception/recognition tasks (social perception), so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the provided full text reports ROI-based MVPA and ROI/visual-field region regression analyses; it does not present or describe an unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or coordinates/figures clearly identified as a healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and there are no qualifying whole-brain results reported (I6 not met). This meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion IDs met: E2. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (and consequently I6).

The study includes a social-related fMRI task (facial expression discrimination) and reports a healthy adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group; reported task results are described mainly as between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls) and region-specific findings (left amygdala), without a clearly-identified whole-brain healthy-group task effect. This fails inclusion criterion I5. Therefore the study is excluded under exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses a social task (Cyberball) and includes a healthy adult group (adults, n=16), fulfilling I3 and I4. However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy adult group alone. The reported whole-brain results are for the combined sample (adolescents + adults) and the Condition×Age-group interaction, with adult-specific effects probed via small-volume correction and post-hoc tests rather than an adult-group whole-brain map. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group interaction/SVC/post-hoc adult effects without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain adult-group task map). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of healthy adult participants (n=16, ages 20–28) that investigates perception/understanding of self (distinguishing self- vs. other-related visual feedback), a construct within the review’s social-related processing domain. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Aa–As, Pa–Ps, interaction) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds and stereotactic coordinates. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates social perception (emotion recognition from dynamic avatars/gait) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age ~28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effect GLMs, multi-subject activity maps, Monte Carlo cluster correction) and displays whole-brain statistical maps and ROI analyses. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures) is present.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly probes social-related processing (mentalizing/social cognition and self-related processing) while participants read news articles and links neural activity to behavior. Participants are healthy adults aged 18–24 in two samples (n=41, n=39), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (see whole-brain search, Fig. S3 and Table S5; permutation and cluster-corrected maps) in addition to ROI analyses, and whole-brain results pertain to the healthy participant samples. Supplemental materials and main text include the whole-brain findings. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of joint attention (a social communication/process) in healthy adults (N=13, ages ~25), reporting whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (RJA−RJAc, IJA−IJAc, conjunctions, and contrasts) with FDR-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, tables, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (empathic judgments/ emotional egocentricity) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (fMRI Experiment 1 whole-brain analysis; fMRI Experiment 2 with SVC using independent localizer and complementary whole-brain checks) with coordinates and statistical contrasts clearly attributed to the healthy/control group. Sample consists of healthy adult (undergraduate) participants. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, empirical study).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (rapid fearful face processing), including a healthy adult control group and reporting control-group results. The paper reports within-group activation for the control group (e.g., right amygdala, pulvinar, superior colliculi, fusiform) and describes whole-brain analyses in the Supplementary materials (FLAME whole-brain analyses and Supplementary Table 1), satisfying the requirement for a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map for healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts without unmasked healthy-group effects, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This study examines self-referential processing (a social-cognitive construct) during a task-state fMRI paradigm, so I3 (social-related task) is satisfied. However, the paper’s main results are ROI-based and seed-based voxelwise functional connectivity maps derived from task-state time series rather than univariate, task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for the healthy/control group. The manuscript does not report a group-level, whole-brain task activation (main effect or within-group contrast) for controls, and the analyses are connectivity-focused. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based/connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Also, the report does not provide ages for participants, so I4 (healthy adults 18–65) cannot be confirmed and thus is not met. I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map for healthy group) is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (implicit and explicit theory-of-mind/belief processing) in healthy adults. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=22, mean age 24.4) within 18–65. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM for the explicit general-belief localizer (false-belief vs false-photograph) with a reported statistical threshold (q(FDR)<0.05) and Talairach peak coordinates and figure—i.e., a whole-brain task-evoked map for the healthy group. Although the implicit task analyses used ROIs, the explicit localizer provides the required whole-brain group map (reported in text/figure/tables), satisfying inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Core article sections (methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults: participants (N=18, ages 19–28) performed a task believing they received messages from a friend or a computer. The paper reports full methods, results, and discussion (full text present). Whole-brain group-level task effects are reported and thresholded (univariate SPMs, cluster-corrected) and are described in text/tables/figures (e.g., dmPFC, VOT clusters). Multivoxel analyses (searchlight MVPA and MVCA) and univariate contrasts are whole-brain analyses. Thus the study meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (explicit facial emotion identification), meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult group (n=22; ages within 18–65) with results reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy control group (one-sample t tests for the 'faces minus animals' contrast), with coordinates and figures described in the text and tables. Methods, results, and discussion are provided in full, and whole-brain results for the HC group are clearly presented (figures/tables and coordinate lists). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, healthy-group whole-brain maps are present, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates natural touch by another person (a social-related stimulus) in healthy adult participants (n=8, ages 22–39), so it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). However, the paper reports results derived from group ICA component maps and component time courses without reporting a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (e.g., GLM main effect or within-group voxelwise contrast). The analysis relies on ICA-derived spatial maps and temporal responses rather than standard voxelwise task activation maps; per exclusion criterion E3, studies that report only ICA/connectivity-style analyses without a whole-brain task activation map must be excluded. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded.

The provided full text is incomplete (HTML head/metadata and references only) and lacks core sections (introduction, methods, participants, results). Cannot verify inclusion criteria: I3 (cannot confirm fMRI task details or that a social-related task was used from methods), I4 (participant sample/healthy adults not reported), I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group activation maps or coordinates are present). Therefore the study cannot be confirmed eligible for the review. Full text incomplete prevents assessment of ROI vs whole-brain analyses, connectivity vs task activation, or age/sample details.

This is an fMRI study of self- and other-referential (social) processing and includes a healthy, age-matched control group; however, the manuscript reports mainly between-group contrasts and combined-group maps and ROI/connectivity analyses. It does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone (i.e., within-group TD whole-brain task maps are not reported in the full text). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an fMRI task of self-referential processing and perspective-taking, which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’ (social-related processing). It includes a healthy control (HC) group and reports within-group, whole-brain task activation for HC (e.g., left VMPFC/MOFC activation for self>other) with coordinates and statistical thresholds. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described in the text and tables. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy control group reported), I5 (whole-brain, group-level healthy-task effects reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures/tables acceptable). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply based on the provided full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20; ages 22–50) that used task-based whole-brain BOLD analyses to examine neural responses to romantic (affiliation/attachment-related) and sexual stimuli. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (e.g., romantic > neutral; sexual > neutral) with thresholding and cluster correction, and presents tables and figures of activation maps and between-/within-group contrasts. Thus it meets the review objective (social-related processing) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social/affiliation stimuli), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not limited to between-group contrasts without healthy-group maps, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22) that used a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) during fMRI, satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., CC vs CD; OT/AVP vs PL contrasts) with cluster-corrected thresholds and figures/tables of activations, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (whole-brain analyses are reported), not connectivity/resting-only, and includes unmasked within-group healthy-group task effects. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

This study uses task-based fMRI probing social-related processing (viewing fearful and calm faces), includes a healthy adult control group (mean age ~39.8) reported separately, and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation results for the control group (within-group maps and tables/figures thresholded and reported using SPM99). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are explicitly described (tables and figures), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. The full-text contains methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside 18–65, or absence of healthy-group whole-brain task maps) are met.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social-evaluative task (naturalistic positive/negative/neutral social videos) in a sample of healthy adults (N=37, mean age 24.8). The authors report group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., negative>neutral, positive>neutral) with familywise error (FWE) correction and tabulated MNI coordinates and figures, clearly presenting healthy-group activation maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral, whole-brain and ROI analyses), and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this review: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text).

This is an fMRI experiment that examines visual perspective-taking (a social-cognitive/Theory-of-Mind task) in healthy adult participants (final N=16, mean age 22.4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts (SPM8; cluster-level FWE correction; tables and figures of results and coordinates) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, task, image acquisition, analysis), results, and discussion; thus full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (theory of mind/social-exchange reasoning) in healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=12, mean age 24.6) are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (story and card contrasts versus rest and between-condition contrasts) with tables and cluster thresholds (p<.005, extent threshold), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps/contrasts), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion discrimination (a social perception/understanding-of-others task). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=12) with results reported separately and matched to clinical subjects. Whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM2 analyses are reported (conjunction and within-group contrasts), and within-group contrasts for controls (e.g., sad > neutral) are described and illustrated. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps for the healthy group), and I6 (results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not present original, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI results for a social-related task in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports resting-state fMRI and meta-analytic coactivation modeling (MACM) but no within-study healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample: healthy adult participants, age 18–65; 20 right-handed healthy adults, mean age 18.5). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the study does not use fMRI during a social-related task; it uses resting-state fMRI and derives task-related coactivation via BrainMap meta-analysis rather than an in-study social task), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports group differences (patients vs controls) and conjunction analyses influenced by diagnosis but does not present an unmasked/whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (no clear within-group, whole-brain statistical map for the healthy/control group is reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses task-based fMRI targeting social processes: Theory of Mind and empathy) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map from the healthy/control group). I6 (acceptable reporting formats) is not satisfied for a healthy-group whole-brain effect because qualifying healthy-group whole-brain results are not presented in tables/figures/text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude because study does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map (E4).

The study includes a whole-brain, group-level fMRI task contrast (RMET “mind” vs “age”) in a healthy control group and reports voxelwise activation maps and coordinates. However, the healthy fMRI sample comprises older adults aged 51–84 (mean 68.4), with no separate analysis of a healthy subgroup constrained to ages 18–65. This fails inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample aged 18–65). Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for healthy participants), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (healthy sample age 18–65). Exclusion criterion applied: E5 (participants outside the 18–65 range without an analyzed subgroup in that range). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition using a theory-of-mind (ToM) task (mentalising vs control) in a sample of 109 healthy volunteers. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (ToM>control) with family-wise error and FDR-corrected results, figures, and coordinate tables, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for an fMRI social task in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI to study social processing (emotion recognition and gaze integration); (I4) includes a healthy young adult group (17–27, mean 20.65) providing a healthy adult sample within the 18–65 range for analysis; (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (PLS whole-brain results) with voxelwise maps and peak coordinates; (I6) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no only between-group-without-healthy-group maps, and includes an eligible healthy adult group). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study directly investigates social communication (imitation of communicative gestures) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (multiple contrasts, interaction effects) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo simulation) and describes results in text/tables/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

While the study uses fMRI with a social-related task (inferring others’ social emotions) and includes a healthy adult control group (17 typically developing males age ~30), the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported voxelwise results are primarily between-group contrasts (typically developing > ASD) and regions where ASD showed less activity; no standalone whole-brain healthy-group task map or within-group healthy activation image/coordinate table is provided in the results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5.

The study reports fMRI data acquired during a social joint-attention task (hyperscanning) demonstrating social interaction processing, meeting I3. It includes a large sample of healthy adult participants (80 HCs, ages within 18–65) with results reported for HC-HC pairs separately, meeting I4. The paper describes group-level whole-brain task analyses (INT>NoINT contrasts entered into group ANOVAs) and reports results obtained for the whole brain (see Methods and Results), satisfying I5. Reporting of whole-brain results in the text/figures/tables meets I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and includes healthy adults with whole-brain task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of others' eye gaze and face identity), meeting I3. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=9, mean age 24 ± 2.5), meeting I4. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (face vs control) with cluster-based thresholding (z>4) and reports anatomical coordinates obtained with SPM/Talairach and figures/tables of activation, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants within 18–65, and empirical fMRI data present). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation fMRI study of social processing and should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criterion I3 is met: the study used fMRI during a social-related task (perception of racial ingroup vs outgroup faces). Cannot confirm I4 (healthy adult sample aged 18–65) because ages and health status are not reported in the provided content. Cannot confirm I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) — the abstract references amygdala BOLD effects and an ROI-based analysis but does not clearly state whole-brain voxelwise results. Because not all inclusion criteria can be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied based on the available information.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates task-based fMRI probing empathy/forgiveness (social processing) and reports activations, but core article content (methods, participant ages, detailed results, and explicit statement of group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses or tables/coordinates) is not present to verify all inclusion criteria. I3 is satisfied (fMRI during social-related task). I4 cannot be confirmed because participant ages (18–65) are not reported in the provided text. I5 cannot be confirmed because the provided content does not include full methods/results or explicit whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinates (the abstract reports activated regions but this is insufficient to verify unmasked, group-level whole-brain maps). I6 cannot be confirmed for the same reason. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the available information. Recommend obtaining the complete full text to determine final eligibility.

This is an event-related fMRI study that investigates trustworthiness judgments of faces (a social evaluation/perception of others), using healthy adult participants (final N=14, ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level, random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPMs), with whole-brain results and coordinates/tables/figures and small-volume corrections; results for the healthy control group are clearly described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of causal attributions (social events) in healthy adult participants (12 neurologically healthy males, ages 20–51). The task is social-related (attribution of positive and negative social events), and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (internal vs external; self-serving vs non-self-serving) with tables of peak coordinates and figures, tested at voxelwise thresholds and corrected for multiple comparisons. Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, or non-empirical) apply.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study investigating social cognition (moral status of faces learned via an interactive Prisoner's Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (scanned sample: 11 right-handed adults, ages 21–36). The task is clearly social-related (learning about cooperators/defectors), and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM random-effects, with tables of coordinates and reported contrasts (main effects and interactions) for the healthy group. All required elements for inclusion are present: fMRI during a social task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported in text/tables. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (passive viewing of realistic social interaction video clips) in healthy adult participants (13 adults, mean age 27.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA; voxelwise threshold P ≤ 0.05 corrected across the whole brain), with coordinates/figures and cluster tables (Fig. 1, Table 1) showing activations (including dorsomedial PFC and precuneus) for relational vs. alone and relational vs. rest contrasts. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social gaze processing (social-related task: perception/understanding of others) conducted in healthy adult participants (8 right-handed young adults). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Although the study performed ROI analyses, it also performed voxel-based, group-averaged analyses and generated across-subjects t-statistic activation maps (displayed on a standard brain; Figure 4), satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group. The paper reports behavioral and imaging results for the healthy adult sample separately. Full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (cooperation vs competition) in healthy adults (12 participants aged 21–28). The methods report whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported contrasts, tables of activations, and figures—fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The task is clearly social-related (interaction with another player; mentalizing, self–other processing). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages within 18–65) using a social-related task (evaluative judgments of self-conscious moral emotions: guilt and embarrassment). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (G−N, E−N, G−E, E−G) with statistical thresholds, tables of coordinates, and regression analyses for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

Only abstract/metadata (PDF not accessible) is provided. The abstract indicates fMRI experiments of social (theory-of-mind/intentions) processing, satisfying I3. However, the full text (methods/results) is not available to confirm critical criteria: whether the sample comprises healthy adults aged 18–65 (I4) and whether at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group is reported (I5). Because these inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete content, the study must be excluded at this screening stage. Full text incomplete prevents assessing reporting format (I6) as well.

This is an empirical fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-cognitive task addressing Perception and Understanding of Self), conducted in a healthy adult sample (N=10, mean age 26.9). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-corrected Z-stat maps) and provides tables of peak MNI coordinates for contrasts (self>other, other>self), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation of people vs objects) in healthy adults (N=14, ages 18.3–23.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trial types; impression > sequencing) with stereotaxic coordinates, thresholds (P<0.001), and tables of regions, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an event-related BOLD fMRI investigation of self-face versus familiar and unfamiliar faces, directly addressing social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self). The sample is 12 healthy adult participants (mean age 19.36) reported separately and screened; no clinical groups confound the healthy-group results. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects one-sample t-tests) are reported, with contrasts and cluster-corrected maps/tables described in the text and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of emotional prosody (social communication/perception of others) in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.4). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 RFX, whole-brain contrasts) with coordinates and statistical maps/contrast results for the healthy sample (e.g., emotion vs neutral, attention effects). It is not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind and empathy) using a task-based paradigm in healthy adult participants (n=13; age 19–36). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, voxelwise thresholding, cluster tables/coordinates and figures) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of design and outcomes. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment probing social-related processing (gaze, social vs. arbitrary facial expressions) in healthy adult participants. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=18, mean age 25.9). Analyses used whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise statistics (SPM2) with reported contrasts, SPM{z} maps, tables of coordinates and figures of activated regions (main effects and interactions) clearly described for the healthy group. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study directly probes perception/understanding of self vs other (detection of visuo-motor and visuo-proprioceptive synchrony/ownership), a construct falling under ‘‘Perception and Understanding of Self’’ relevant to the review. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=15 after exclusion), ages 20–28, meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM2 one-sample t tests, cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) with tables/figures of significant clusters and contrast maps for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core article content is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception), using a perceptual one-back task tied to social constructs (perception and understanding of others). Sample: healthy adults (ages 18–32), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects group contrasts, Talairach coordinates, cluster tables and figures). Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages, or between-group-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/summary provided). From the abstract, the study used fMRI on face perception (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants, so I3 and I4 appear satisfied. However, the available content does not allow verification that at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported (I5 cannot be confirmed) nor whether whole-brain results are present in tables/figures/supplement (I6 unverified). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone. Because the full article (methods, results, figures/tables) is not provided, I exclude this record pending retrieval of the full text for verification.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social interactive task (competitive reaction-time paradigm inducing reactive aggression). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; thresholding and tables of activation coordinates, conjunctions, and figures) clearly for the healthy/control subjects. Sample consists of healthy adult males (mean age 28.6; two excluded as noted). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical).

This empirical task-based fMRI study examines social cognition (perception/understanding of others) using an affective assessment task of social-group images. Participants were healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 19.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses and coordinates (Talairach), contrasts, figures, and ROI checks, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 29.4) that used a social-related task (meaning-relatedness judgments for social concepts vs. animal function concepts). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain and ROI analyses are described; figures and tables report voxelwise activations and conjunction analyses at voxel-level thresholds), clearly attributable to the healthy participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. The provided full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study examines facial emotion recognition (explicit vs implicit), which is a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). The sample includes 29 healthy adult participants (ages 20–35), with results reported for the healthy group. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (FWE-corrected whole-brain analyses reported, tables/figures of activations), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is eligible for inclusion.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract-level content provided). The study clearly uses fMRI in a social-related task (self vs. other; perspective taking), so I3 is met. However, the provided content does not report participant characteristics (age range, health status) needed to confirm a group of healthy adults 18–65 (I4 not confirmed). While the abstract reports activations in MPFC, the excerpt does not explicitly state that group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group are reported (I5 not confirmable). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and the full text is incomplete, I exclude the study pending full-text confirmation of participant details and whole-brain results.

This fMRI study investigates communicative speech (a social communication task) in healthy adult volunteers (N=29, ages 18–24). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and contrasts are reported (e.g., communication vs description; communication vs control), with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; activation tables/figures and coordinates are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables and text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study used a social interaction simulation task probing friendship (social-related processing) and reports task-evoked whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5; FWE-corrected results, cluster-thresholded) in a sample of healthy adult participants (n=28, age range 19–27). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results (behavioral and neuroimaging), and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adults, 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Only abstract and metadata are available (full text inaccessible). The study uses task-based fMRI of emotional facial expressions in healthy adults (N=12), which meets I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). However, the full text is not available to confirm that the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (I5). The abstract lists regional BOLD increases but does not explicitly state whole-brain voxelwise maps, tables of coordinates, or provide sufficient detail to verify I5/I6. Per screening rules, absence of confirmation for any required inclusion criterion leads to exclusion. Recommend obtaining the full PDF to reassess.

The study reports event-related fMRI (with complementary EEG) in 14 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 29±6) performing a social cognition task (perception of others' emotional facial expressions), satisfying the review objective. The abstract states that statistical parametric mapping identified activation in dorsal medial frontal cortex during emotion perception, indicating group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis. Therefore criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (acceptable result reporting) are met. However, only the abstract and metadata are provided here (no full methods, results, or figures), so the full text is incomplete and I cannot fully verify detailed reporting (e.g., exact whole-brain maps, coordinates, or thresholding). Inclusion recommended but fulltext_incomplete=true; full article should be reviewed to confirm.

The provided text (appears to be an abstract) describes an fMRI study of social nonverbal communication (viewing, imitating, producing facial expressions and hand gestures), so it meets the review topic. However the full text is incomplete: participant characteristics (health status, ages) and details confirming group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (e.g., unthresholded or reported coordinates/tables/figures clearly identified as healthy-group contrasts) are not provided. Therefore I cannot confirm inclusion criteria I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available information, but because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete/fulltext content, I must exclude. Recommend obtaining the full article (methods, results, participant details, whole-brain maps or coordinate tables) for reassessment.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind: perception and understanding of others) using task-evoked BOLD during cartoon-based ToM tasks, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 13 healthy adults aged 22–38 with results reported for the healthy group, satisfying I4. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain exploratory contrast (ToM conditions vs non-ToM) and subsequently presents voxelwise contrasts and coordinates (figures/tables), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, analyses), results (whole-brain and ROI findings), and discussion; it appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining neural processing of social hierarchy (social processing), using task-based fMRI with explicit social tasks (stable and unstable hierarchies) in healthy adult participants. The sample comprises healthy adults within the 18–65 range (N=72, analyses on 48 social participants). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and provides thresholded statistical maps, coordinates, tables, and figures for key contrasts (e.g., ‘superior player > inferior player’) and outcome contrasts, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, tasks, imaging acquisition and analysis), results, and discussion; sufficient core content is present for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses task-based fMRI to probe social-related processing (self- and mother-referential tasks and a Social Attribution Task), includes a healthy adult sample (final n=17, mean age 21.5 years, within 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps (composite t-maps, FDR-corrected results and tables of peak coordinates for contrasts such as Self vs. Letter, Mother vs. Letter, Friends vs. Bumper Cars). Results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables, satisfying acceptable reporting modes. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range participants, or only between-group contrasts without healthy-group maps) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, figures/tables descriptions and discussion, so full text is complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study using a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) and a non-social control (Gamble), fulfilling the social-processing requirement. Participants are healthy adults (Experiments 1 and 2: mean ages ~20.8 and 21.2; N=20 and N=30), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (PD vs. Gamble; in-group vs. out-group), thresholded maps, tables of activations, and ROI/ connectivity analyses; whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of self-recognition (perception/understanding of self), a social-related construct. Healthy adult sample (n=35, aged 18–24) is reported. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses are described (SPM5, cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) with tables of coordinates and figures. The paper reports task-evoked activation maps for healthy participants across contrasts (self, friend, control) and meets reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages ~24) using a social/empathy task (SELF/OTHER emotional attribution) — satisfying the review scope. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SELF vs baseline, OTHER vs baseline) with results thresholded at p<0.05 FWE-corrected and provides tables and figures of activation peaks (whole-group simple effects), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (Social Motor Response Learning task involving social inclusion/exclusion) in healthy adults (n=18, mean age 42, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-group t tests; FDR whole-brain correction) and presents coordinates/figures of task-evoked activations in healthy participants (dorsal ACC, frontal operculum, ventral striatum, etc.). Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within age range).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social communication task (gaze following vs finger pointing) in healthy adult participants (N=17, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (gaze vs baseline, finger vs baseline, and contrasts between conditions) using random-effects models with statistical thresholds and cluster reporting; results are presented in figures and text with coordinates. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, participants within age range, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating perception/understanding of self vs others (own vs others' body parts), which fits the review's social-related constructs (I3). Participant samples are healthy adults (Experiments: n=12 and n=15; adults), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level voxelwise localization contrasts and provides Talairach coordinates and cluster voxel counts for EBA, LOC, and early visual cortices (whole-brain contrasts used to identify ROIs), satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map (I5) and allowing coordinate-based reporting (I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, resting-state-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study probing social-related processing (attribution of intentions/theory of mind) using a task manipulating perceived agency (Composer vs Computer). Sample includes healthy adults (n=12 included in analysis), ages 21–31. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts with coordinates and cluster-level correction (Tables/Figures), and links activation to behavioral ratings. It is empirical fMRI task data in healthy adults and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: it uses task-based fMRI during Wason selection tasks contrasting social-exchange (cheater detection), precautionary, and descriptive rules (addresses Theory of Mind and social-exchange reasoning). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=12, mean age 24.6), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses and contrasts (story and card-phase contrasts), with thresholding and tables/figures of activated clusters and coordinates — meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=12, ages 22–37) that uses task-based fMRI to examine social-related processing (perception/understanding of others and group dynamics from footstep sounds). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and multiple whole-brain contrasts (e.g., STEP1+STEP2 – REST; STEP1 – NOISE1; STEP2 – NOISE2) with statistical maps and Talairach coordinates presented in tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to investigate social processing (perception of socially relevant facial expressions) (I3); includes a healthy adult sample (17 right-handed male volunteers, mean age ~25.9) with results reported for the healthy group (I4); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and lists coordinates/activation tables from random-effects analyses (SPM5) (I5); and whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=17, mean age 26) that uses a social-related task (observation of social vs. individual actions with gaze manipulation) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM maps, coordinates, thresholding, and tables/figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported via tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are applicable. Full text appears complete (core article content present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (viewing approaching characters with happy vs. angry expressions) in healthy adult participants. The sample consists of healthy young adults (fMRI N=10), and methods/results describe group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (Angry>Happy and Happy>Angry contrasts) with MNI coordinates and voxelwise thresholds reported. The task probes social-related constructs (affiliation/dominance). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20, ages 20–34) that investigates mirror-system responses to action observation and sensorimotor training. The task involves passive observation of hand and foot actions (perception/understanding of others) and is framed in terms of social cognition/action understanding. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, conjunctions and contrasts thresholded at p<0.05 corrected for whole brain) and provides peak coordinates and tables of activations. All relevant inclusion criteria are met (I3: social-related fMRI task—action observation/mirror-system; I4: healthy adult sample; I5: whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported; I6: results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition (inferring preferences, age categorizations) in healthy adult participants (undergraduates, mean age 20). The methods include whole-brain fMRI preprocessing and random-effects GLM analyses, and the Results report group-level, voxelwise activation contrasts with Talairach coordinates, cluster sizes, statistical thresholds, tables and figures (mPFC and other regions). The sample and analyses are clearly described for the healthy adult group. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (behavioral n=10; fMRI n=12; ages 18–40) that manipulates social context (direct vs averted gaze) during a task probing perception/understanding of others. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with reported contrasts, statistical thresholds, figures and tables of activated loci (e.g., Tables 1–2, whole-brain maps), satisfying whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social-related task (faces as target stimuli) embedded in a target-detection oddball paradigm, satisfying I3. The sample consisted of 19 healthy adults (age range 19.3–47.5), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL mixed-effects, cluster-corrected maps) for contrasts including face targets > novels and direct comparisons with shape targets, with figures and tables of MNI coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not restricted to between-group contrasts, participants are within age 18–65, and this is an original empirical report. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) fMRI during a social-related task—participants viewed eye stimuli with pupillary biofeedback probing social perception; (I4) sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=14, mean age 22, within 18–65); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (main effects and interactions reported with whole-brain corrected thresholds and coordinates); (I6) whole-brain results presented in text, figures and tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore include.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during social-related self-judgment tasks (perception/understanding of self). Participants are healthy adults (n=24; ages reported within adult range), and analyses include whole-brain, voxel-wise random-effects contrasts with tables/coordinates and ROI follow-ups. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses fMRI during an explicit emotion-recognition task (social processing) in a healthy adult sample (21–33 years). Group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (whole-slab) are reported and illustrated (activation maps and coordinates) for task-evoked contrasts across the healthy sample, not limited to ROI-only results. Although spatial coverage was restricted to an amygdala-optimized slab, the paper reports voxelwise group results (whole-slab maps and coordinate results) in the text/figures/tables, satisfying the review’s requirement for group-level voxelwise reporting. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy (social cognition: perception and understanding of others) in healthy adult participants (n=23, ages 19–34). The Methods and Results report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM contrasts, tables of coordinates, figures) for task-evoked activations (e.g., Pain > No Pain contrasts, No Pain: Dissimilar > Similar), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references; thus fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-perceptual mentalizing task (the Reading the Mind in the Eyes), conducted in healthy adult participants (native Japanese and white American, ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., RME − GD; same- vs. other-culture contrasts) analyzed in SPM5 and presents coordinates and thresholded activations in multiple tables and figures (Tables 1–4, conjunctions, and contrasts). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample within 18–65; I5: whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported; I6: results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (Trust Game reciprocity) in a healthy adult sample (ages 18–22). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and regression analyses are reported (e.g., defect > reciprocate, regressions with reciprocity) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level correction (AlphaSim), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. ROI analyses are also reported but do not replace the whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met.
