Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (acceptable coordinate/figure reporting).

This is a task-based fMRI study of social processing (attachment-related perception of others' facial emotions) in a sample of healthy adults (N=51, mean age 28.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (main effects of masked sad and happy faces vs neutral, and regressions with attachment scores) with coordinates and multiple-comparison correction. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical data present).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=26, mean age 24.4) that directly probes social-related processing (perception of others' pain, perceived agency/intentionality). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts such as pain>no pain and social context contrasts), provides tables of coordinates and thresholding methods (FDR p<0.05), and shows activation maps and ROI analyses from a random-effects group analysis. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

Although this is an fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults (I3 satisfied) with a healthy adult sample aged 18–41 (I4 satisfied), the paper reports a region-of-interest (individual STS mapping) analysis extracting contrast estimates from measuring points and performing within-ROI one-sample tests. I find no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map or voxelwise results for the healthy group (no whole-brain contrasts/tables/coordinates from a whole-brain analysis reported). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (direct and reflected self-appraisals/mentalizing), includes a healthy adult sample (N=12, ages 22.6–30.4), and presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses and contrasts clearly reported for adults (within-group conjunctions and condition vs. rest results, whole-brain corrected/thresholded). Therefore it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group in 18–65 range), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group task maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition using an ecologically valid Movie for the Assessment of Social Cognition (MASC) task (Theory of Mind), performed in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 20–45). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical results from GLM analyses (tables of coordinates, figures) and complementary model-free T-PICA results. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: task-based fMRI of social processing; I4: healthy adult sample age 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported; I6: results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI experiment probing empathy and social cognition by presenting social scenes (emotional vs. neutral; one vs. two people) to healthy adult participants (N=17, 16 analyzed; mean age 27.8). The paradigm is explicitly social-related (perception/understanding of others). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are described (random-effects GLM, FDR thresholding, Talairach coordinates, tables and figures), and contrasts for healthy participants are reported. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults examining self- and other-referential processing (social cognition). The task involves trait judgments about self and a close friend, which falls under perception/understanding of self and others (I3). Sample comprises healthy adults aged 19.4–31 with group-level analyses reported for the healthy participants (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts analyzed with SPM5 and provides coordinates, figures, and tables of group-level activation (I5, I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Included for the meta-analysis of social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This full-text reports an fMRI study of social processing (joint attention/theory of mind) in healthy adults and meets all required inclusion criteria. I3: The task is explicitly social (perception/understanding of others; participants infer what an avatar is seeing). I4: Sample comprises healthy adults aged 20–31, with group results reported for the healthy participants. I5: The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task contrasts (body>place and place>body) with figures and a table of coordinates (Table 1). I6: Whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables and described in the text. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of charitable donation decisions—a social decision-making task involving social cognition (empathy, perspective-taking). Participants were 22 healthy adult females (age range 19–38), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation by donation amount; contrasts and whole-brain corrected statistical maps and coordinates are reported) and presents whole-brain corrected SPMs and coordinate tables; supplementary tables provide additional results. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only analyses, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are clearly reported. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (live face-to-face interaction and joint attention), using task-based functional MRI with healthy adult participants (ages 18–29) and reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Live > Recorded; Joint Attention > Solo Attention) with corrected maps and peak coordinates. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (coordinates and maps clearly described). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social expectancy violations along warmth/competence) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (Princeton undergraduates, mean age 20.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected thresholds and Talairach coordinates (tables/figures) and presents full methods, results, and discussion, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study directly examines social-related processing (intimacy/attachment/empathy) using task-based fMRI, with healthy adult participants (N=36; mean age 23). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Pain vs. Neutral across Self/Loved-one/Stranger), with SPM thresholds, tables of activations, and correlation/PPI analyses. Results for the healthy sample are reported at the group level. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=21, ages 23–51) using a social-related task (socio-emotional preference; judging whether they liked faces). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Preference > Gender and baseline contrasts) thresholded and FDR-corrected, with tables of activation coordinates and figures. Thus it satisfies: I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented as coordinates/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes task activation maps in addition to connectivity analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study with a social-related task (familiarity judgments involving personally familiar, famous, and unfamiliar faces) probing social cognition and adaptive social responses. Participants were healthy adults (n=24 analyzed; ages 19–31). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM5) with cluster-level correction and presents activation maps and tables of peaks/coordinates. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, empirical data present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Study 2: n=21 heterosexual male undergraduates, ages within 18–65) examining neural responses during passive viewing of social targets (sexualized vs. clothed men and women) that probe social-cognitive processes (mentalizing/perception and understanding of others). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (voxelwise p < .001, cluster correction via AlphaSim), tables/figures of activations, and correlations with hostile sexism scores. Full article text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition/analysis), results (whole-brain contrasts, correlations), and discussion. Thus I3, I4, and I5 are satisfied (and whole-brain results are reported in standard tables/figures, consistent with I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (charades) in healthy adults (mean age 27.5, N=18 analyzed), directly addressing social communication and perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain differential Granger-causality maps and thresholded cortical maps (cluster-corrected at P<0.05) identifying brain regions during the task, satisfying whole-brain reporting (maps/figures and cluster thresholds are described). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (appropriate reporting). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates social processing (dynamic facial expressions) in healthy adult participants (ages ~22), meeting I3 and I4. However, the reported group-level results are presented via ROI analyses with small-volume corrections (amygdala, insula, striatum, OFC) and ROI-based conjunction/interaction tests. The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map or whole-brain coordinate table/results that would qualify as a whole-brain effect. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results) and fails I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing/understanding others) using task-based functional MRI. Participants: 64 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 21.2, range 18–26), satisfying the sample inclusion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholds, peak coordinates, tables, and figures (MPFC and other regions) — satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, design, imaging procedure, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages, or only between-group contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment that directly manipulates a social stimulus (gaze shifts) within a task assessing action control, meeting the review’s scope. Participants were healthy adults (n=23; ages 21–37). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM second-level random-effects ANOVA), thresholding and cluster coordinates, and presents activation tables/figures for the healthy sample. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social rejection paradigm) addressing social rejection and related social processing (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult group (16 adult female participants; adults are reported separately from adolescents) satisfying the adult healthy-sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exclusion>inclusion contrasts with cluster-level FWE correction across participants) and reports coordinates and cluster tables; it also reports group comparisons and within-group post-hoc tests for adults (interaction and t-tests), providing voxelwise results identifiable for the healthy adult group (I5). Whole-brain results and coordinates are presented in tables/figures in the main text (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (n=98, mean age 20.7) using task-based scans involving self/friend/stranger judgments. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., self > Bush; friends > strangers) with whole-brain maps and thresholding described, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task results), and I6 (appropriate reporting). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI with social-emotional stimuli (empathy/sympathy) and reports whole-brain group-level activation maps and coordinate tables, meeting I3, I5, and I6. However, the sample is a mixed-age cohort (ages 7–40) and the paper does not present a separate adult-only (18–65) healthy-group whole-brain analysis or subgroup results for adults. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (at least one healthy adult group reported separately) is not met. No formal exclusion criteria (E2–E6) strictly apply, but failure to meet I4 prevents inclusion for a review restricted to healthy adult fMRI results.

The study reports fMRI during a social task (Trust Game) so I3 is met. However, the sample consists of adolescents (three phases of adolescence) and no healthy adult (age 18–65) group is reported or analyzed separately, so I4 is not met and exclusion E5 applies. The provided document is limited to abstract, references, and metadata (no full methods/results), so I cannot verify whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group maps (I5 not met) — fulltext is incomplete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not include an eligible adult healthy group (E5) and key methodological details/whole-brain results cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met: I4, I5. Exclusion IDs met: E5.

The study uses task-based fMRI to examine identity discrimination of faces (a social-perception task—Perception and Understanding of Others), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults (mean age 24.8, final N=15), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (ANOVA and cluster-threshold corrected contrasts; whole-brain results described and reported in figures/tables/supplementary material with coordinates), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are presented in the main/supplementary text (tables of coordinates and figures) which is acceptable. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and whole-brain analyses and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy maps, participants in age range, and is empirical).

This fMRI study examines social interaction perception using point-light displays (social interaction vs non-social), a social-related task (I3). The sample is 14 healthy adults (mean age 29.4), within 18–65 (I4). The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SI vs NSI), with FDR-corrected whole-brain results and cluster tables/figures (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and contains qualifying whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study of humor processing (a social-cognition-relevant task that involves theory-of-mind/mentalizing and social emotion), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=29, ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (Cartoons vs Neutral and parametric modulation analyses) with tables/coordinates and conjunctions, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of person perception/impression formation (social-related processing) in healthy adults. fMRI task: event-related design presenting faces paired with political views to probe violations of social expectations—clearly social cognition (perception/understanding of others). Sample: healthy adults aged 19–30 (n=18 after exclusions). Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (random-effects incongruent vs. congruent contrasts), with FDR-corrected results, tables of coordinates, and figures—satisfying requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, and empirical). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly manipulates social context (social vs. non-social/single conditions) and assesses brain activation during retrieval of socially encoded vs. non-socially encoded words. Sample: 24 healthy adults (ages 18–28) meeting the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects, contrasts, cluster-corrected results) with tables/figures and coordinates identifying mPFC and other regions. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text is not available (PDF-only); abstract/metadata indicate: I3 satisfied (fMRI during social interaction videos) and I4 satisfied (healthy young adult sample). However I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met. Because one required inclusion criterion (I5) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending access to the full article.

This is an fMRI study of allocentric social hierarchy/alliance judgments in healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 24.2). The task is clearly social in nature (judging social hierarchy and alliance), meeting the review’s social-related construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task contrasts (thresholded at p<0.05 FWE) with Talairach coordinates, tables, and SPM maps for the healthy control group. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial (social-related) decision-making toward family (affiliation/attachment, understanding of others). Sample: healthy young adults (N=25; Mage=20.2) within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain task contrasts (Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward) with tables of coordinates and corrected results, and whole-brain PPI analyses; thus whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group are reported. Reporting meets acceptable formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-related task under ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’) in healthy adult participants (ages 19–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses with explicit thresholds and coordinates (e.g., MPFC, PCC, precuneus; P < 0.001 voxelwise, cluster-level corrected P < 0.05), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present, and the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

The study reports an fMRI task probing observation of virtual social interactions (meets I3). Participants were recruited as healthy subjects and results are reported for a healthy group (data from 15 participants), meeting I4. The paper describes whole-brain EPI acquisition with full-brain coverage and presents group-level activation maps (t-value maps) for social interaction vs. control trials based on the healthy participant sample, satisfying I5. Results are presented as figures of activation maps and time courses (acceptable per I6). Core methods and representative group results are provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears to include methods and representative results; core empirical content is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 23) using a social task manipulating eye contact and action mimicry. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Direct > Averted, Incongruent > Congruent, interaction contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables of coordinates (Table 1) and figures; random-effects analyses are described. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20, mean age 18.7) that used task-based functional MRI during social-comparative judgments of Close Others (romantic partner) and Non-Close Others (roommate). Group-level, voxelwise contrasts were performed (second-level random-effects SPM analyses) and results are reported with peak coordinates and corrected statistics; whole-brain second-level contrasts (e.g., Target × Breadth, Valence, Target) are described and coordinates/clusters are reported. Although multiple-comparison correction was performed within a priori ROIs, the paper reports group-level task-evoked activation maps and coordinates for the healthy sample. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract and metadata indicate an fMRI task investigating perception of faces and voices (social-related processing), with 20 healthy adult participants and group-level voxelwise results (regions reported, e.g., left hippocampus; voxelwise statistical criteria discussed). This satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results reported), and I6 (results described). However, the provided full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata present), so methods/results/discussion cannot be fully verified; therefore fulltext_incomplete=true. No exclusion criteria appear met based on available information.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults: participants (N=19, ages 19–28) performed social and non-social semantic tasks during fMRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., ‘social’ > ‘non-social’ and ‘non-social’ > ‘social’) with cluster-level correction (P<0.05) and peak coordinates in tables/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI task study of supramodal emotional perception (social communication / perception of others), with a healthy adult sample (N=24; ages 18–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses (e.g., AV > A, CAV > ICAV) with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activations. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (human–human competition invoking theory-of-mind), using a task-based paradigm during MRI (Stroop with human vs machine opponents). Sample: healthy adults (n=14, mean age 35.9) within 18–65 and results reported for healthy group. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects one-sample t-tests, contrasts, cluster thresholds, tables of coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball social exclusion), with healthy adult participants (n=20 after exclusions; ages ~25), and within-subject design. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (social exclusion vs fair play), cluster-level correction, tables/coordinates, and figures describing group-level effects and correlations — satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social decision-making task (ultimatum game) with online and offline analyses. Participants: healthy adult males aged 23–28 (meets age/sample criterion). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (offline whole-brain SVM across subjects) with reported discriminating volumes and MNI coordinates (Tables and figures) constituting voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of biological motion perception (socially relevant: perception/understanding of others’ actions) in a healthy adult sample (13 right-handed males, mean age 28.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (canonical vs scrambled biological motion) with corrected statistics and MNI coordinates (Table 1, figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The task is social-related (perception of others’ actions), and healthy-group results are reported separately. Although the paper also includes seed-based functional connectivity and DCM analyses, these supplement rather than replace the reported whole-brain task activation. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of affective (social) touch in healthy adults: 22 right-handed participants aged 19–35. The task clearly targets social-related processing (affective/affiliative touch). The paper reports multiparticipant whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results (arm > baseline, palm > baseline, and direct arm > palm contrasts) with correction and cluster thresholds and provides tables/figures of group-level activations. Prescan behavioral data, methods, results, and discussion are present; full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study reports task-based fMRI of emotional prosody comprehension (a social-communication / perception-of-others task), using healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 18–51). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests and whole-brain cluster-corrected results for contrasts such as emotional vs neutral and complex vs simple emotion), with coordinates and figures described in the text. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social group manipulation (minimal team paradigm) and an action-judgment task probing perception of others’ actions (social perception/affiliation). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (age range includes participants up to 43 years; the group-level analyses are reported for the healthy participant sample). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked contrasts (e.g., single-video > fixation; own-team > other-team; paired-judgment > press) with cluster-level FWE correction across the whole brain; results are reported in the text and figures. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social working memory task (social cognition/mentalizing) with healthy adult participants (N=16, mean age 20). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric effects across social load) with thresholding and coordinates/tables (Tables S2/S3) and whole-brain statistical maps described in the text and figures. Results are reported for the healthy sample (no exclusive clinical-only sample). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and imaging analysis details, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathic decision-making, a social-related task (empathy/understanding others). Participants: 32 healthy adult males (mean age 22.8), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM results, conjunctions, tables of activations and cluster-level inference reported, and descriptions of PPI and whole-brain contrasts), meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Results are reported as whole-brain corrected maps and tables of activations, consistent with inclusion. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text is complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 22) using a task contrasting communicative versus noncommunicative vocal sounds. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (vocal > nonvocal; communicative > noncommunicative) with thresholding and peak coordinates, and includes methods, results, and discussion. Whole-brain maps and peak coordinates are clearly reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study that directly investigates social perception (affiliation vs isolation) while participants performed pleasantness judgments (I3). The sample includes a healthy younger adult group (M age = 20.75), satisfying the 18–65 healthy adult requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and thresholded results (conjunctions, contrasts) with tables/figures of significant clusters (voxelwise maps reported/thresholds described), meeting whole-brain reporting requirements (I5,I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references) is provided here, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age-out-of-range only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social/self-other referential task (VV-SORP-T) clearly within social-related processing. Sample: 20 healthy adult women aged 18–52, with clinical exclusions, satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (SPM8 random-effects analyses; Figures/Tables report voxel-wise results and coordinates; cluster thresholds and correction procedures described). Results for the healthy group are reported directly. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social evaluation/impression formation (meets I3). It includes a healthy young adult group aged 20–29 (meets I4); although an older group (61–85) is also reported, the presence of the young healthy group satisfies the age requirement. Analyses are whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise group contrasts (social vs. non-social; social-meaningful vs. social-irrelevant) with cluster correction and conjunction analyses, and results are reported in tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, reports within-group/healthy-group effects, and is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation/updating of others) in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–45). The task is explicitly social (person perception, forming/updating impressions based on behavioral vignettes). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (voxelwise contrasts, interaction L2>F3 by consistency, thresholding, cluster correction) with results described in text, figures, and tables. All core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in 51 healthy adults (ages 18–53) that investigates social-cognition-related processing (affective/emotional speech comprehension and theory-of-mind inference). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with SPM analyses, FWE-corrected maps, activation peaks and tables, and detailed methods/results/discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample; I5: whole-brain group-level task maps reported; I6: results presented as maps/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures, discussion). Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion.

The article reports an original fMRI experiment examining empathy/threat to self, friend, and stranger (a social-related task). Participants were healthy adults (n=22, mean age 23.6), within the 18–65 range. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (threat minus safe) with conjunction and whole-brain analyses, cluster thresholds, and supplementary whole-brain results; coordinates/tables and figures are reported. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task-evoked group maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related task (adult expert advice) and includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the full text presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses primarily as developmental (between-age-group) contrasts and reports ROI-based within-group comparisons; it does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map explicitly identified for the healthy adult group alone. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (clear whole-brain healthy-group task map) is not met. Because the paper reports mainly between-group/developmental contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain adult-group task effect, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study using naturalistic social-emotional film stimuli that probe perception/understanding of others and empathy (meets I3). Sample: 16 healthy adults aged 25–49 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ISC maps and ISC-by-valence/arousal GLMs) with voxelwise permutation testing and FDR correction; results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps and figures/tables (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects, empirical fMRI data in adults). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-affective task (Socio-affective Video Task) probing compassion, empathy, and positive/negative affect—clear social-related processing. Sample: healthy adults (N=94 women, age 18–35) reported separately. The paper reports group-level task-evoked whole-brain activation results (HE vs LE; parametric modulations; FWE-corrected whole-brain results are described) and provides coordinate tables and figures; ROI analyses are also used but whole-brain effects are explicitly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults: subjects performed an ‘Other’ task requiring prediction of another person’s choices (social perception/understanding of others), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample comprised healthy, normal adult participants (39 recruited, n=36 analyzed), reported separately and used for group analyses. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain regression analyses with cluster-level correction, Tables 1–2 and figures showing activations), and results are described in the main text and tables. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are healthy adults, and paper is empirical). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based movie clips to elicit social motivations (affiliation and power), meeting the review objective. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=17, mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (affiliation>control, power>control) analyzed with SPM5 and provides activation clusters and MNI coordinates (Table 1, Fig. 2), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=27, ages ~25) that uses task-based functional MRI to investigate social-intention understanding (observation of cooperative vs affective social interactions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, direct contrasts, FWE-corrected maps, and tables of coordinates/activations) and ROI analyses; behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Thus it meets the review’s fMRI social-processing task requirement, includes a healthy adult sample within 18–65, and provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 21–34) who viewed social audiovisual movie clips, addressing social perception—meeting the review objective. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses are reported (non-orthogonalized and orthogonalized regressors), with statistical maps thresholded and summarized (figures and coordinates/tables), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. All inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an event-related fMRI task manipulating affiliative vs nonaffiliative social scenarios (social-related processing: affiliation/attachment). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=27, mean age ~27) within the 18–65 range. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with FWE-corrected results and ROI-corrected small-volume results, with coordinates and figures/tables (e.g., affiliative vs nonaffiliative and valence contrasts). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining maternal neural responses to infant cry (an attachment/social-affiliation stimulus), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Participants are adult mothers (mean age 24.1), within the 18–65 range, and the reported results pertain to this healthy adult sample. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (whole-brain FDR thresholding, cluster coordinates/tables and figures) for contrasts of interest (own cry > control/other), fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without healthy-group task maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathy/perspective taking) in healthy adults (N=18, ages 21–31). The methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level SPM8 analyses, cluster- and peak-level FWE corrections) and report significant activations (tables, conjunctions, time-course analyses), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The task is social-related (Self/Other perspective taking during observation of pain). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an original empirical report). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary figures, so fulltext appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task fMRI with social-related tasks (social texts and social videos probing theory of mind/emotional state inference); (I4) the sample includes a healthy adult group (N=45; ages 19–23) with results reported for that group; (I5) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and random-effects analyses are reported (conjunction contrasts, corrected maps, and peak coordinates in Appendix A); (I6) whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables/appendices. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining processing of emotional facial expressions (social communication/perception of others) using task-based whole-brain analyses in healthy adult humans (N=23, ages 24–34). The paper reports group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (significance maps with cluster correction and stereotactic coordinates/supplementary table) for the healthy human group and displays group activation figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition/action understanding (why/how/what/how tasks) in healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32). The manuscript describes group-level, voxelwise analyses and explicitly states that whole-brain results and details about the mask are provided in the Supplemental Methods (satisfying I5/I6). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, and the sample meets the healthy adult criterion (I4). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual perspective taking (a social cognition/‘perception and understanding of others’ task), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (final N=16, mean age 22.4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM8) with cluster-level correction and reports contrasts and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults, 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI task study in healthy adults (n=21, mean age 24) that investigates mirror-system responses during observation and execution of actions and trained shape-action mappings, which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (social-related processing). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses including ROI and a whole-brain analysis (threshold p<0.001 uncorrected) with peak coordinates and tables/figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 25) using task-evoked BOLD responses to social (ostensive vs non-ostensive) stimuli, meeting the review objective. The manuscript reports group-level RFX whole-brain ANOVAs and presents task-evoked voxelwise results (including an exploratory whole-brain finding in visual cortex) and peak MNI coordinates for reported effects, and thus provides group-level whole-brain task activation evidence for the healthy sample. Sample falls within 18–65. Although the primary inferential tests were constrained via ROI small-volume corrections, the authors explicitly ran whole-brain group analyses and report whole-brain exploratory results; peak coordinates for effects are reported (MNI). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study that directly manipulates social information (trustworthiness judgments) in an n-back task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables of activations. Participants are healthy adults (initial N=16, analyses N=14; mean age 22 within 18–65). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, satisfying completeness. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and reports healthy-group task-evoked whole-brain maps. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n≈36, mean age ~21) that used a social-related task (viewing others in pain—perception and understanding of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (painful vs non-painful contrasts) with FDR correction and provides coordinates/tables and figures describing the activations (pre- and post-priming whole-brain results). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied: fMRI social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level task maps reported (I5), and reporting of coordinates/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining social/person-related processing (familiar, famous, novel faces), satisfying the review objective. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=15 females, ages ~22), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and ALE meta-analysis, with voxelwise results and peak coordinates (Talairach) presented and thresholding procedures described. Whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Facesfamous vs. Facesnovel, Facesfriends vs. Facesnovel, faces vs. landmarks) are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (face gender categorization), involving healthy adult participants (n=16, ages 19–42). The paper reports both region-of-interest analyses and a whole-brain, random-effects voxel-wise group analysis with reported clusters/coordinates (gender-different > gender-same), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and the study should be included.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of interpersonal resource conflict (a social-related task) in a sample of healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects contrasts are reported (e.g., Conflict > No-Conflict, Condition × Conflict interaction), with tables/figures of activation maps and reported coordinates and thresholding details. Behavioral and covariate whole-brain regression analyses are also described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (core article content present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using well-defined social-cognitive tasks (Why-How and Categories-Exemplars) that probe understanding of others’ actions/intentions (mentalizing/theory-of-mind constructs). Sample: 24 healthy adult participants aged 18–27. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM5; thresholding, cluster correction, Table 2 and figures), including conjunction contrasts of task conditions. Results are presented as whole-brain activations and coordinate tables. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables, appendix).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (attractiveness comparisons of people; includes social perception of others). Sample consists of 25 healthy adult women (mean age 23.46), within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results (whole-brain analyses, conjunctions, thresholds, and tables/figures) clearly from the healthy participant group; ROI analyses are also reported but whole-brain results are present. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate to include in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using a social interaction task (modified cyber-ball) with pre- and post-learning face perception runs, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises 15 healthy adults (mean age 24.1), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain searchlight analysis (post- vs pre-learning pattern similarity differences) with results corrected for whole-brain multiple comparisons and MNI coordinates in superior temporal sulcus, constituting a whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group. Whole-brain results are described in the text and coordinates are provided. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This article reports original task-based fMRI data examining social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals), meeting the social-related task requirement. Participants were healthy adults (Experiment 1: n=25, ages 19–27; Experiment 2: n=14, ages 18–23), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical), with statistical thresholds, tables of brain regions/coordinates, and figures — satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This empirical fMRI study used a social task (real-world speed-dating) examining responses to romantic interest and rejection, satisfying the review objective. Sample includes healthy adult participants (scanned group N=38, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., main effects and contrasts thresholded and reported with tables of activation coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction), and results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (communicative vs private intentions) using a task involving action observation. Participants: 23 healthy adults (mean age 24), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt, interaction effects) with stereotaxic coordinates and thresholding across the whole brain, and presents PPI connectivity analyses as well. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (hand-holding by friend/stranger during threat anticipation) in healthy adults (mean age ~23.6). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (threat vs safe) identified via cluster-wise whole-brain analyses (FEAT/FLAME with Z and cluster p thresholds) and lists ROIs and coordinate results (Table 1). The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria: uses fMRI during a social task (I3); includes healthy adult participants (I4); reports whole-brain group-level task activation maps/contrasts (I5); and presents results in text/tables consistent with acceptable reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not a non-empirical paper, and participants are within 18–65).

This is a task-based fMRI study probing social communication (perception and understanding of others) via different laughter types, using healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts and second-level random-effects analyses (e.g., CSL>TIC, CAT>COU) with coordinate tables, cluster/FWE thresholds and whole-brain PPI analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion so the provided full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Task is social-related (imitation/processing of communicative gestures, social communication/understanding); (I4) Healthy adult sample reported (20 adults, mean age 24.6, right-handed, exclusions for motion documented); (I5) Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps reported (SPM analyses, group contrasts, Monte-Carlo cluster correction, tables/coordinates reported); (I6) Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria met. Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI during social-related processing (compassion/altruism toward others) (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–45 and results are reported for these healthy groups (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; whole-brain corrected results identifying IPC and DLPFC clusters) that are clearly derived from the healthy participants (I5). Results are reported in the main text with reference to whole-brain corrected maps and supplemental materials, satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I6). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26) using a social-related gambling task manipulating beneficiary (self, friend, antagonist). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (one-way and 3x2 repeated-measures ANOVAs) with tables/figures and coordinates and applies small-volume correction; the healthy-group whole-brain results are clearly described. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (interns and producers; mean ages ~20.5) that investigates social communication/mentalizing processes during a task of encoding and recommending ideas. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (whole-brain threshold p<.005, cluster k=60) with coordinates and figures described in the text and tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating recognition of 'vitality forms' (socially relevant perception of others’ actions). It used task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 21–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., how vs what), with tables of coordinates and figures (PFWE-corrected results), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study is not ROI-only, not resting-state or connectivity-only, and participants fall within the 18–65 range. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based functional MRI focused on social cognition (theory of mind/emotion understanding), matching I3. The sample comprises 46 healthy adults (female, age 18–31), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (multiple whole-brain contrasts, figures, tables, and permutation-based cluster inference), satisfying I5 and I6. It is an empirical fMRI study with full methods, results, and discussion; it does not rely solely on ROI analyses, connectivity-only methods, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical data. The provided full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

The study meets inclusion criteria: I3—task is an fMRI social-evaluation paradigm (being watched by a peer). I4—sample includes healthy adult participants (ages 18.0–22.9) within the 18–65 range. I5—authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked GLM results (corrected whole-brain maps and cluster statistics) derived from the healthy participant sample (age-related whole-brain analyses are reported). I6—whole-brain results are described in the text and figures (supplemental material referenced). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, and the paper contains empirical task-based fMRI data in healthy adults. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is referenced but not required for inclusion. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants (n=21 healthy adult males, ages 23–33) performed a social-related task (rating naturalness of dyadic nonverbal interactions) during fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects SPM8 flexible factorial ANOVA) with contrasts, cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates presented in tables and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social impression formation (dmPFC) in healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 19.1). It includes group-level voxelwise contrasts (functional localizer: form-impression > sequencing; main task contrasts), reports cluster-corrected whole-brain results and cluster coordinates (Tables 1–2), and describes preprocessing and GLM random-effects analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported via cluster-corrected maps and coordinates), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study employing a social-perception task (passive viewing of biological vs. scrambled point-light displays), reporting group-level adult results. The adult sample (n=48; ages 20–35) are healthy and analyzed separately. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (e.g., Biological > Scrambled) and a Sex×Condition ANOVA with cluster-corrected maps, tables, and figures clearly attributed to the healthy adult group. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (eye-gaze, self-propelling motion, mental-inference/ToM tasks) in healthy adult participants (ages 19–28). The methods report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (one-sample t-tests, contrasts such as E–O and S–X) using SPM, with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results are reported in figures and tables. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of third-party punishment (a social-cognition task assessing perception/understanding of others and moral judgment). Participants were healthy adults (N=26, mean age 26, within 18–65) with demographics and controls reported. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (GLM; reported activations with FDR q<0.05) for task-evoked decision-phase contrasts in the healthy sample. Results are presented in text, figures, tables (Talairach coordinates) and described as multisubject whole-brain maps. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, out-of-range age) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is includable for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social stimuli (traffic-campaign videos) to probe socio-cognitive processes (mentalizing/empathy), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 19–30) with separate groups, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (CV vs NV) and presents whole-brain maps for the healthy/control groups (Fig.1), satisfying I5. Results are reported in standard formats (text, figures, tables), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps, appropriate ages, empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines face perception (a social cognition domain) in a healthy sample including adults and reports whole-brain analyses across the full, mixed-age sample (age regression). However, it does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult subgroup alone (18–65). The meta-analysis requires a whole-brain healthy/adult-group activation map (I5), which is not provided; therefore the study cannot be included. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task: face perception) and I4 (healthy adult participants present). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no adult-group whole-brain task activation map clearly reported). Applicable exclusion: E4 (only between-group/age-regression style contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-adult task map). Full text is complete for assessment.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (attribute framing and self/other evaluations) in healthy adults (ages 19–41). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative frame, frame-consistent vs inconsistent) with coordinates and thresholding details, and describes methods, results and discussion in full. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (paywalled; provided content contains abstract and references but core methods/results/discussion are not accessible). Based on available info: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is met (approachability judgments of faces). However I4 (explicit confirmation of a healthy adult sample aged 18–65) and I5 (clear reporting of group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy/control group) cannot be verified from the truncated text, despite abstract-level claims of activations. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available content. Because essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed without the full text, I exclude the study pending full-text access.

The full text reports original fMRI experiments using a social/empathy visuo-tactile task in healthy adult participants (right-handed female undergraduates). It presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and explicit contrasts (e.g., (other incongruent > congruent) > (self incongruent > congruent)), reports significant clusters with MNI coordinates and SVC-corrected p-values (rSMG peak reported), and includes tables/figures of activation. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked maps from a healthy adult sample during a social-related task, satisfying inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures). Sample consists of healthy young adults (mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7) so includes adults in the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (TFCE with permutation testing) and presents main effects and contrasts in text/figures/tables. All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-task (collaborative vs competitive handgrip task) that probes social motivation/understanding of others. It included 32 healthy adult participants (ages 18–39), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8), with clusterwise FWE correction and SPM maps/tables/figures showing activations (e.g., TPJ, ventral basal ganglia), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study testing tactile priming effects on social judgments (social coordination), matching the review objective of social-related processing. Participants: 20 healthy right-handed native German adults aged 23–39 (meets I4). The task involved judging ambiguous social interactions (social coordination), satisfying I3. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and t-contrasts) with FDR correction and displays statistical maps and tables (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This paper is excluded because it does not report task-based fMRI whole-brain activation maps for healthy adults. Although the study uses a social-related behavioral task (VMST) and a healthy adult sample (N=63, ages within 18–65), the imaging modality is structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) and the reported primary results concern grey-matter volume associations. The manuscript does not present group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI statistical maps from the healthy/control group; it only references or uses previously acquired SSC-BOLD responses from a subgroup (N=29) for secondary correlational analyses, with no new whole-brain healthy-group fMRI maps reported here. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked fMRI map). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered by this report.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses functional MRI during a social-related task (live verbal interaction between interlocutors) (I3); includes a healthy adult sample (22 right-handed women, mean age ~27) reported separately (I4); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses with voxelwise t-tests, cluster thresholds and tables/figures (I5); and whole-brain results are clearly described in text/figures/supplementary materials (I6). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Given the clear task, sample, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting, the study is appropriate for inclusion in the review.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study of explicit social judgments (trustworthiness and attractiveness) on vocal stimuli, with 44 healthy adults (age range 21–60). The methods include whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM8) with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates reported in tables/figures. Thus it satisfies: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/empathy using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (n=27, mean age 34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts and conjunction analyses with MNI coordinates and figures describing task-evoked activations (e.g., contrasts E > N, modality-specific contrasts), clearly from the healthy/control sample. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only reporting, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within age range, and this is empirical original data).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=15 males, ages 21–40). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholds, cluster-size correction, and coordinates/figures for contrasts (e.g., ToM > empathy, empathy > self-reference), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The sample falls within the 18–65 age range and results for the healthy group are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) probing social cognition, mentalizing, and trust—clearly a social-related task. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 24.6, range within 18–65) and results are reported for healthy subgroups (prosocial and proself) drawn from the healthy sample. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (multi-subject GLM, cluster-corrected whole-brain maps; coordinates and figures/tables provided). Whole-brain results are described in the text and shown in figures/tables. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion met: E6 (non-empirical review without original fMRI data). The article is a review (Japanese) summarizing social neuroscience and references fMRI studies but presents no original methods, participant samples, or whole-brain task results. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no original fMRI task data reported), I4 (no healthy adult participant group data reported), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), I6 (not applicable because no original whole-brain results). Full text appears incomplete for screening purposes (only abstract/metadata present).
