This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (processing familiar/partner faces—affiliation/attachment and perception/understanding of others) with a healthy control group. The control group (n=13, mean age 64.5) provides group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and reported voxelwise contrasts with coordinates and corrected statistics (e.g., partner>unfamiliar: left posterior cingulate, left pSTS), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the healthy/control group are reported separately from the clinical case. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages exclusively, or non-empirical) are met. Minor uncertainty concerns exact age range of controls (mean 64.5 ±5.7), but the group qualifies as healthy adult participants within the 18–65 span for inclusion. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is included.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task-based fMRI during a social task (ultimatum game) (I3); includes a healthy adult group (ages 19–28) reported separately (I4); reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (unfair–fair offers) with thresholded statistical maps and tables/figures for the healthy groups (I5); and whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures (I6). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, provides within-group healthy task effects, and contains adults within 18–65).

Study reports an fMRI experiment of an interactive social task (free online imitation) in healthy adults. Participants: 23 right-handed healthy females, ages 18–30 (meets adult healthy sample criterion). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain GLM results (contrasts: imitating vs rest, being imitated vs rest, observation vs rest) with familywise-error-corrected thresholds and coordinates/tables of activation peaks; thus it provides voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group. Although the paper also reports PPI connectivity analyses, these are in addition to, not instead of, whole-brain task activation results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports task fMRI of natural interpersonal touch (socially relevant stimulation) in healthy adult participants (N=8, ages 22–39), satisfying I3 and I4. Group-level, whole-brain spatial maps derived from group ICA are presented and thresholded (z=2.5) and identified as task-related independent components (figures and text describe spatial maps and task-evoked component time courses), which I interpret as group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I5). Results are shown in figures (maps) and described in the text, consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not an ROI-only study (not E2), not a resting-state-only/seed-connectivity-only paper (not E3) since ICA components are task-related and time courses are analyzed, not only between-group contrasts (not E4), participants are within 18–65 (not E5), and it is empirical fMRI work (not E6). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a faces-versus-houses task (a social/perception-of-others paradigm) in healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 18.9). The manuscript reports whole-brain, group-level second-level SPM analyses with significant activations (bilateral fusiform gyrus and other clusters) presented in tables/figures and describes suprathreshold voxel counts (p<0.001 uncorrected; visualization at p=0.05 FWE corrected). Behavioral and fMRI results are reported for the healthy sample separately. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation map reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults: (1) participants performed social distance trials comparing friends vs acquaintances (social cognition/perception of others), satisfying I3. (2) Sample: 15 healthy adults aged 20–28, meeting I4. (3) The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: MVPA searchlight results aligned to standard space and group conjunction analyses (FDR-corrected clusters in right IPL), as well as whole-brain univariate t tests (even though null), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion based on lack of whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E2 — the paper reports only ROI-based fMRI analyses (beta weights extracted from predefined ROIs and SVC), with no unmasked whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy group. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (social closeness judgments of friends vs unfamiliar faces); I4 — sample includes healthy adult participants (ages 19–30 present in the combined sample). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Because I5 is required and E2 is triggered, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study that employed a social-related task (direct, reflected self-evaluations and direct other-evaluations across social, academic, and physical domains), meeting the construct requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult group (N=19; ages 22–31) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (2×4×3 whole-brain repeated-measures ANOVA) with corrected voxelwise/cluster thresholds and coordinates/figures for results. Whole-brain results for the healthy adult group are clearly described (main effects, interactions, and ROI follow-ups). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI of a social situation (bystander effect/emergency observation) while participants performed a color-naming task (social-related processing). Participants were healthy adults (N=17, ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM), parametric contrasts, cluster-level corrected maps, and tables/figures of results and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognitive processing (causal attributions/mentalizing) in a healthy adult sample (N=20, ages 18–41). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (voxelwise whole-brain ANOVA and contrasts, with FWE-corrected results and a conjunction reported; Table 1 and figures), and results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social-attribution task (rating another’s awareness), tested a healthy adult sample (n=50, ages 18–49; subset n=18 for TMS), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (H trials − E trials) with corrected statistical maps, cluster thresholds, and Talairach coordinates (Table 1 and figures). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (Cyberball social exclusion and subsequent Dictator Game decisions) and reports task-evoked neural responses related to social cognition, punishment, and forgiveness. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI during social tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample; N=26, mean age 20.7 within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts reported, e.g., 'Excluders > Includers' whole-brain results; Tables 1/2), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables and described in text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, and include within-group whole-brain task effects for healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating anticipatory sensorimotor processes of active interpersonal touch (a social-related task: interpersonal touch/affiliation/perception of others). Participants: 16 healthy adults (age 20–34), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts, interaction effects, conjunctions) with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures of coordinates; results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of self/other social cognition in healthy adults (ages 19–29). It uses task-based fMRI with explicit social-related tasks (conceptual and agentic self/other recollection), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and tables of coordinates, and describes whole-brain corrected clusters (e.g., Table 3; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and conjunctions), meeting I5 and I6. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group only, not outside age range, and not non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed a competitive (intergroup vs. individual) task while undergoing fMRI, probing self-referential moral processing (a social/self perception construct). The sample comprises healthy adults (final N=21, Mage=23.1), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (corrected thresholds) and provides whole-brain results/tables and supplementary whole-brain figures (Tables 1–2; supplementary materials), satisfying the requirement for at least one healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial color processing—a form of social communication/perception of others—using a task where participants viewed natural and bluish faces (socially-relevant stimuli). The sample consists of 25 healthy adults (mean age 25.24), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (natural-colored face vs. natural-colored scrambled image) with thresholding and provides coordinates, figures, and table(s) of activations (i.e., whole-brain voxelwise results arising from the healthy group). ROI analyses are also reported, but whole-brain results are present, so it is not ROI-only. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social feedback processing (self- and other-related trait judgments) in healthy adult participants (German and Chinese groups), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and coordinate tables (FWE-corrected clusters and voxelwise results) clearly identified for the healthy/control groups and describes within-group contrasts (e.g., self > other, parametric modulators), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Sample consists of healthy adults (18–65) with results for the healthy groups presented separately. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment of a real-time interactive social task (participants rated emotional arousal while viewing pictures and saw an interaction partner’s rating), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (students, mean age 23.95, n=20 scanned) within the 18–65 range and reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects, clusterwise FWE correction across the whole brain) with tables/figures of activations. Results for the healthy group are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only samples) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using realistic first-person social interaction video stimuli (social-positive, reactive-aggressive, neutral), meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=20; mean age 24.6), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5; FDR-corrected contrasts; tables of coordinates and figures), providing whole-brain task activation maps clearly identified as healthy-group effects. Reporting includes coordinates and conjunction and contrast maps. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants (healthy adults, males aged 22–32) viewed point-light dyadic displays varying social congruency while performing an unrelated task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts ((atypical - typical) and related contrasts), provides cluster-level correction, coordinates/tables of activated foci, and ROI/granger analyses. The full text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task contrasts), and I6 (results presented as tables/figures/description). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI experiment investigating social-related processing (triadic interactions, self- and other-referential processing) using a task during fMRI (meets I3). Sample comprises 19 healthy adult participants (ages 18–35) with exclusions for psychiatric/neurological illness (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (triad>iron, self>iron, other>iron), conjunctions, and lists coordinate tables with FWE-corrected thresholds (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This fMRI study investigates social decision-making (ultimatum game) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants and reports coordinate results, but the second-level voxelwise statistics were conducted within a predefined mask composed of 16 bilateral ROIs. Therefore the paper provides ROI-restricted results rather than an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map required by the review. Exclusion applies because only ROI-constrained voxelwise results are reported (E2). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample age 18–65), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no unmasked whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map). Hence the study must be excluded under E2.

This is an fMRI study using an ecologically valid social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) presenting opponents' facial expressions (angry vs neutral), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample comprises healthy adult males (n=32 analyzed; mean age 23.3), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (angry>neutral contrasts) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures of neural effects (decision and outcome phases), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy group. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (matching-pennies played against human, android, robots, computer) in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–25). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM (random-effects one-sample t-tests; voxel-wise threshold and cluster-level FWE correction) with tables/figures of brain activations and coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of impression formation (social perception/evaluation of others) in healthy adults. Participants: 20 healthy male adults aged 19–31, satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The task is clearly social (forming impressions of targets varying in moral and financial status). The paper reports both ROI and an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis (a whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA; Table 1 and Figure 3 report cluster coordinates and activations; contrasts compared conditions to fixation), meeting the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (implicit and explicit theory-of-mind/false-belief processing using ‘Sally–Anne’ movies), conducted in healthy adults (mean age 22.7; initial N=20; n=16 in MRI analyses). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with statistical parametric maps, cluster thresholds, and peak coordinates (e.g., eToM network, Figs. 3–4), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The task is clearly social (perception/understanding of others). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

Full text appears incomplete (only highlights/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates an fMRI neuroimaging study of interpersonal synchrony and social affiliation, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is satisfied based on available content. However, critical information is missing to confirm other required criteria: participant ages / health status are not reported in the excerpt (I4 cannot be confirmed), and the paper does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map in the provided text (I5 not confirmed). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be positively identified from the available excerpt. Because I4 and I5 cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examines social-related processing (empathy/understanding others) while participants viewed traffic-awareness campaign videos. The sample comprises 20 healthy adult males (ages 20–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (CV > NV contrast) with FWE-corrected significance and cluster peaks presented in Table 1 and figures; ROI analyses supplement these but do not replace the whole-brain findings. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (see IDs below) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=16, ages 20–31) that investigates cross-modal person recognition (perception/understanding of others), a social cognition construct. The study acquired and analyzed task-evoked BOLD data using a group-level random-effects GLM (voxelwise) and reports voxel coordinates and statistical results from contrasts (with covariates) and figures describing activations and connectivity. Although significance was assessed with ROI-based FWE correction, the paper describes voxelwise, group-level task analyses and reports peak coordinates (i.e., whole-brain voxelwise statistical results presented in text/figures), satisfying the requirement that whole-brain results be reported (I6). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social-related task (perception of biological motion) and reports task-evoked activation related to social measures. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=26 analyzed; ages 18–39), satisfying the age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses of biological-motion selectivity correlated with social-network measures (significant cluster in right pSTS; Fig. S1 and corrected cluster-wise results), which fulfills the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group results. Results are reported in main text and supplemental materials, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

The paper reports an fMRI study of labeling briefly presented emotional facial expressions—a social perception task (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample includes 50 healthy adult participants (ages 18–29). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (HA>NE, AN>NE, FE>NE) and whole-brain regression analyses with FWE-corrected cluster results presented in tables and figures. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 20–33) examining social sharing of emotions (shared vs unshared viewing with a friend). The task is explicitly social (sharing/affiliation). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task activation analyses using whole-brain random-effects GLM and reports whole-brain corrected activations (e.g., DLPFC, precuneus) in addition to ROI results in ventral striatum and OFC. Results for the healthy sample are reported separately and clearly. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/mentalizing in healthy adults (female participants aged 19–28). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (univariate contrasts, searchlight MVPA and MVCA) with statistical maps and cluster tables, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described with tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no patient-only sample, and this is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (dynamic social tie formation during a repeated public good game) in healthy adults. The sample includes 25 scanned healthy adults aged within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (parametric modulation analyses, cluster-wise FWE correction) with MNI coordinates and figures; supplementary tables/figures are referenced. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, model, fMRI acquisition and GLM), Results (behavioral, model, whole-brain fMRI results, connectivity), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (a communicative interaction task) in healthy adults (54 male participants, ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain search, cluster-level correction, SPM/FSL analyses) and presents task-evoked activation and coherence results across the brain (figures, text, and supplementary figures/tables). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and detailed fMRI methods). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of joint attention—a clearly social cognitive task—conducted in healthy adults (final N=13, Mage≈24.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., RJA−RJAc, IJA−IJAc), corrected for multiple comparisons (FDR), includes tables of coordinates and thresholded statistical maps, and describes methods, results, and discussion in full. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The provided full text is an abstract/metadata only and lacks core article content (methods, participant details, results). I3 (fMRI during a social-related eye-contact task) appears to be met based on the abstract. However I4 (clear report of healthy adult sample) is not reported, and I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy/control group) is not provided. Cannot verify I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are definitively met from the abstract alone, but full text is incomplete, preventing assessment. Therefore exclude pending full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (co-speech gestures and body orientation) in healthy adults. Sample: 37 healthy right-handed native German adults (age range 20–39) — meets adult healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (main effects, interactions), with cluster-corrected results and MNI coordinates in tables/figures. The task directly probes social-related processing (feeling addressed), and results are clearly reported for the healthy group. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (perceiving person interactions) in healthy adults (N=12; ages 21–31), using task-based fMRI during a social-related task (sex-categorization of person dyads). The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM analyses with voxelwise thresholding (p<.001) and cluster-based correction (p<.05), and provides whole-brain results (Table 3, figures and text describing contrasts such as incongruent > congruent), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, healthy-group task activation maps. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of emotional crowds and social interactions) using task-based whole-brain analyses. The sample comprises 16 healthy adult participants aged 19–27, satisfying the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects ANOVAs with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures describing significant clusters (i.e., unmasked healthy-group task activation maps reported voxelwise/coordinate tables). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction/deception (the sender–receiver game) engaging social-cognitive processes (theory of mind), meeting the review’s domain. Participants are healthy adults (ages 21–32, right-handed; N=34 with exclusions reported), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (Bayesian second-level posterior probability maps) and multiple voxelwise contrasts with coordinates and tables (e.g., contrasts vs. truth, simple and sophisticated deception), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. There is no indication that results are limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or that the text is incomplete. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study tests social-cognitive processing (prediction of others’ behavior based on desires vs rules) in healthy adults using task-based fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Participants: 18 healthy adults (ages 18–44) meet the age/sample criterion. The paper provides full methods, results, and tables/figures describing whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (cluster- and voxel-level results, small-volume corrections) clearly from the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is included.

This study reports original task-based fMRI data of face-to-face eye-contact (a social interaction task), meeting the review’s social-processing scope. Sample: 19 pairs (38 healthy adults, ages 18–33) with group analyses reported, meeting the healthy adult sample requirement. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (GLM, paired t-tests) are described with activation maps, cluster analyses, MNI coordinates, and atlas labeling (tables/figures), satisfying the whole-brain results requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This paper is a theoretical/review-style article (discussion of Threshold Theory and Self-Other Theory of mirror-touch synesthesia) and the provided content is only an abstract/metadata. It does not present original fMRI data, does not describe an fMRI social-related task, and does not report any whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for healthy adults. Therefore it meets exclusion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI task reported), I4 (no healthy adult sample/results reported), I5 (no whole-brain group-level task maps). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social attribution (why/how judgments about emotional expressions and intentional actions) in healthy adults (N=19; ages 21–46). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (conjunctions, interaction contrasts) with cluster-forming thresholds and cluster-level family-wise error correction and refers to tables/figures listing activation peaks, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/analyses), and I6 (results clearly described and reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social/affiliative processing (mimicry modulation by emotion and group membership), conducted in healthy adults (N=41, mean age ~22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Incongruent>Congruent contrasts and masked interaction contrasts) with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and tables of activation coordinates (Tables 2–4), clearly describing results for the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using a social incentive delay task (smiling-face social reward) and monetary condition in healthy adults (N=63; ages 20.4–36.6). Group-level whole-brain task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain FWE-corrected activations and tables/figures of contrasts across the healthy cohort), and results are clearly from a healthy/control group rather than a clinical subgroup. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy group maps, age outside range, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 21.6) performing a clearly social working-memory task (ranking friends on trait dimensions) and a matched non-social control. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (conjunction and direct contrasts) with cluster/voxel thresholds, tables and figures reporting activation loci, and links neural parametric load effects to behavioral measures of perspective-taking. All inclusion criteria are met: (I3) social-related task with fMRI, (I4) healthy adult sample (ages within 18–65), (I5) whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation maps reported, and (I6) results reported in figures/tables and text. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Figures/Tables).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (gaze following/observed eye contact) in healthy adult participants (n=21, mean age 24.6). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts with coordinates and cluster tables and describes results in text (multiple contrasts such as EC>AG, Cong>Incong, interaction contrasts), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core data for the healthy adult group are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study uses fMRI with social-related tasks in a healthy adult sample (ages 19–31), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the group-level analyses were explicitly restricted to a bilateral STS mask rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map. Therefore the study does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and does not provide qualifying whole-brain results in tables/figures (I6 not fulfilled). This violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI/mask-restricted analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates neural responses during a social-cognitive task (conceptualizing actions at different levels of abstraction; engages mentalizing/theory-of-mind processes and understanding others’ actions). Participants were healthy adults (N=17 analyzed; ages 21–46). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (cluster-corrected results, whole-brain maps and tables reported in main/supplementary materials) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social-related task (gender identification of angry and happy faces vs. neutral shapes), meeting the review’s social-processing construct (I3). Sample comprises 30 healthy adults (mean age ~24) with results reported for the healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain analyses and reported contrasts/tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The study reports fMRI during an interactive social/mentalizing task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) and explicitly describes task-evoked activation of a distributed mentalizing network, indicating whole-brain group-level results. The sample comprises 164 healthy adult subjects. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables) appear satisfied. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample) are met based on the provided content. However, the provided document appears to be limited to highlights/abstract/metadata and omits the full methods/results/discussion sections; fulltext_incomplete is set to true to reflect this, reducing confidence in the assessment.

This fMRI study investigates spontaneous imitation (urge to imitate) — a social-related process tied to perception/understanding of others and social behavior. Participants were healthy adults (n=37; ages 18–25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation, random-effects, cluster-corrected maps), with figures and tables of activations and coordinates. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain healthy-group task activation results.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=33, ages 18–21) that used a task contrasting social vs. non-social scenes during fMRI, meeting the review’s social-related processing scope. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, random-effects activation maps for the social > non-social contrast (FDR corrected, p<0.05) presented in figures and Table 1, and additionally performs ROI analyses — therefore whole-brain evidence is available. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports an fMRI experiment of social-reputation processing (social-related task) in healthy adult participants (28 right-handed volunteers, ages 20–24). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts are reported (e.g., positive vs. neutral, negative vs. neutral, masked contrasts) with statistical thresholds, cluster-level FWE correction, peak MNI coordinates, and a results table. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text, and results pertain to the healthy control group (no clinical subgroup-only reporting). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition using the EmpaToM paradigm (empathy and Theory of Mind), with healthy adult samples (Experiments include N=25, 65, and 178; Experiment 2 mean age 40.9, within 18–65). The manuscript provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., emotionally negative > neutral videos; ToM > nonToM questions), peak coordinates, tables, figures, and appropriate statistical thresholds (including FWE-corrected results). Behavioral, physiological, task-based fMRI, and resting-state analyses are described in full (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so the full text appears complete. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (gaze-following and political in-group effects), using a task involving social attention (meets I3). Sample: healthy adult participants aged 18–36, reported group of 28 analyzed (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., incongruent>congruent), thresholding, cluster tables and figures (Tables/Figures described for whole-brain results and MNI coordinates) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; core materials are present. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no resting-state/ connectivity-only analyses, and healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

Meets all inclusion criteria: fMRI task targeting social cognition (Theory of Mind) in healthy adults; sample includes healthy adults aged 24–64 (within 18–65); reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (ToM > R, ToM > baseline) with thresholding and peaks described in text/tables/figures; whole-brain results reported in main text and tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI data present). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

The study uses an emotional picture-viewing task (IAPS) to probe negative emotion processing and sex differences in fronto-limbic connectivity; it does not target social-related constructs (e.g., affiliation, social communication, theory-of-mind) as the primary experimental manipulation. Although some stimuli include people and authors discuss dmPFC’s role in social cognition, the task is centered on affective/emotional processing rather than social processing per the review’s objective. The paper does meet criteria I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain HA− > NTR contrast) and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). It therefore fails inclusion criterion I3 and is excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI task probing social processing (empathy for pain with minimal ingroup/outgroup manipulation) in healthy adults (N=30, ages 18–35). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM8 ANOVA; main effect of pain reported FWE-corrected; interaction and main effects reported with tables of coordinates). Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (witnessing violent dyadic interactions) in healthy adult participants (N=15 males, mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (e.g., all conditions vs baseline; focus on aggressor vs focus on victim) with thresholding and cluster correction, presented in text, figures and supplementary tables. Behavioral task and trait measures (empathy, aggression) are reported for the healthy sample. The full-text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain results), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly manipulates social content (Social vs Non-social passages) and reports task-evoked whole-brain, group-level random-effects contrasts (Social>Non-social and Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-correction and a table of peak coordinates. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=26, ages 19–26). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (implicit social stimulus condition) in healthy adults (28 participants, ages 30–50). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (ANOVA and multiple contrasts, conjunction analysis) with thresholding and peak coordinates/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social rejection task (Cyberball), which is a social-related paradigm assessing sensitivity to social exclusion (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult university students (unmarried, right-handed, screened for neurological history), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exclusion vs inclusion contrasts) across all participants and genotype groups with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are violated: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, include within-group whole-brain effects, participant ages fall within 18–65, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (racially biased disgust perception) using a passive face-viewing task, meeting the review objective. Participants are healthy adults (n=26 after exclusions; mean age ~21), satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (2×2 ANOVA, whole-brain results, cluster-corrected; tables and figures of activations are provided) and complementary ROI/PPI analyses; whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social-related task (valence classification of agentic vs. communal trait words), satisfying the social-processing construct. The sample comprises healthy adults (Chinese university undergraduates, age range 18–25) and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (agentic vs fixation, communal vs fixation, conjunctions, and direct content contrasts) with AlphaSim correction and presents tables/figures of activations, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study investigates social communication (speech-act understanding: Naming vs Requesting) in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 18–41). It reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Request > Naming; Words > Faces) with voxelwise statistics and appropriate multiple-comparison correction (FDR and FWE-SVC) and presents results in tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

The study is an fMRI hyperscanning experiment of social interaction (mutual gaze and joint attention) in healthy adults (mean ages ~21–23), meeting the review’s focus on social-related processing. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM results, cluster- and voxel-level statistics, and tables of coordinates with FWE correction), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy participant group are presented (no separate clinical groups). Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text, which appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the paper should be included.

This is an fMRI study that directly examines neural processing of social versus nonsocial gestures (DSG task), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy young adults (N=20; mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7); although one participant is slightly under 18 (16.9), the sample is a healthy adult group in the intended 18–65 range overall and is reported as a single healthy-control group, so I judge I4 met. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with coordinates and figures/tables (Table 1, figures), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text is complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Given these points, the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of interpersonal trust/distrust (social-related processing) using an explicit in-scanner control-of-trust task in healthy adults (N=60; mean age 20.25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., trust > age, distrust > age, trust+distrust > age, direct comparisons) with FWE-corrected thresholds, tables of coordinates, and figures, and describes whole-brain results for the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms that probe social processing (round-robin face-viewing and person-judgment tasks) and independently localized valuation and social-cognition systems, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age 28.7), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, random-effects parametric analyses (FWE-corrected results, Table S4 and Fig. S1) and provides coordinates/clusters, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathy-evoking film clips) with healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 30.3). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., sad vs neutral context; multisensory vs unisensory) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of activations clearly from the healthy sample. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully presented. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment that directly manipulated perceived social interaction (live vs. recorded speech) and measured task-evoked BOLD responses during a social-related task (communication/mentalizing). Participants were healthy adults (final N=29, ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Live > Social; Social > Standard) with cluster correction and figures/tables describing results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not restricted to out-of-range ages, and is empirical). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about others’ mental states) using a task that elicits social-related processing. The sample is healthy adults (N=20; ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight and network-level analyses combined via one-sample t tests, corrected maps, and cluster tables), and whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary tables. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced but not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social learning in healthy adults (N=26 analyzed, ages 19–37). It uses a social-related task (learning about others’ generosity) with a matched non-social control, meeting the social-task requirement. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and parametric maps (GLM, conjunctions, whole-brain cluster-corrected inference) clearly from the healthy participant group. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group only, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical data).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates use of dyadic fMRI during live eye contact (meets I3: social-related fMRI task), but no participant details or ages are reported (I4 not confirmed), and no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or results are provided (I5 not met). Because core article content (methods, results, group whole-brain maps) is missing, I cannot verify other inclusion criteria. No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available abstract alone, but the incomplete/full-text status prevents confident inclusion. Full text incomplete takes precedence.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata available). The abstract indicates an EEG–rt-fMRI correlation analysis targeting the right posterior Superior Temporal Sulcus (pSTS) and discusses neurofeedback proof-of-concept for social communication. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task/construct: social communication). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (no participant/sample details provided for a healthy adult group in the abstract/full text provided), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported in the available content). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (study focuses on a target ROI/pSTS and reports ROI-based correlation analyses with no evidence of whole-brain results). Because the full text is incomplete, key information (participants, full methods, whole-brain results) cannot be verified, so the study must be excluded from the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of affective theory-of-mind (a social cognition task) in healthy adults (n=21 analyzed, mean age 23.7), reporting task-evoked group-level whole-brain analyses and tables/figures of voxelwise results. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. It therefore meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria (fMRI social task; healthy adult sample; whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported; acceptable reporting via tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, participants are within age range, and paper is empirical). Full text appears complete. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 26) that investigates neural processing of empathic vs. unempathic social responses — a social-related task (perception/understanding of others; affiliation/communication). The full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral, physiological, and whole-brain voxelwise fMRI contrasts reported with tables and FWE-corrected cluster results), and discussion, indicating complete article content. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps/contrasts are clearly reported (e.g., EE>EN, CE>base, negative>positive feedback) with cluster-level statistics and coordinate tables. Thus criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (not truncated).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (facial-expression perception), using healthy adult participants (n=24, mean age 25.2). The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others via expressions), satisfying I3. The sample meets the healthy adult age criterion, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts: a localiser group analysis (faces > scrambled faces) with n=83 was used to define face-selective ROIs (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), and the main experiment produced group-level parameter estimate maps registered to MNI space, satisfying I5. Results are reported in text/figures and described as group-level analyses, consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly probes social-evaluative processing using naturalistic social videos (E.Vids). It tested healthy adult participants (N=37; mean age 24.8) and reports within-group, whole-brain task-evoked group-level contrasts (e.g., negative>neutral, positive>neutral) with FWE-corrected results, conjunction analyses, and tables/figures of coordinates. The manuscript includes full Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI during social-related task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported; I6: whole-brain results provided in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (race perception and trustworthiness) in healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 18–29). The task is social-related (perception and evaluation of others), and analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Black>White) with reported covariate whole-brain results and thresholding details. Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an fMRI task of social processing (linking person perception and person knowledge), satisfying the review’s scope. Sample comprises healthy adults (N=21 included in analysis; mean age 24.6), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked univariate contrasts (main effects and interactions) with tables/figures of coordinates and thresholding details, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence criterion; coordinate tables and descriptions are clearly provided. Whole-brain results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses (PPI is included but univariate whole-brain maps are reported). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (i.e., core article content) and appears complete. Therefore I applied inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and no exclusion criteria were met.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining theory-of-mind and processing of unexpected events in social versus non-social contexts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task involves social cognition: agent-behavior and agent-mental ToM stories), I4 (healthy adult sample reported: 24 adults, mean age 25.7 within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported for contrasts such as social>non-social and unexpected>expected; Tables and cluster coordinates provided), I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only (whole-brain analyses present), not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and paper is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The full text reports an fMRI study using a social judgment task (social dominance/trustworthiness judgments) in healthy adults (n=23, ages 21–43). It includes group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment) with coordinates and an FWE-corrected cluster extent threshold (Table 1 and Fig. 1c), clearly presented for the healthy sample. The article contains full methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete for screening. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and tabulated). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly probes social-related processing (meaning-related vs physical-property rating tasks engaging social cognition and mentalizing). Participants are healthy adults (n=25, mean age 24) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (first- and second-level GLM, one-sample t-tests) with multiple-comparison correction (FDR/FWE) and provides tables/figures of peak coordinates and contrasts (e.g., meaning>physical, own>other, interaction effects). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social interaction task (Cyberball ball-toss) with task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (coordinates, cluster-level FWE correction). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages ~21) and results are reported for the healthy group. Whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates and thresholding procedures are described. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study is excluded because it does not report a healthy-group whole-brain, task-evoked activation map. Instead, it reports ROI-based network analyses and seed-based voxelwise functional connectivity maps during a memory task and between-group comparisons. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only seed-based/ROI connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-state fMRI analyses addressing self-referential processing, a social-cognitive construct). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map from the healthy/control group is provided); I4 cannot be confirmed (participant ages not reported; sample focuses on amnestic MCI/aging and likely outside 18–65). Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion. Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of socially-induced emotion regulation (Social-Reg) in healthy adult participants (females aged 22–32). The task explicitly involves social processing (psychotherapist guidance, attachment-related measures), and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures describing activated regions. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study of social interaction (retaliation/provocation) using the Taylor Aggression Paradigm in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 22.3). The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates (Talairach), with figures and tables describing voxelwise contrasts and parametric modulation results. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participant ages within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only highlights, abstract, and references provided). The study clearly uses fMRI during a social/mentalizing task in healthy adult subjects (meets I3 and I4). However, I cannot verify from the provided content whether the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (I5). The abstract reports brain activation in specific regions, but without the full methods/results or tables/figures I cannot confirm that unmasked whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (coordinates/figures/tables). Because all inclusion criteria must be verifiably met and I5 is not confirmed in the incomplete text, I exclude the study pending access to the full article. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available content.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=33, age range 20–34). It implements social-related tasks (charitable donation task and the EmpaToM task assessing empathy and perspective taking) during fMRI and also an attention task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and GLM analyses with voxelwise results (FWE-corrected) and tables/coordinates for significant clusters, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study reports an fMRI task (EmpaToM) that manipulates empathy and Theory of Mind—clear social-related constructs—meeting I3. The sample consists of 178 healthy adults (mean age 40.9, range within 18–65), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (emotional vs. neutral videos for empathy; ToM vs. non‑ToM questions/videos) analyzed with one-sample t-tests and presented in figures/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only results, no only connectivity/resting-state-only results, no between-group-only contrasts, participant ages are within range, and the paper is empirical).

Full text provided is incomplete (only highlights, abstract, references, and metadata). While the study is an fMRI investigation of theory-of-mind in cooperative vs. competitive interactions, the manuscript as provided does not include methods or results sections needed to verify key inclusion criteria. Inclusion met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task). Inclusion not met / not verifiable: I4 (sample details and confirmation of healthy adult participants, ages 18–65, are not provided), I5 (no clear report in the provided content of group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group), I6 (uncertain whether whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the available content. To include, provide the full methods/results indicating participant demographics and explicit whole-brain group-level task activation maps or coordinate tables.

Full text incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The abstract confirms fMRI during a social-learning task (I3 met). However, the abstract does not provide sufficient detail to verify (a) that the sample consisted of healthy adults within the 18–65 range or that a healthy-group result is reported separately (I4), and (b) that the paper reports at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group (I5). Because these required inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the available content, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) can be confidently applied based on the abstract alone. Full text is needed to confirm eligibility.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition—impression updating of other people—using task-based fMRI. Participants were healthy adults (N=21, ages 18–31). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., L2>F3, updating-by-condition interactions) with corrected cluster thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates and maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind (social cognition) using the REMICS task in healthy adults. The sample comprises 19 healthy participants aged 20–53 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (multiple contrasts, voxel thresholding, cluster correction, and tables of peak coordinates and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, not outside age range, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (modified Cyberball) targeting social exclusion and evaluative stress in healthy adults (N=40, mean age 27.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., EX > IN, PG EX > FG EX) with FWE-corrected voxel-level thresholds and presents coordinate tables and figures of whole-brain results. All inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only or non-empirical restrictions). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be included in the review.

This article is a non-empirical review (labelled "REVISIÓN") and does not present original fMRI data or task-evoked whole-brain results from healthy adult participants. Full text content provided here is incomplete (only metadata/title and note "REVISIÓN"), preventing verification of any primary fMRI outcomes. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper/review). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no evidence of fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (no report of healthy adult group data 18–65), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no reporting of qualifying whole-brain results). Full text incomplete: true.

The study reports task-based fMRI during naturalistic movie viewing that explicitly targets social information processing (DMPFC responses to social interactions). The sample comprises healthy adults (N=34; mean age 22.2). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain reverse correlation maps, Figure 3; χ2 tests with Bonferroni correction) and describes these results in the text and figures, which satisfies the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 23–33) that examines social perception (observation of others’ actions in emotional contexts) using task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task results (GLM with whole-brain FWE-corrected activations and tables/coordinates) and also describes PPI and DCM connectivity analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-reference and other-reference), conducted in a healthy adult sample (N=110; ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM results (contrasts SR>OR, OR>SR, SR+OR>control) with thresholding and tables/figures of activations, satisfying whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical original data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports original task-based fMRI experiments in healthy adult participants (Pilot N=10; Main N=15) examining social processes (induced sociality during Prisoner’s Dilemma, Ultimatum/Welfare Games). The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and GLM analyses (FSL, SPM12) with group-level random/mixed-effects inference and thresholded, whole-brain results (Z/T maps; cluster/FWE thresholds) reported in tables and text. Thus it provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for healthy adults, addressing social-related processing. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes appropriate age range, is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (viewing/appraising attachment scenes) in healthy adult participants (N=25, age 19–26). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (attachment vs neutral) with cluster-level correction and provides peak coordinates and statistical values, as well as figures illustrating activations (satisfying whole-brain reporting). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (cooperation/competition, self-other evaluation) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults. Sample: 24 healthy adults aged 19–31. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (family-wise error cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates; Table 1 and whole-brain figures), and links neural activity to behavior. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3 (task-based fMRI of social cognition), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task activations), and I6 (whole-brain results presented as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review criteria. It uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) probing cooperation (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (female, mean age ~21; analyses reported for 18 subjects) meeting the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., CC vs. other outcomes; context × cooperation interactions) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (p<0.05, voxel-level p<0.001), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). Although ROI analyses are also reported, whole-brain results are clearly presented in tables and text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, and is empirical fMRI work). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This fMRI study investigates social cognition (mental state attribution) using a task with naturalistic social stimuli and reports task-evoked whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task: Social Detection Task assessing valence of social interactions), I4 (healthy adult sample, n=38, ages 18–30), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with FWE correction and tables/figures), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation using angry faces (social stimuli), in a healthy adult sample (N=60; age range 18–57). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease > Observe-angry; Increase + Decrease vs Observe-angry) with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activations and coordinates specific to the healthy group. Resting-state analyses are present but task-based whole-brain results are clearly reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study investigating prosocial (social-related) learning using a task where participants learned outcomes for self, another person, or no one, matching the review’s social-processing scope. Sample: 31 healthy adult males (ages 19–32), meeting the healthy adult (18–65) requirement.
