The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (flexible factorial), parametric PE contrasts, and presents voxelwise results/coordinates and figures (main effects reported at P < 0.05 FWE whole-brain or SVC; tables and SI provide peak coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps/results. Results for the healthy group are reported separately and clearly. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only samples) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial behavior) in healthy adult participants (N=32, ages within 18–65). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Mentalizing > baseline; Dissimilar > Similar; Empathy Task ANOVA) with cluster-level correction and coordinate tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (results presented in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related mentalizing task (judgments about friends and kin) in healthy adult participants (25 female adults, mean age 23.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (friend > kin, kin > friend) and linear parametric whole-brain analyses across network layers, with cluster-thresholding and tables/figures of activation clusters. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Face Matching Task with fearful and neutral faces) in healthy adults (N=10, mean age 25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM results (one-sample t-tests; contrasts such as face processing and fear > neutral; thresholding and tables/figures reported, with supplementary coordinate tables). ICA task-related components are also reported but do not replace the presence of whole-brain task activation maps. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social competition task (socially competitive vs noncompetitive learning) and measured brain activity during working memory and feedback, directly addressing social-related processing. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (20 females, ages 18–35) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (contrasts, cluster correction) with coordinates and figures (e.g., Competition > No Competition), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that tests neural responses to social language during a social-communication task (product descriptions and re-transmission), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult undergraduates (n=19, mean age 20.55), satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (parametric modulators, whole-brain maps, thresholding, and tables/figures with coordinates), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (emotion recognition, gaze integration, and theory-of-mind correlations). It reports task-based, group-level whole-brain analyses (PLS) with peak coordinate tables and figures for healthy participant groups. The younger participant group (reported ages 17–27, mean 20.65) provides a healthy adult sample within the 18–65 range (majority in range and reported as a separate healthy group), satisfying the sample criterion. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of empathy for pain (a social-related process: perception/understanding of others) in healthy adult participants (male, ages 18–40). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical analyses (whole-brain FWE-corrected results reported for contrasts such as INJECTION>QTIP and BIOPSY>QTIP and group comparisons), and results are clearly derived from the healthy participant groups (stress and control). Behavioral and imaging results are reported at the group level and whole-brain coordinates/figures are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not resting-state/seed-only; includes healthy adults within age range; is empirical fMRI task data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16–17 analyzed) that investigates social-related processing (attribution of emotions to humans and non-human animals; perception and understanding of others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (Emotion > Expression; Face > Scramble) with cluster-level FWE correction and whole-brain conjunctions and provides tables/figures of results. Participants are healthy adults within the 18–65 range. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described and presented). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study used task-based fMRI to measure neural responses while healthy adult participants (N=40) viewed emotional facial expressions, which is a social-related task (affiliation-relevant emotions). The abstract reports neural responses in several brain regions (thalamus, temporo-parietal regions, cerebellum, amygdala, cortical areas) associated with implicit extraversion during masked and unmasked faces, indicating group-level whole-brain task-evoked effects rather than ROI-only results. However, the provided full text appears to be incomplete (mostly highlights/abstract/metadata) so I could not verify the presence of voxelwise statistical maps, tables of coordinates, or full methods/results; therefore confidence is moderate and fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (final N=25; ages 21–33) that uses a social perception task (attending to emotional valence vs. age of faces), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: random-effects whole-brain faces>objects localizer and whole-brain searchlight MVPA (SnPM-corrected results and uncorrected searchlight clusters reported), with tables/figures describing whole-brain results. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

Study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction recognition (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult group (ages 20–41) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts for the adult group (SI > NM) with voxelwise statistics and correction details (meets I5 and I6). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and group-level whole-brain maps described. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study probing social-related processes (self-related processing and social cognition/mentalizing) during an article-reading/sharing task, linking neural activity to population-level sharing. Participants were healthy adults aged 18–24 and screened for MRI eligibility. Group-level whole-brain analyses are reported (SI Fig. S3, Table S5) and described in the main and supplementary text, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, task-evoked maps from the healthy group. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and SI references).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (person knowledge retrieval, perception/understanding of others) in healthy adults. The manuscript reports data from two studies (total N=50) with healthy adult participants (means: 23.2 and 20.4 years), satisfying the sample age and health requirements. The paper provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (univariate GLM results reported with voxel-level FWE-corrected threshold P<0.05; Figures and Tables of coordinates are provided and described), and also whole-brain searchlight MVPA results, meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Results for the healthy/control groups are presented and not limited to subgroups. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not resting-state/seed-only; not only between-group contrasts; empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory-of-mind) using task-evoked BOLD imaging. Healthy adult participants (Experiment 2: N=17, mean age 22; Experiment 1: N=39, ages 18–60) are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level SPM analyses), thresholding and lists significant whole-brain-corrected activations (Table 1; figures of contrasts mentalising>factual and parametric modulation). Results are reported in tables and figures and the methods/results/discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets I3–I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (action-outcome contingency during joke-telling and listener laughter) in healthy adults (N=38, ages 19–29). The study reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., SELF vs OTHER; listener responses; action-outcome interaction) with stereotactic coordinates, statistical thresholds, and FWE cluster correction. Results for the healthy sample are reported directly and not limited to an ROI-only or connectivity-only analysis (although PPI analyses are also included). The full-text is complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18–24) that uses a social-related task (decisions to share/select news articles; engages social cognition, self-processing, and valuation). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (select > content, share > content, share > select) with corrected thresholds and tables/figures describing these results. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses. The neuroimaging cohort (n=62 after exclusions) are healthy adults aged 18–53. The paper describes whole-brain GLM analyses (random-effects) with voxelwise maps, reports regions and refers to supplementary tables and NeuroVault collection for statistical maps. The task explicitly probes social-related processing (social influence, perception of others) during decision-making. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social decision-making task (Trust Game) probing reciprocity, clearly a social-related construct. The sample includes healthy adult participants (reported ages 18–30; n=19 included in imaging analyses). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise analyses (GLM contrasts, cluster correction via 3dClustSim, tables of activations and figures with MNI coordinates). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in the text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within 18–65). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (mental simulation of personally familiar people) meeting the review objective. Sample: healthy adults (n=25, ages 18–27). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (searchlight RSA, random-effects t tests, permutation correction), with maps and peak coordinates described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social-related processing (schadenfreude and fremdscham) during a task. Inclusion criteria met: (I3) the experiment used functional MRI during an explicit social-cognitive task; (I4) the sample is healthy adult participants (N=34, ages within 19–31/22–29); (I5) the paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (SIT vs NEUT) with FWE-corrected whole-brain results; (I6) whole-brain results are reported as coordinates, figures, and described in text/tables. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include within-group whole-brain task effects for the healthy group. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind/ belief attribution) in healthy adults (final N=22, mean age 24.4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM results from an explicit general-belief localizer contrast (false-belief vs false-photograph) thresholded at q(FDR)<0.05 and provides Talairach coordinates and figures. Although the implicit task analyses were ROI-based, the explicit localizer provides an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map for the healthy sample, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of theory-of-mind (social cognition) in healthy adults using task-based fMRI and multi-voxel pattern analyses. Participants were healthy adult volunteers (ages within 18–65). The paper reports task contrasts (e.g., the ToM localizer Belief > Photo) with voxelwise thresholding (p<0.001, k>20) used to define ROIs, indicating group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (figures/Supplementary Materials referenced). The stimuli and tasks probe perception and understanding of others (belief justification, modality, valence), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Whole-brain results are presented/used (and acceptable reporting via figures/SI). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (heterosexual men age 22–50) that used whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses to examine neural responses to social/affiliation-related stimuli (romantic images). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (e.g., sexual>neutral across all participants; romantic>neutral between and within groups) with cluster-corrected statistics and figures/tables of activations/coordinates. Thus it meets the review objective (social-related processing) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, tables, references). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not only between-group contrasts without a healthy-group task map; participants within 18–65; empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (male, age 20–32) examining implicit attitudes and executive control during tasks relevant to affiliation/attachment and interest in extra-pair relationships. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (IAT incongruent vs. congruent) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and tables/figures, and describes imaging methods and statistical thresholds. The sample meets the adult healthy range, tasks are social/attachment-related, and whole-brain results are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social-related processing (perception of third-party social interactions). It meets inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI with stimuli depicting social interactions and relevant contrasts; (I4) sample consists of healthy adults (N=14, ages 20–32) with results reported for that group; (I5) reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (e.g., interaction > independent contrast with MNI coordinates and group maps) and whole-brain results are described in the text and figures; (I6) whole-brain results are reported in figures, coordinates, and supplementary descriptions. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity-only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within age range (E5), and it is original empirical work (not a review; E6). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and supplemental figure descriptions, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Overall high confidence that this paper should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This empirical fMRI study tests social perception (impression formation of others varying in race and socioeconomic status), using a task-based fMRI paradigm in healthy adult participants (N=60, mean age 23.8). The paper reports both ROI and exploratory whole-brain second-level GLMs (voxel-wise thresholding and cluster extent; whole-brain clusters described and a VMPFC cluster reported), clearly derived from the healthy/control group. All core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task-based social fMRI), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, mean age 22.8) that uses task-based fMRI while participants viewed/judged biological motion (PLD vs HL) — a clearly social-related perceptual task involving perception and understanding of others. Group-level, voxelwise second-level contrasts were performed and reported (BOLD peaks and stereotaxic coordinates in Table 1), and results are described for the healthy/control sample. Reporting of coordinates and voxelwise contrasts (with FWE correction) satisfies the whole-brain reporting requirement (acceptable per I6). Although main statistical testing focused within MNS/MS masks, the paper describes second-level whole-brain contrasts and provides group-level voxelwise results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E3 met: the paper reports only seed-based/resting-state functional connectivity analyses (post-narrative resting-state CN seed maps) and does not present any healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with social-related stimuli: listening to attachment narratives) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map from the healthy group). Full text appears complete.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI during a social/communicative task contrasting collaboratively- vs individually-learned labels and examines social-cognition/theory-of-mind-related activations (I3). The sample is healthy adult participants (directors and matchers; ages 18–33; N=70 after exclusion) (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts with cluster-level correction and presents whole-brain results (tables and figures) as well as an ROI analysis (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), this is not a connectivity- or resting-state-only study, it reports healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts, participants are within the 18–65 range, and it is empirical fMRI work (no E2–E6). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants (N=36 healthy adults, ages within 18–65) passively observed pictures of social interactions varying in cooperativity and affectivity. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (parametric and categorical contrasts) with cluster-FDR corrected results and tables/figures, and also reports DCM effective connectivity analyses. All core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (joint action with haptic contact) in healthy adult dancers; it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (partnered vs non-partnered; improvisation contrasts) with tables of Talairach coordinates and corrected statistical maps. Participants are healthy adults (n=18, mean age 40.4±13.2) within the target adult range. Whole-brain results are reported in figures and coordinate tables. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 25.9) that uses a social-related task (perception of affective vocalisations from humans and other primates), matching constructs of social communication and perception of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (species contrast human>chimpanzee>macaque) with coordinates and tables and mixed-effects (FLAME) group analysis, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy adult group are reported separately. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

The full text reports a group-level task fMRI contrast explicitly assessing social cognition (TOM vs Random) using the HCP dataset. Sample: 787 healthy adult participants (ages 22–>35), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and cluster tables (level-2 cope files, Cohen's d maps, Table 1, Figs. 2–4), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; coordinates and maps are clearly described. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, and tables).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a social-role judgment task (Self, Friend, Celebrity) that directly probes social-related processing (Perception/Understanding of Self and Others), satisfying I3. The sample comprises 37 healthy adult males (mean age 22.9), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with FDR-corrected thresholds and provides peak coordinates and tables/figures for contrasts (e.g., self vs. celebrity, friend vs. celebrity), satisfying I5 and I6. Although the study also includes gPPI connectivity analyses, it clearly reports unmasked whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the article is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This is an fMRI study using a social decision-making task (iterated prisoner's dilemma) targeting Theory-of-Mind and processing of others’ intentions — a social-related construct. Sample: 20 healthy adults aged 23–38 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and contrasts (e.g., COMP>COOP, conjunction analyses) with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and reported coordinates/tables; whole-brain results are clearly from the healthy group. Not ROI-only and not limited to connectivity-only results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study reports task-based fMRI comparing social vs. non-social image appraisal in healthy adults (N=14 analyzed, ages 23–50). It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (social > non-social contrast) with FDR-corrected results and coordinates, and ROI analyses; methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the full text. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI of social processing, healthy adult sample within 18–65, and reported whole-brain group-level task activation maps). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating perception/understanding of others’ emotions (social communication/perception). The methods include whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA; PFWE<0.05; whole-brain contrasts and tables of activations are reported), and reported results pertain to the healthy adult sample (university students aged ~19–24 and 19.67). The study explicitly uses fMRI during a social-related task (emotion perception from faces/voices), reports group-level whole-brain maps and coordinate tables, and provides behavioral and ROI analyses in addition to whole-brain results. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Based on the available content: I3 is met — the study used fMRI during a social-related task (control aversion in social interactions). I4 cannot be confirmed because ages of participants (18–65) are not reported in the provided text, so membership in the required adult age range cannot be verified. I5 cannot be confirmed because the abstract does not explicitly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group; the reported results emphasize functional connectivity, which may reflect connectivity analyses rather than unmasked whole-brain task activations. Because the full text is incomplete, key inclusion criteria cannot be verified; per instructions, fulltext_incomplete takes precedence. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the abstract alone.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided), preventing verification of key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-related task; abstract describes an fMRI task probing social communicative intentions/prosody). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable from provided content: I4 (sample details/ages of healthy adults 18–65 not reported in abstract), I5 (no confirmable report of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map in the healthy group; abstract mentions activations but full methods/results and maps/tables are not available), I6 (reporting format of whole-brain results cannot be confirmed). Exclusion criteria met: none (no evidence of ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical study, or out-of-range sample). Because I4 and I5 cannot be confirmed and full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of social cognition (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluations), involving healthy adult participants (final N=31; ages 19–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with self-esteem (thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction), with results presented in figures and tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, and not limited to between-group contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion requirements for social fMRI in healthy adults.

Exclusion met: E2. Inclusion met: I3 and I4. Inclusion not met: I5. This fMRI study clearly investigates social perception (intelligence/friendliness judgments from faces) using task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (31 participants aged 18–28), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the authors report analyses restricted to a set of a priori ROIs (“search regions were restricted to these ROIs”) and present ROI-based voxelwise results; there is no clear unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or whole-brain voxelwise results reported for the healthy group. Because the paper provides only ROI-restricted task results and no whole-brain task activation maps, it meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This article reports fMRI data including a social cognition (theory-of-mind) task (social interaction vs. random movement). The samples are healthy adult participants (HCP: ~100 unrelated healthy adults, ages 22–36+; UCLA: 114 healthy adults, ages 21–50). The manuscript describes voxel-wise GLM analyses and displays group-level whole-brain task activation results for the social cognition task (figures and ROI-wise activation summaries are reported), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (the paper includes whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled task-based fMRI study in 55 healthy adult males (mean age 24.9) that probes social-related processing (attachment/affiliation via erotic couple scenes and fearful social scenes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., erotic > neutral; fearful > neutral; erotic > fearful) with FWE-corrected results and cluster tables; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain findings are clearly presented. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps/contrasts reported), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mind perception/gaze cueing) in healthy adult participants (N=22; mean age 24.36), using task-based functional MRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level parametric analyses with cluster-based correction and gives peak coordinates and tables for significant activations (e.g., vmPFC clusters with MNI coordinates), consistent with whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps for the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods (imaging acquisition and preprocessing), results, and discussion; supplementary material not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI of a social-related paradigm (emotional face recognition of own vs. unknown child) (I3); includes a healthy adult sample (control mothers without ELM, age range consistent with adult mothers 18–65) and reports results for that healthy/control group separately (I4); reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts (both whole-brain and ROI analyses are reported, and within-group whole-brain effects are described for the control group, e.g., a medial frontal gyrus familiarity effect) (I5); and results are presented in standard text/tables/figures (I6). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the paper should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (recall of self- and other-related relationship episodes) in healthy adults. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (self>control, other>control) with FDR-corrected cluster inference and tables/figures of significant clusters. The sample consists of 35 healthy adult participants with diagnostic screening and results reported for the healthy group. Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables/figures, text). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Therefore none of the inclusion criteria can be confirmed. No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 can be confidently applied from the limited metadata, so none are marked. Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI investigating social-related processing (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions — perception/understanding of others); (I4) Healthy adult sample (n=24, mean age 26); (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain RFX analyses with voxelwise results (FWE-corrected maps, conjunction contrasts) clearly from the healthy/control group; (I6) Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables. Does not violate exclusion criteria: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task activations. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants made face-based trustworthiness judgments and received feedback (social task). The sample includes healthy younger adults within 20–33 years (and older adults), satisfying the healthy adult requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA; whole-brain results and figures/tables, FWE cluster correction) and presents task-evoked activation maps/results for the healthy groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adult participants (age range 18–22). The task explicitly involved judging others' mental states (social-related processing). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain representational similarity (searchlight) and repetition-suppression analyses with corrected voxelwise results and peak MNI coordinates (whole-brain maps and social-brain network analyses described), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, males, age 21–37) using an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma social decision-making task during functional MRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (main effects and treatment×opponent interactions) with cluster-level FWE correction and presents results in tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met (task is social-related, healthy adult sample, whole-brain group-level maps reported, and results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an fMRI study using a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) with BOLD acquisitions and task contrasts (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–22 and analyses are reported for the healthy groups (meets I4). The paper presents group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (cluster-thresholded maps; Z/stat thresholds and FWE correction) and reports whole-brain results (regions, tables, and figures) derived from the healthy sample (meets I5). Reporting of whole-brain results in text, tables and figures satisfies acceptable reporting formats (meets I6). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task activation).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult males (ages 18–35) using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes social processing/response to others. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (high vs low provocation) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides tables/figures of peak coordinates and statistical maps. Healthy-group results are clearly reported (main effects of provocation and decision-phase activations), and whole-brain results are presented in the text/tables/figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical dual-fMRI hyperscanning study using a social interactive task (pattern game) that probes cooperation and competition, meeting the review focus on social processing. Participants are healthy adults (N=44; mean age 22.37, range within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (FEAT/FLAME) with non-parametric permutation correction and lists cluster results (Tables/Figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, age outside range, or between-group-only reporting) are met.

Based on available information: Inclusion met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task—dynamic facial expression perception/imagery). Inclusion not verifiable / not met based on provided content: I4 (no participant demographics or clear report of healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (no clearly reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or explicit whole-brain results are present in the provided text). This is an fMRI study of face perception/recognition, which maps onto the review’s social-related constructs (Perception and Understanding of Others) and therefore meets I3. The samples are healthy adult participants (ages ~23–25 across experiments; N≥20 per experiment), satisfying I4. The methods describe group-level mixed-effects (FLAME) higher-level GLM analyses used to derive group patterns for each viewpoint condition and an independent group localizer (n=83) to identify face-selective ROIs, indicating the presence of task-evoked, group-level voxelwise maps for healthy participants (I5). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply based on the available information.

This is an empirical fMRI study using live bidirectional conversation to probe social interaction (human–human vs human–robot), which is a social-communication task. The sample comprises 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.8) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (main effects and contrasts HHI vs HRI) with cluster-level FDR correction and presents results in text and figures; data are also shared on NeuroVault/OpenNeuro. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study probing social-related processing (empathy for pain/pleasure when observing human vs. robot), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults aged 18–27 with group results reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected maps) and provides whole-brain contrast maps (NeuroVault/OSF), meeting I5 and I6. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical).

This paper reports an fMRI task examining social communication (co-speech gestures) during narrative perception, which directly addresses social-related processing. The sample comprises 20 healthy adult native German speakers (ages 22–35), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts with cluster tables and MNI coordinates (e.g., low_ID>high_ID, speech>gestures+speech, gestures+speech>speech, and interaction effects), clearly reported for the healthy/control group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range participants, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This study uses fMRI with a social task (cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the full text does not present a standalone, unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (e.g., HC group main effect or within-group contrast) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The paper mainly reports between-group contrasts (BPD > HC, NSSI > HC) and conjunctions and refers to a prior paper for some BPD vs HC results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear healthy-group whole-brain map reported) and I6 (no HC whole-brain results provided in tables/figures/text for the healthy group). Full text appears complete. Excluded on grounds of E4; I3 and I4 met, I5 and I6 not met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Task-based fMRI probing animacy perception — a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others/animacy); (I4) Healthy adult participants reported (N=111, ages 19–36; fMRI groups N=20 each, healthy); (I5) Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps are reported (whole-brain random-effects analyses with FWE correction; coordinates and clusters reported in main text/Tables S1–S2; Figures 2–4 show whole-brain results); (I6) Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures and tables. The study is empirical, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper reports fMRI data in healthy adult participants (N=78; ages 18–40) who performed several social-cognition tasks (false belief, animacy/intentional triangles, vocalizations, eyes intention, trustworthiness, face tasks). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (RFX; p<0.05 FWE-corrected) with figures and supplementary peak listings, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus it meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, supplementary material).

This is an empirical fMRI study of dynamic facial-expression perception (a social communication / perception-of-others task), conducted in a healthy adult sample (n=51; mean age 22.5, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs) with family-wise error correction and presents whole-brain activation maps and tables/figures describing results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the study does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy adult group. Instead, analyses are ROI/parcellation-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical metrics derived from the Power-264 atlas. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (reports only ROI/connectivity-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-evoked fMRI of vocal emotional processing, a social-related construct) and I4 (sample of healthy adults aged 20–35). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded under the review’s rules.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition using a take-advice/trust paradigm (social evaluation, trustworthiness), with group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses reported (MVPA searchlight, univariate contrasts with voxel- and cluster-level FWE correction) in healthy adult participants (N=31; mean age 24.3). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based (block and event-related) auditory stimulation contrasting vocal (socially relevant) versus non-vocal sounds. Participants are healthy adults (two samples, ages 18–41 and 18–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and contrasts (vocal > non-vocal and related maps) with thresholds described, and describes whole-brain time-frequency ICA results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (observation of socio-affective touch) that includes a well-matched healthy neurotypical adult control group (N=21). The paper reports group-level task-evoked whole-brain results for the healthy/control group (univariate contrasts; group effects and coordinates are presented in the main text and Additional file 1 / Table S2), and multivariate ROI analyses are supplemental. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is available in the provided full text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating how collective (social) memory structures are represented during memory recall. It meets inclusion criteria: I3 - uses task-based fMRI probing social-related constructs (collective/social memory and social knowledge representation in mPFC); I4 - healthy adult sample (N=24, ages 22–39); I5 - reports group-level whole-brain analyses (surface-based searchlight with TFCE whole-brain correction) in addition to ROI analyses; I6 - whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and figures (Extended Data Fig.1) and reported at group level. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.
